thread.label: Genesis 3:1-6
thread.text: Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?

classes.title: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 3:18
precepts.why:
“Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made.” The serpent is counted among the beasts, and in the scriptures the Most High compares men to beasts. Solomon wrote, “I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.” So the serpent in Genesis 3 is a representation of a man.

He was more subtle than any beast: more crafty, better with his lies, better with his persuasion. Satan’s first weapon was persuasion. Eve was not subdued physically; he did not grab her. He came to her with words. “Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?” Notice what he brings: doubt and fear. Eve answered correctly, that God had said “Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die.” Then came the doubt: “Ye shall not surely die,” and “ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.” She was already meant to be eternal, but he threw doubt in to persuade her to eat.

“she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.” She was persuaded by the serpent, and then she defiled Adam as well. The serpent used no force; he used words to sway Eve’s perception of reality, and then she went into sin. He went to the woman first, which is why the woman is to learn from her husband at home.

That same serpent spirit is still speaking. Christ told the Pharisees, “Ye are of your father the devil,” “a liar, and the father of it.” The serpent seed came through Cain, and it lives on in Esau, the so-called white man, the pioneer of lying, who persuades the world today through his media and his religion. It is a battle for the minds of the people, and the answer is to stay in the word.

thread.label: Genesis 3:1
thread.text: Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?

precepts.label: Job 26:13
precepts.why:
When did the war start? Through the envy of the devil, when he made his move on Adam’s kingdom. And he made that move through Adam’s wife: “Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made.”

The serpent is Satan, the devil. It says serpent, but it is not talking about a snake; he is called a serpent because he is slick, forked-tongued, tricky. And notice, “which the Lord God had made.” God created him to be exactly who he is. He was subtil because God made him subtil.

Job confirms it: “By his spirit he hath garnished the heavens; his hand hath formed the crooked serpent.” God formed that crooked serpent, Satan. He is not a rival power that rose up on his own to equal God; he is a creature God made, crooked by design.

So Satan tricked Eve, the weaker vessel, and caused her to sin, and Eve went and convinced her husband to sin. Then the Most High came to deal with Adam, Eve and Satan, and brought judgment on all three. From there God declared the war: “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”.

That is why we have to know our adversary. The serpent that deceived Eve is the same one we fight today, in his whispers and in his children, and the one who formed him is the one who will judge him.

thread.label: Genesis 3:14-15
thread.text: And the Lord God said unto the serpent, Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field; upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life:

precepts.label: Luke 4:5-6
precepts.why:
Satan made his move on Adam through the weaker vessel, and God brought judgment on the serpent, the woman and the man. To the serpent: “Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field”. That is not about livestock. This is paradise; he is cursed above every creation God made there. And, “upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life”.

That one line says two things. Man was made from the earth, and Satan is a celestial being, so “all the days of thy life” means his days are numbered: he will be destroyed in the future for what he did. And eating dust means he is on the earth, and the Lord handed him power over it.

Luke shows it: “the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it.” When was the power of this earth delivered to Satan? In Genesis 3, what we just read.

And he gave it to whom he would: first to Cain, and then to Esau, the so-called white man in these last days. That is why Esau is able to create all this technology.

Then comes the declaration of war: “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”. Back then her seed was Abel, then Seth and the chosen lineage, and Satan’s seed was Cain and his descendants. Today her seed is the twelve tribes of Israel, and his seed is the so-called Caucasians, Edom. And “it shall bruise thy head”, because his seed, the Romans, crucified Christ. Then, “and thou shalt bruise his heel”: the Lord will take down Satan and his children. So when the Bible says to be soldiers of Jesus Christ, we fight Satan, his wicked thoughts and whispers, and we also fight his children, his physical counterpart.

precepts.label: Job 1:6-7
precepts.why:
“Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came also among them.” Satan does not run around doing his own thing. He goes before the Lord and answers to him.

“And the Lord said unto Satan, Whence comest thou? Then Satan answered the Lord, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.” That walking up and down in the earth is the dust he eats. In Genesis 3 God said, “upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life”. Here is that judgment being lived out: his job is to walk the earth to see whom he can tempt and destroy. Satan became the tempter, and that is his judgment; soon he will be destroyed.

It happened after Satan was judged, and it shows the order of things. The power of this world was delivered to him, but he still presents himself before the Lord and reports where he has been.

The word Satan comes from a Hebrew term meaning adversary: accuser, opponent. And the word devil means deceiver. He is the Lord’s adversary and our adversary. And not only the spiritual Satan: his seed, his children, are our adversary too, because God put enmity between his seed and her seed. The so-called white man is our adversary, and the spiritual demon Satan is our adversary. That is the war we are in.

thread.text: And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the Lord.

precepts.label: 1 John 3:12
precepts.why:
Genesis 4 shows Satan’s children being born in the earth. Eve bare Cain and then Abel; Abel kept sheep and Cain tilled the ground. “And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering: But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth”. The Lord told him, “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.” Do good and you will be accepted; do evil and Satan will rule over you. Cain would become the child of Satan and serve him.

Then Cain talked with Abel, “and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him”. That is the fulfillment of Genesis 3:15, “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”. The enmity started there. Cain, Satan’s seed, killed our forefather: the first murder on the earth and the first blood shed in the war.

John proves Cain was that seed: “Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.” Cain was always evil. His descendants were the children of the devil, and they corrupted everyone on the earth, even the sons of God, until God destroyed the world. All the evil you see Esau doing on the earth today, Cain was doing back then.

Then the sons of God and the sons of the devil came back. Rebekah’s children “struggled together within her”, and the Lord said, “Two nations are in thy womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels”. Jacob is the twelve tribes, the so-called Negroes and Hispanics; Esau is the so-called white man. This fight did not start with slavery, Jim Crow or civil rights; it started in the beginning with Cain and Abel, and was reborn as Jacob and Esau: good against evil. Many of our people followed Cain then, and many follow Esau now and have become children of the devil themselves.

Esau “came out red, all over like an hairy garment”, born without pigment, as Cain lost his when the earth cursed him. Jacob took hold on his heel, a prophetic sign of Genesis 3:15: our Lord coming to destroy Satan and his children. And when scripture says “the devil shall cast some of you into prison”, it was Herod, an Edomite, who “killed James the brother of John with the sword” and took Peter. The devil means the deceiver, and it is interchangeable: the father and his children, who can do nothing without the father that dwells in them.

thread.label: Genesis 4:3
thread.text: And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord.

classes.title: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.label: Romans 9:13
precepts.why:
Cain “brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord”, and Abel brought “of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof.” “And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering: But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect.” What happened to Cain and Abel physically is a foreshadowing of Jacob and Esau spiritually: one is chosen and one is not.

Paul explains it with Rebecca’s twins: “For the children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth”. Then: “As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.” Cain was not rejected because he was wroth; that was ordained from the beginning. It is about election, the purpose God makes. He can make one vessel for one use and another vessel of wrath fitted for destruction.

Christians take “not of works” to mean the law need not be kept. What it tells us is that from the foundation God chose his elect. He still requires the works of the law, not the sacrificial law, but being clean and repented, to obtain the kingdom of heaven. When the first world was formed every nation was supposed to follow the laws, and judgment followed whoever did not. Cain’s rebellious nature showed itself, and it continues to this day in Esau.

People say God doesn’t hate, and they isolate “God is love.” But notice it says “as it is written”: it is in the Bible. It was written first in Malachi: “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob, And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.” Edom says, “We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places”, and he did, in the Renaissance. But the Lord says, “They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” God lets him rise to power so that he can take him down.

And the Lord asked Cain, “Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen?” Remember that, because the same reason Cain hated Abel is the reason Esau hates Jacob today. It is the same spirit; only the name changes. “Satan” simply means adversary, one who obstructs and opposes. That is why everything they do is about us: they were made for that purpose, to obstruct and oppose us, because God purposed it from the beginning.

thread.label: Genesis 4:9
thread.text: And the Lord said unto Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? And he said, I know not: Am I my brother’s keeper?

classes.title: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.label: Job 10:14
precepts.why:
The Lord asked Cain, “Where is Abel thy brother?”, and he answered, “I know not: Am I my brother’s keeper?” But “the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth unto me from the ground. And now art thou cursed from the earth”. That curse is layered, but the ultimate curse is the utter destruction of Cain and his seed, and it has not yet been fulfilled. It is a deferred judgment, held “until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled”: a set time that has to be fulfilled of these heathen nations, starting with Esau as the top one. It is the same spirit of Cain today. Unless we accept who this man is, the son of perdition, nothing else about the last days will make sense.

The Lord told him, “a fugitive and a vagabond shalt thou be in the earth”. Apart from the little land he had in the kingdom of Esau, he takes up the identity of others: he calls himself the Greeks, when the real Greeks were black, of the Japhetic seed; the Romans; the last samurai; the Israelites and the Egyptians in The Ten Commandments. The confusion of faces was supposed to be his curse, and he flipped it onto us, until we became the astonishment, the proverb and the byword.

Cain feared that “every one that findeth me shall slay me”, and “the Lord set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him.” Why not judge him right then? Because God had a purpose for him, as he raised up Pharaoh so that his power would be magnified when he comes to redeem his people and the earth.

Job tells us what the mark is: “If I sin, then thou markest me, and thou wilt not acquit me from mine iniquity.” The mark is sin. And sin preserves him, because sin is witchcraft: by it he seduces the nations that might stand against him into the confederacy of Psalm 83. They all know what he is, but lust, the love of money and power, make them put that aside and ally with him, the way criminals make alliances knowing one day someone will stab them in the back. Under Trump that confederacy is starting to crack.

So Cain is protected only for a time. The judgment was promised through Esau: “I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste”, and they shall call them “The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” That border of wickedness is the mark. “The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof; if not, where, and who is he?” If not Esau, the United States of America, who is he? And “evil shall hunt the violent man to overthrow him”: his demise will come the same way he ruled.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 4:12
precepts.why:
Why would a mark of sin protect Cain? Solomon answers: “For the bewitching of naughtiness doth obscure things that are honest; and the wandering of concupiscence doth undermine the simple mind.” Sin is bewitching. It is seductive. It hides what is honest, so that, as the scripture says, if it were possible even the elect would be deceived.

That is how the mark works. Cain’s line would have rulership for a time, and he would rule the earth with darkness, with sin and with evil, and people would be enticed by it, Israelites included. Our northern kingdom, the majority of it, fell for it, and now they are getting their wake-up call, though there was always a remnant that rebelled against the colonialism they saw in Latin America.

The bewitching is also how the confederacy holds together. The other nations know what he stands for; it is common knowledge. But the love of money, power and rulership says, put that aside, this is the one it was given to, nobody else could get me these things. So they ally with him, and there is no honor among thieves with this man. We watch him boast of taking Venezuela’s president in an operation so fast and violent, threaten the vice president with worse, and name Colombia and Mexico next.

But the spell does not last. “The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” We know who brings him down: first those he dealt with turn against him, and then Christ and his elect have the glory and honor of taking him down. The wicked are revealed and restrained for a time, a hedge around them until they fulfill what the Lord wants, and then comes their final judgment.

thread.label: Genesis 4:22
thread.text: And Zillah, she also bare Tubal–cain, an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron: and the sister of Tubal–cain was Naamah.

classes.title: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.label: Genesis 27:38
precepts.why:
Tubal-cain was “an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron”. He worked metal, and at that time metal meant tools of war; he was not making decorations for your house. The mark followed Cain’s lineage: sin, violence and hatred were in his spirit. Where an artist sees art in raw material, his mind saw weapons. Weaponry came into the earth, or at least advanced, through Cain’s line. Murder led to industry, hatred led to technology, and violence led to institutional power, the hegemony that controls everything.

Then that spirit comes through Esau. “Hast thou but one blessing, my father? bless me, even me also, O my father. And Esau lifted up his voice, and wept.” Isaac answered, “Behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above”: he would have rulership and authority. And the connection to Tubal-cain: “And by thy sword shalt thou live”. The fatness of the earth, everything he has, he gets by violence.

Then: “and shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck”. That happened once our kingdom passed. We had a kingdom for a little while, and since then we have never been in any kind of power up to this day, while he increased through the process of time.

We see it in the graphic of Trump straddling the Western Hemisphere, the Monroe Doctrine renamed the Donroe Doctrine: this is mine. That is the one that sits upon many waters. The wicked are revealed, restrained for a time with a hedge around them to fulfill what the Lord wants, and then comes their final judgment.

precepts.label: Isaiah 54:16
precepts.why:
“Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work”. The Lord is over all of it. He puts it on Satan, his emissary, and Satan passes it around. It is twofold: it speaks of the brass and iron of Tubal-cain, and then it names something more.

Notice “an instrument”: not all weaponry, one in particular. Then he names it: “and I have created the waster to destroy”. What weapon at that time could have been called the waster? Nothing. Zechariah describes it: “Their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet, and their eyes shall consume away in their holes, and their tongue shall consume away in their mouth.” Nobody could have imagined such a weapon then. They had no word for nuclear weapons or atoms, so they saw visions and explained them the best they could: it is the waster.

Malachi says, “behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble”: Esau, the other nations, and rebellious Israel that does not repent. The day that cometh burns them so “it shall leave them neither root nor branch”. A fire leaves ash; this leaves nothing. Peter says “the elements shall melt with fervent heat”. The nations know it: their treaties against nuclear proliferation show the Lord staying their hand, because whoever uses one ends the world as they know it. Isaiah 29 says the strangers “shall be like small dust” and it shall be “at an instant suddenly”, not like regular fire, and all the nations that fight against Ariel, the lion of God, “even all that fight against her and her munition”, her weapons, “shall be as a dream of a night vision”, gone that quick. They filled their bellies and lived deliciously, and in an instant it is all gone. God put it in their spirit to make that thing, and he will use their own weapon, the thing that gave them their power and respect, to end them.

This should move us. The Lord “is longsuffering to us-ward”; the day waits until the set number is sealed, and it comes “as a thief in the night.” “Seeing then that all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy conversation and godliness”? Paul says the same: “let us watch and be sober”: do not drink of her wine, do not sleep thinking you are an American and nothing can touch you. “For God hath not appointed us to wrath, but to obtain salvation by our Lord Jesus Christ”. So “comfort yourselves together, and edify one another”: this is the time to be more united, not divided over simple issues. We look boldly for that day, because “we, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness”: a baptism by fire that cleanses the evil and makes the earth fit for the kingdom.

precepts.label: Genesis 27:40
precepts.why:
Zillah bare “Tubal–cain, an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron”: Tubal-cain designed weaponry. Then Lamech, of the same line, boasts to his wives: “I have slain a man to my wounding, and a young man to my hurt. If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold.” Anyone who tries to avenge himself on Lamech, he will rain hellfire on them. That line through Cain is the lineage that comes back again as Esau, and it was given the art of weaponry.

So Isaac’s word over Esau fits: “Behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above; And by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother”. By his weaponry he lives. He was to serve his brother, but his skill with the sword would be so great that “when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.” He breaks the yoke his brother had over him.

And the principalities, the powers, the thrones he rules through were all created by Christ. Edom’s might comes from the one who made him.

That is the war we are in. Isaiah 14 calls him Lucifer and the king of Babylon: “how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!” He weakens the nations through war, and “smote the people in wrath with a continual stroke”, mostly God’s people. We have watched it: a whole country’s defense taken down and its president taken out in thirty minutes, jets shot out of the sky in ninety-three seconds, sonic weapons that left soldiers bleeding without a bullet fired, as in Panama in the eighties, and DARPA always twenty years ahead. They changed the Department of Defense back to the Department of War, because they know a name matters, as we should know the name of Israel matters.

Our people see that power and think he must be God, or that God must be with him. That is the great war of ignorance. Revelation 13 asks what the world asks: “Who is like unto the beast? who is able to make war with him?” But his pride has deceived him: “I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the most High.” He will fall, and when these devils fall, “The whole earth is at rest, and is quiet: they break forth into singing.”

thread.label: Genesis 4:23
thread.text: And Lamech said unto his wives, Adah and Zillah, Hear my voice; ye wives of Lamech, hearken unto my speech: for I have slain a man to my wounding, and a young man to my hurt.

classes.title: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.label: Genesis 27:41
precepts.why:
Lamech told his wives, “I have slain a man to my wounding, and a young man to my hurt. If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold.” That was cold-blooded murder, killing with no anger behind it, for the thrill of it. Cain killed in anger; if he is judged, how much more Lamech, who just had violence in him. He boasted in it. It went beyond Cain; it increased. That is when murder was normalized and celebrated in that line.

That is why Esau has the same spirit: “And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.” It is in his spirit till this day. Rebekah was told, “Behold, thy brother Esau, as touching thee, doth comfort himself, purposing to kill thee.” Killing is a comfort to him. Trump boasted that the Venezuela raid was very violent, and said of the boats, we are just going to kill them.

“Now therefore, my son, obey my voice; and arise, flee thou to Laban my brother to Haran”. The only thing Jacob could do was flee; he could not stand against that bloodthirsty violence. It is the same spirit as Cain: patient, vengeful and calculated. Cain lured his brother into the field; Esau said, I will wait until the days of mourning are done, and get him when he least suspects it.

That spirit is the son of perdition. “Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition; Who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God”. It says revealed, not elected: he was ordained from the beginning. Ezra was told, “Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau. For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.” People blame Jacob for grabbing the heel, but none of them had done good or evil in the womb; it was a sign, and Jacob was always supposed to be in rulership. Christ said, “those that thou gavest me I have kept, and none of them is lost, but the son of perdition; that the scripture might be fulfilled.” He is not kept; he is ordained for destruction.

The Lord “shall destroy with the brightness of his coming” him “whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders”: the bomb, the weapons, the industrial complex and the economics. So it runs like a ring: Cain murdered his brother Abel, his line built weapons, Esau plotted to murder his brother Jacob, Isaiah 14 reveals the oppressor of the nations, and 2 Thessalonians shows the man of sin fully manifested in these last days. The spirit did not disappear; it evolved from individual murder, to weapon maker, to institutional violence, to global domination, a man who says nothing can stop him but his own morality. But “The whole earth is at rest, and is quiet” once he is laid down.

thread.text: And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them,

classes.title: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.label: 1 John 3:1
precepts.why:
Genesis 5 traces the lineage from Adam down to Noah, who “begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.” Then Genesis 6 says “the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair.” The sons of God are that lineage just named; the daughters of men are the daughters of the other nations that were created. These are not literal angels. The chapter before gives the understanding, and the scriptures that follow prove who the sons of God are.

John writes it in the New Testament: “Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God.” That is what God calls us. Brothers, you are walking gods, whoever gets upset about it, the apologists included.

“therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not.” The world looks at our people, calls us Negroes, and refuses to believe these could be the people of the book, the sons of God. And it knew him not: to this day they refuse to say Christ was a black man. They put the image of Cesare Borgia in every church, comic book and piece of media, while the Bible says he is black, of the tribe of Judah.

So when Genesis 6 speaks of “the sons of God” going in to the daughters of men, it is speaking of the same people John calls the sons of God: Adam’s line, our forefathers.

precepts.label: Psalms 82:6
precepts.why:
“the sons of God saw the daughters of men” in Genesis 6 is about men, not spirits; God says “My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh.” Psalms 82:6 shows who these sons of God are and what God calls them: “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.”

We are gods, and we are children of the Most High. That is why the sons of God in Genesis 6 are called by that name: they carried that DNA, made in the image of God.

It is also why their sin was so serious. Back in Genesis 6:4, “There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men.” The sons of God, the children of the Most High, took wives of the other nations, which was forbidden. The children born to them “became mighty men which were of old, men of renown,” and “God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.” So the Most High brought destruction, and later we had to pay for what we did as the sons of God; he told Abraham his seed would be afflicted in a land not theirs for four hundred years.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 14:1
precepts.why:
The sons of God in Genesis 6 are Adam’s line, the lineage traced in Genesis 5. Did that name change later, after the flood and after Egypt? No. Deuteronomy 14:1, spoken after the Exodus, says to Israel: “Ye are the children of the Lord your God.”

We are the children of the Lord our God because we are the sons of God. The same people carried the same title from Adam through Noah, through the fathers, out of Egypt, and into the law.

This matters for reading Genesis 6 rightly. The sons of God who went in to the daughters of men were not angels coming down from the sky; they were men of that same chosen line, God’s own children, who mixed with the other nations when it was forbidden. That sin brought the flood, and later the affliction of our people. The scriptures do not change the name: from Genesis, to Deuteronomy, to the prophets, to the New Testament, it is our people who are called the children and the sons of God.

precepts.label: Hosea 1:10
precepts.why:
The title “sons of God” runs through the whole book. After Deuteronomy called Israel “the children of the Lord your God,” did anything change in the prophets? No. Hosea 1:10: “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered.”

“And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people.” That place is where our people are today: America and the diaspora, Jamaica, Haiti, Africa, Europe. Everywhere we were told we are not God’s people. “there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.”

God calls us the sons of the living God. That is who we are. So the sons of God of Genesis 6 are the same nation the prophet speaks of: the children of Israel, scattered and counted as nothing, yet still his sons. The world does not know us, but God does, and in the very place where we were called not his people, he will call us his sons again.

precepts.label: Judith 16:7
precepts.why:
Genesis 6:4 says the children of the sons of God and the daughters of men “became mighty men which were of old, men of renown,” and that “There were giants in the earth in those days.” Judith’s song names that kind of people: “For the mighty one did not fall by the young men, neither did the sons of the Titans smite him, nor high giants set upon him: but Judith the daughter of Merari weakened him with the beauty of her countenance.”

The sons of the Titans and the high giants are those giants, the men of renown of Genesis 6, the offspring of the sons of God.

That is where Esau gets his Titan movies, and his Greek mythology of Hercules and the half-gods. He always mixes some lies in with the truth. He tells those stories because he looks at us as gods: because of our DNA, our physical prowess, our melanin. We are the sons of God, demigods on the earth, and that is why when our people are put into sports or anything physical, we dominate. Everybody wants our rhythm, but nobody wants our blues.

So the Titans of the Greek stories are not fallen angels or gods of another people. They are a twisted memory of the mighty men born when the sons of God went in to the daughters of men.

precepts.label: Baruch 3:26-28
precepts.why:
Baruch says the same thing as Genesis 6: “There were the giants famous from the beginning, that were of so great stature, and so expert in war.” Those giants were the offspring of the sons of God, the mighty men of renown, and they were expert in war as well.

“Those did not the Lord choose, neither gave he the way of knowledge unto them.” God did not choose them; they were wicked. “But they were destroyed, because they had no wisdom, and perished through their own foolishness.” How were they destroyed? The flood. God saw that “every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually,” and he wiped it out.

But those same spirits came right back, by way of the three sons of Noah, Shem, Ham and Japheth. There is no new thing under the sun. Jude speaks of “certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation,” the same words, “of old,” that Genesis 6 uses of the men of renown. The same kind of wickedness is still here, reserved “unto the judgment of the great day,” which has not yet come.

So the giants are not a fantasy of fallen angels, the Nephilim Esau talks about. They were men, the offspring of the sons of God, who had no wisdom, and whose spirit lives on until the judgment.

precepts.label: 2 Peter 2:5
precepts.why:
God told Noah, “Come thou and all thy house into the ark; for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation.” Why was Noah chosen to be delivered with his family? Peter explains it: God “spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly”.

The old world is the world we read about in Genesis 7, and God did not spare it: he killed all flesh. Noah was righteous because he preached righteousness and kept the commandments. He was a godly man in an ungodly world, and he had received his orders from God on exactly how to build the ark and did it faithfully. His standing up for God is what brought the flood in upon the ungodly.

Why is he called the eighth person? The other seven were his wife, his three sons, Shem, Ham and Japheth, and their wives. Noah is counted eighth because a true captain, a true leader, made sure his wife, his sons and their wives were on first, and he was the last one to get on the ark. When Noah gave the word, they did not question him; they got on.

That is why men of God have to be strong. We come to the Sabbath because we are sick. We are surrounded by the world all week and fighting the sin around us and in our own thoughts, so we need to be around brothers and sisters who will correct us in righteousness.

The flood shows the mind of God for destruction. Nobody was righteous except the ones on the ark. The coming destruction, a thermonuclear war, will be on another level, and we want to be spiritually the men and women in that ark, not the ones drowning. A lot more than eight will make it this time, but very few, so do not be surprised when your family does not listen. Keep the commandments, preach righteousness, and God will deliver us.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 10:1-4
precepts.why:
Exodus 14 is one of the wars of the Lord: the Lord fought for Israel, overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea, and “there remained not so much as one of them.” Paul looks back on the same crossing: “Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea”.

That cloud is a chariot. And who is Paul speaking to? The Corinthians. If all their fathers passed through the sea, then the Corinthians were Israel. Did the Egyptians pass through the sea? No. And some will say there was a mixed multitude; the mixed multitude came out lusting after evil things and all died in the wilderness. If the wicked of our own people did not make it, what about the mixed multitude?

“And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea”: baptized unto Moses means Moses taught us; he taught us God's laws. “And did all eat the same spiritual meat; And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.”

Who was following us in the wilderness? Christ. Who killed the Egyptians? Christ. The Lord who fought for Israel at the Red Sea, the one Moses wrote of, was always Christ, and he is the one who will come back and smite spiritual Egypt, the land we live in today.

precepts.label: Exodus 13:21-22
precepts.why:
In Exodus 14:19-20 “the pillar of the cloud went from before their face, and stood behind them: And it came between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel; and it was a cloud and darkness to them, but it gave light by night to these”. Who was in that pillar? Exodus 13:21 says it: “And the Lord went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light; to go by day and night”.

Who went before them in the pillar of cloud? Christ. That pillar of cloud is a chariot, and the Lord was inside it. It is the Rock that followed them in 1 Corinthians 10. Imagine seeing something bright, what you would call a UFO today, come down and stand between you and your enemy. The Egyptians saw that, and you know they were afraid.

“He took not away the pillar of the cloud by day, nor the pillar of fire by night, from before the people.” Day and night it was with them. And it was through that same “pillar of fire and of the cloud” that the Lord looked unto the host of the Egyptians in the morning watch, troubled them and took off their chariot wheels, until they said “Let us flee from the face of Israel; for the Lord fighteth for them against the Egyptians.”

precepts.label: Proverbs 3:1-5
precepts.why:
“The Lord is my strength and song, and he is become my salvation: he is my God”. He will guide us. Many of us choose the ways of the world to guide us: the job guides you, the children guide you. But each of us has to walk a path, some of us start to go off it, and we have to seek good and not evil. Proverbs 3 shows what his guiding looks like.

“My son, forget not my law; but let thine heart keep my commandments”. Whose law? God's laws. Your heart is your mind. You have to learn the laws and keep the commandments, and that proves the laws are the commandments. “For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee”. You want to live long? Despite all these wars, rumors of wars and mayhem throughout the world, you want peace? Do what he said.

“Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding”. Trust that the prophecies have to go in order. Iran is not going to bring in World War III; Iran will help unite the Arabs, and you are seeing it. And lean not on your own understanding: in the Christian church some of us used to say we're already saved. No, that's not the understanding. He that endureth to the end, the same shall be saved, and we don't know when that end is coming. So we keep enduring, keeping the commandments, seeking the good and not the evil. “In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths”.

That is how the Lord becomes our salvation in Exodus 15:2: trust in him, endure to the end, and do his commandments. Then the habitation we prepare him is the kingdom, where we have power and rule and every wrong done to us is turned upside down, not the pie-in-the-sky fairy tale of modern Christianity. The Lord is a man of war, and he is using these nations to bring a final battle. I pray I make it, and I pray you make it.

thread.label: Exodus 15:3-6
thread.text: The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.

classes.title: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 18:14-19
precepts.why:
Some people still question it and say the Lord in Exodus 15:3 is the Father. Solomon gave the same account Moses gave. “For while all things were in quiet silence, and that night was in the midst of her swift course, Thine Almighty word leaped down from heaven out of thy royal throne, as a fierce man of war into the midst of a land of destruction”.

Who is the word of God? The anointed, Christ. He has a royal throne in the heavens, and during Exodus he leaped off his throne and came down for war. So when Moses says “The Lord is a man of war”, he is speaking of the word of God that came down at the Passover, killed the Egyptians and drowned them in the Red Sea. Moses said it because he saw the Lord warring for his people.

He “brought thine unfeigned commandment as a sharp sword, and standing up filled all things with death; and it touched the heaven, but it stood upon the earth.” The Lord filled all things with death when he came down in Exodus. A lot of you do not fully understand what Passover is really about: it is about death and destruction of our enemies.

“Then suddenly visions of horrible dreams troubled them sore, and terrors came upon them unlooked for. And one thrown here, and another there, half dead, shewed the cause of his death. For the dreams that troubled them did foreshew this, lest they should perish, and not know why they were afflicted.” The Lord sent the Egyptians horrible visions and dreams; he was afflicting them and warring with them. That is the right hand of Exodus 15:6 that “hath dashed in pieces the enemy.”

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 15:47
precepts.why:
Who is the Almighty word that leaped down off his throne? “The first man is of the earth, earthy: the second man is the Lord from heaven.” The Lord from heaven is Christ. He is the one who came down and killed the Egyptians in Exodus, and that is why Moses says the Lord is a man of war.

Paul says the same thing about the wilderness: our fathers “drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.” And Exodus 13:21: “the Lord went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire”. That pillar of cloud was a chariot, and the Lord inside it was Christ. Who was following us in the wilderness? Christ. Who killed the Egyptians? Christ.

So when Exodus 15:3 says “the Lord is his name”, it is speaking of the anointed. He smote the Egyptians, and the same way he is going to come back in the future and smite spiritual Egypt, the land we are living in today.

thread.label: Exodus 15:3-7
thread.text: The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.

precepts.label: Isaiah 31:1-2
precepts.why:
The Lord is a man of war, and his vengeance is on all the nations read in Psalms 83; he has a big payback coming for all of them. Egypt is one example. Exodus 15 says “Pharaoh’s chariots and his host hath he cast into the sea”, and Isaiah 31 shows what all that power was worth: “Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help; and stay on horses, and trust in chariots, because they are many; and in horsemen, because they are very strong”.

Did the power help them? No. All their chariots and all their war materials did not help them at all. And “they look not unto the Holy One of Israel, neither seek the Lord!” We did not look to the Holy One of Israel, to our God, to save us. The God of Israel is the only God that is going to save us out of all this foolishness. The wars are going to come to the point where thermonuclear ICBMs are put in full effect and a lot of people die, and the question to ask yourself is, will it be us?

“Yet he also is wise, and will bring evil, and will not call back his words”. He is not calling back his word. Evil is set for all these nations, and these nations will be destroyed. Where will you be? You cannot have God to trust in and Christ coming to save you while you sit in confederacy with all these nations, thinking all nations are going to be saved and we are all together. That is not the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

So the right hand that “hath dashed in pieces the enemy” in Exodus 15:6 is the same hand that will overthrow every nation Israel trusts in instead of him.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 51:13-14
precepts.why:
Prophecy is coming to pass and there is no stopping it. The wild and crazy ones made demands to the proud one: not only fall back out of our country, but pay us back for all the destruction. The proud man says no, we are not going to do that. Even while they talk about peace talks, God has them in the trick bag.

“O thou that dwellest upon many waters”: that is New Babylon, America. She is “abundant in treasures”: rich from all the nations, because they have taken all the land and all the resources and oppressed all the people. And “thine end is come, and the measure of thy covetousness.” The Most High is already telling her that her end is come and it is time to step down. She is not going to step down, so God is going to put her down.

“The Lord of hosts hath sworn by himself”: the same Lord of hosts who is a man of war in Exodus 15:3. “Surely I will fill thee with men, as with caterpillers; and they shall lift up a shout against thee.” Those caterpillars are the wild and crazy ones.

If proud Babylon gives in to the demands, she loses her sovereignty over the economy, and that is her downfall. Because she is prideful and already in power, she will not do it, so it leads to war, and God activates the caterpillars. Either way it goes to war. As the Lord cast Pharaoh's chariots into the sea, he will consume this enemy as stubble.

precepts.label: Isaiah 41:14
precepts.why:
The Bible says God is a man of war. War is coming to this place; God is bringing war to the earth. And we should not be afraid of it. Isaiah 41: “For I the Lord thy God will hold thy right hand, saying unto thee, Fear not; I will help thee. Fear not, thou worm Jacob, and ye men of Israel; I will help thee, saith the Lord, and thy redeemer, the Holy One of Israel”. God is talking to us. Don't be afraid; he is going to help us.

Read on: “Behold, I will make thee a new sharp threshing instrument having teeth: thou shalt thresh the mountains, and beat them small, and shalt make the hills as chaff”. A new sharp threshing instrument is a weapon, a weapon of war. The mountains are the nations, and we are going to beat them small. “Thou shalt fan them, and the wind shall carry them away, and the whirlwind shall scatter them”. A time is coming when we will say, there was a place named America; what happened to it? It will be wiped out and never remembered again.

So when war comes, we should be celebrating, happy, not sad, because through those wars our salvation and our freedom come. We should pray for that thing. Our job now is to prepare for it, spiritually and mentally, not physically: prepare ourselves and our people, and keep a food pantry, as Bishop has been teaching for a while.

That preparing is spiritual warfare: “For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh”; the weapons of our warfare are “mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds”. Don't get caught up in the foolishness of this place, the marches and the stupidity, even with your own family. Stay in the scripture, cast down every evil imagination in the minds of our people, and bring every thought “to the obedience of Christ”, the black Messiah. The man of war fights for us.

precepts.label: Exodus 20:5
precepts.why:
Exodus 34:7 says the Lord will “by no means clear the guilty; visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children’s children, unto the third and to the fourth generation.” Exodus 20:5 shows who that is spoken of: “Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me.”

Of them that hate me. To disobey God's commandments is to demonstrate that you hate God. He pardons iniquity and transgression and sin, but if we are guilty of breaking his laws, we are going to pay.

That is why this is read in the wilderness, right after the commandments and statutes were given. A lot of us did not learn from the mistakes we made back then. We came back and did the same damn thing, still wicked and evil and covetous to this day, and the Most High is going to keep sending those afflictions until the lesson is learned. Read the book of your fathers to find out what we did and why all this hell is on us, and you will know what not to do today.

precepts.label: Exodus 20:17
precepts.why:
The iniquity visited upon the children in Exodus 34:7 is the same sin carried from generation to generation, and covetousness is one of them. “Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.”

To covet means to take what does not belong to you: to take it by wickedness, by deceit. The same BS we were doing back then, we still do today, coveting our neighbour's house and our neighbour's wife.

Then, “nor his ox”: hold it right there. That points to Exodus 22, the same chapter Negroes use to beguile you sisters. The whole of that chapter is about thou shalt not covet. Then, “nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s”: you are not supposed to covet, to take, anything that belongs to that father, that neighbour.

So the iniquity of the fathers that is still being visited on us is the same covetousness, and we should learn not to carry that evil all the way up to now.

precepts.label: Exodus 22:1-17
precepts.why:
Exodus 22 is the law put in place for those that wanted to do evil, and it is proper. The whole chapter is about putting restraints on covetousness. It is not telling you how you are supposed to move. It is like a speeding ticket: your insurance goes way up, and that is the consequence of breaking the original law. Drive the damn speed limit.

“If a man shall steal an ox, or a sheep, and kill it, or sell it; he shall restore five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.” That is covetousness: you coveted thy neighbour's ox, exactly what Exodus 20:17 forbids. If you do, you pay for the one you stole and give him five oxen for it.

“And if a man entice a maid that is not betrothed, and lie with her, he shall surely endow her to be his wife.” The maid belongs to her father. To entice her means you coveted to get her; you did it behind the father's back, in deceit. You broke the tenth commandment, “nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.” You lured her away from her father, and you are going to try to tell me that is righteous? You are a damn fool. And a woman that has no wisdom will follow that and pay for the judgment.

Verse 17 kills it: “If her father utterly refuse to give her unto him, he shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins.” The father said hell no. Even though you enticed her, you are not taking her. That is what happened with Dinah: she was enticed, spoken to sweetly and kindly; she was not raped. Even though he wanted to marry her, her brothers said no, snatched her out of that house, and she had to sit there defiled.

That should be a warning to you women. No backdoor marriages will be approved, period. If we have to snatch you out, and you have to sit with that scarlet letter knowing you were defiled, that is better than being tied up with somebody that means you pure evil. How could you even respect a man who went behind your father's back, your protection's back? This is the guilty that Exodus 34:7 says the Lord will by no means clear.

precepts.label: Numbers 30:3-5
precepts.why:
Numbers 30:6-8 is about your prayers, sisters, and the power the Most High gave the husband over the wife. If the husband hears her vow and holds his peace, “then her vows shall stand”; but if he disallows her the day he hears it, “he shall make her vow which she vowed, and that which she uttered with her lips, wherewith she bound her soul, of none effect: and the Lord shall forgive her.” Some of you will go to the Most High praying against your husband, and he can say, Lord, do not listen to that trash.

Keep reading back in the chapter and it speaks of the father, for those of you who do not have a husband. It starts with the man: “If a man vow a vow unto the Lord, or swear an oath to bind his soul with a bond; he shall not break his word”.

Then: “If a woman also vow a vow unto the Lord, and bind herself by a bond, being in her father’s house in her youth”. Being where? In her father’s house. “And her father hear her vow, and her bond wherewith she hath bound her soul, and her father shall hold his peace at her: then all her vows shall stand”.

“But if her father disallow her in the day that he heareth; not any of her vows, or of her bonds wherewith she hath bound her soul, shall stand: and the Lord shall forgive her, because her father disallowed her.”

So God also gave the father power over the daughter. The same power the husband has over the wife’s vow, the father has over his daughter’s vow while she is in his house. That is the order the Most High set, and nobody made it up: do not get mad at us, we are reading the Bible.

precepts.label: Revelation 7:9
precepts.why:
“After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues, stood before the throne, and before the Lamb”. Christians go to Revelation 7:9 to try to confuse you. They say all people coming out of all nations means all peoples, every race, standing before the throne.

But Moses already told us who would be found in all nations: “the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen”. That scattering was slavery, and we were left few in number because they were killing us. So a great multitude coming out of every nation and kindred and tongue is the scattered children of Israel, gathered back out of the lands they were taken to.

The precepts read right behind it settle it: Acts 2:5 shows Jews, devout men, “out of every nation under heaven”; Tobit 13 says “ye children of Israel: for he hath scattered us among them”; Ezekiel 28:25 speaks of the Lord gathering “the house of Israel from the people among whom they are scattered”; and James wrote “to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad”. The multitude before the throne is Israel out of every nation. If they confound you with Revelation 7:9 on the street, shame on you.

precepts.label: Acts 2:5
precepts.why:
“And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.” This answers the question of who the people of all nations, kindreds and tongues are. They were Jews, Israelites, and they came out of every nation under heaven.

That is exactly what Moses prophesied in Deuteronomy 4: the Lord would scatter Israel among the nations. So when scripture shows a people coming out of every nation, it is not speaking of the nations themselves. It is speaking of Israel, found in every nation because the Lord scattered them there.

So Acts 2:5 is the key for Revelation 7:9. Out of every nation does not mean every nation's people; it means the devout Israelites dwelling among every nation, the same scattered people Deuteronomy 4:27 speaks of, who are seeking the Lord from thence.

precepts.label: Tobit 13:3-4
precepts.why:
“Confess him before the Gentiles, ye children of Israel: for he hath scattered us among them.” Tobit is speaking to the children of Israel, and he tells us plainly where they are: scattered among the Gentiles. The Lord did the scattering, just as Moses said in Deuteronomy 4:27.

“There declare his greatness, and extol him before all the living: for he is our Lord, and he is the God our Father for ever.” There, in those lands where we were scattered, declare his greatness. It is the same thing Moses said in Deuteronomy 4: “But if from thence thou shalt seek the Lord thy God, thou shalt find him”. From thence, from the lands we were taken to, we seek him, and we are seeking him now here in America and finding him.

So Tobit proves both halves of the opened scripture: Israel scattered among the Gentiles, and Israel turning to confess the Lord right there among them. He is our Lord, the God of our fathers for ever, and he has not forgotten the covenant of our fathers.

precepts.label: James 1:1
precepts.why:
“James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.” James wrote his letter to the twelve tribes, and he says where they are: scattered abroad. The scattering Moses prophesied in Deuteronomy 4:27 had already come upon them, and the apostles were writing to Israel in the nations.

It stands with Ezekiel 28:25, read in the same moment: “When I shall have gathered the house of Israel from the people among whom they are scattered, and shall be sanctified in them in the sight of the heathen, then shall they dwell in their land that I have given to my servant Jacob.” Israel is scattered among the people, and the Lord gathers Israel out of them back to the land he gave Jacob.

So the great multitude out of all nations in Revelation 7:9 is the twelve tribes scattered abroad, gathered back. This is what you say when they try to tell you on the street that people coming out of all nations means all peoples. If you let them confound you with Revelation 7:9, shame on you.

precepts.label: John 5:37
precepts.why:
“Out of heaven he made thee to hear his voice, that he might instruct thee”. Whose voice did they hear from the heavens? Some people think that is the Father. No, that was Christ's voice. That was the Lord speaking, the one who came down and gave us the commandments.

Christ said it himself: “And the Father himself, which hath sent me, hath borne witness of me. Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his shape.” The Father sent Christ and bore witness of him, but at no time in history have you ever heard the Father's voice, and you never saw his shape.

So the voice our people heard in the wilderness, out of the midst of the fire, was Christ's. And the shape the seventy elders saw when the Lord came down was Christ. It was always the Lord, always Christ there: the rock and the chariot that followed us, the one who came down and smote the Egyptians, the same one who will come back in the future and smite spiritual Egypt that we are living in today.

precepts.label: Hebrews 12:25-29
precepts.why:
Paul speaks of the same thing Moses did in Deuteronomy 4. “See that ye refuse not him that speaketh. For if they escaped not who refused him that spake on earth”: the one that spoke on earth is Moses. The people said, we do not want to hear God, lest we die; Moses, you tell us what he says. Moses gave us the laws, we refused them from Moses, and everybody was killed in the wilderness.

“much more shall not we escape, if we turn away from him that speaketh from heaven”. The one speaking from heaven was the Lord. “Whose voice then shook the earth”. When he spoke the commandments the earth was shaking, and that is why the people were terrified and said, Moses, you speak to us. “but now he hath promised, saying, Yet once more I shake not the earth only, but also heaven.” He is going to shake nations: that is when he returns in the future. The Lord already knew we would go off and that he would have to come again to deliver us. Then those things “which cannot be shaken may remain”, and we receive “a kingdom which cannot be moved”.

“For our God is a consuming fire.” Why does Paul say this? Because that is what the people saw. The Lord said, do not let anybody come near the mountain when I come down, because anyone who comes near will die. When he came down it was a consuming fire; that is all everybody saw, except the seventy elders, who had the Holy Spirit on them and saw his majesty. That is Deuteronomy 4:36: “upon earth he shewed thee his great fire; and thou heardest his words out of the midst of the fire”, the fire that issues forth from his throne.

thread.text: And the king of Jericho sent unto Rahab, saying, Bring forth the men that are come to thee, which are entered into thine house: for they be come to search out all the country.

precepts.label: Joshua 2:15-16
precepts.why:
When the king of Jericho sent for the men, Rahab hid them “with the stalks of flax, which she had laid in order upon the roof”, and sent the pursuers the wrong way. Then she went further: “Then she let them down by a cord through the window: for her house was upon the town wall, and she dwelt upon the wall.” “And she said unto them, Get you to the mountain, lest the pursuers meet you; and hide yourselves there three days, until the pursuers be returned: and afterward may ye go your way.”

She not only helped the prophets, she helped them with an exit. She gave them a way out and a plan: where to go, how long to hide, and when it would be safe to go their way.

These examples are in here for our learning. In these last days some brothers and sisters are going to be looked to to hide the prophets. As we build this spiritual underground railroad, some of y'all will be required to help one another, and sometimes when you help brothers and sisters you are going to put yourself in danger.

Is that you, sister? Is that you, brother? Are you ready to do that for your nation? Or are you going to sell out to keep this body that gets a headache, gets diarrhea, gets belly aches, coughing and all kind of infirmities? The scriptures tell you we have to be ready in these last days.

That is why Hebrews 13 follows it: “Let brotherly love continue.” “Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.” Start small, in your household. Make that guest room ready to receive a guest; if you can't afford an extra room, instead of buying that leather couch, get a pullout couch. If a prophet is on the run and you can provide shelter for two days, a meal and shelter for a prophet, that is a blessing for you. That is the mindset of Rahab, and the mindset we have to have in these last days.

precepts.label: Hebrews 2:9-10
precepts.why:
By Jericho, Joshua saw a man standing over against him “with his sword drawn in his hand”, and Joshua stepped to him: “Art thou for us, or for our adversaries?” You for me or for my enemies? Let me know. And he answered, “Nay; but as captain of the host of the Lord am I now come.” Who is the captain of the host of the Lord? This is talking about Christ, and Hebrews shows it.

“But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour; that he by the grace of God should taste death for every man.” He came down a little lower than the angels when he came the last time. Before that, in Exodus, he did not come a little lower than the angels; he came down like an angel. That is how he stood before Joshua with his sword drawn.

“For it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect”. The captain of our salvation is the captain of the host of the Lord, the Lord of armies, that we read about with Joshua in Joshua 5. That was Christ who was there.

This is the book of the wars of the Lord. The same Christ who led the host when Israel came out of Egypt and conquered the land, and who is the captain of our salvation, is the one who fights for Israel. Joshua fell on his face and worshipped him, because the battle is the Lord's.

precepts.label: 1 Kings 14:29
precepts.why:
In 2 Esdras 14 the Lord had Ezra write the books over: “In forty days they wrote two hundred and four books.” The first were to be published openly, “that the worthy and unworthy may read it”, but the seventy last were kept back. The scriptures themselves show that this is true, because they name books we do not have.

Joshua 10:13 is the first: “Is not this written in the book of Jasher?” There is a book of Jasher, part of the Bible, one of the books Ezra wrote over, and we don't have it today.

Then 1 Kings: “Now the rest of the acts of Rehoboam, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?” So there is a book called the chronicles of the kings of Judah. Guess what? We don't have that book.

Rehoboam's acts were written down in full, and the Bible sends you to that book for the rest of them. The book is named, but it is not in our hands. It is another witness that more was written than what we hold today.

precepts.label: 1 Kings 14:19
precepts.why:
The southern kingdom had its chronicles, and so did the northern: “And the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, how he warred, and how he reigned, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.” So there is a book called the chronicles of the kings of Israel, and we don't have that today either.

The book of Jasher is missing the same way. Is it that book of Jasher they have out there on the Bible apps? No. Those of y'all that have Bible apps, leave that book alone. It is said to contradict a lot of the Bible, and the books of all the prophets complement each other; they do not contradict each other. If you read a book talking about angels having sex with women, or Esau being saved, and all kind of wacky things, that is Esau making stuff up to throw you off.

There is a real book of Jasher, and the Pope and them likely have it in the Vatican, in those catacombs. But they put misinformation out there to try to confuse the prophets.

So the chronicles of the kings of Judah and of the kings of Israel, and the book of Jasher, are named in the scriptures but are not in our hands. What is out there under their names is not to be trusted.

precepts.label: 1 Kings 11:41
precepts.why:
“And the rest of the acts of Solomon, and all that he did, and his wisdom, are they not written in the book of the acts of Solomon?” So there is a book called the acts of Solomon, and we don't have it today. I would love to read that book.

Some of those books are full of what Ezra was told of the seventy: “For in them is the spring of understanding, the fountain of wisdom, and the stream of knowledge.” Things Solomon revealed there, the Lord likely did not want us to know today, so he made it that we don't have possession of those books now.

That is also why the other books out there are left alone: Enoch, Jasher, the letter of Thomas and all that crazy stuff. This is warfare. Evil communication will corrupt you. You go reading that and certain thoughts start coming to your mind, and where did those thoughts come from? From that book you read. If you think you are strong enough to read it, that's on you, but it could confuse you. I'm going to stay with what the Lord gave us.

precepts.label: 2 Chronicles 33:18
precepts.why:
“Now the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and his prayer unto his God, and the words of the seers that spake to him in the name of the Lord God of Israel, behold, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel.” That is another book, the book of the kings of Israel.

We do have the prayer of Manasseh; it is in the Apocrypha. But that prayer is also part of the book of the kings of Israel, and that book we don't have.

So what are we to do with the books we don't have? Christ answers it in Revelation: “But that which ye have already hold fast till I come.” Today we have 80 books. Don't go looking for other books, and don't try to mix in something someone just found, like a book called Lilith, Adam's second wife. Leave all those books alone.

Read on: “And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations”. If you overcome your lust, the temptations and the white man's lies, and hold on to that little faith and that little understanding you got from these 80 books, you will rule the nations. What is in these 80 books, the laws and the prophecies of what is going to take place, we can get the kingdom with that.

precepts.label: 1 Chronicles 29:29
precepts.why:
“Now the acts of David the king, first and last, behold, they are written in the book of Samuel the seer, and in the book of Nathan the prophet, and in the book of Gad the seer”. We have the book of Samuel, but do we have a book of Nathan the prophet? Do we have a book of Gad the seer? We are missing Nathan and Gad.

Nathan the prophet wrote a book where the Lord showed him certain things. A seer is a prophet: somebody that sees things, sees the future. These look like the books the Lord told Ezra to show only to the wise, because in them are things not everybody can understand.

So we see in part. “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face”. The glass we see through darkly is the Bible. God told Moses to hide some things, so we get bits and pieces; one apostle explains it here and another there, and we put together the full picture piece by piece. We don't have all the books, but we have enough to get the understanding to get the kingdom. When Christ comes, he will teach us face to face, and whatever you are confused about now, the Lord will make it clear.

precepts.label: 2 Chronicles 9:29
precepts.why:
“Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, first and last, are they not written in the book of Nathan the prophet, and in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer against Jeroboam the son of Nebat?” Nathan's book is another we are supposed to have. There is also a prophet called Ahijah who wrote books we know nothing about, and Iddo the seer, another prophet, another book.

Those prophets went into some heavy stuff. Ask yourself why, in the time of the Greeks, when Antiochus came against us, Judas Maccabeus, the woman with the seven sons and our forefathers thought the way they did. They were ready to die. Even that group that said, I'd rather die than fight on the Sabbath, just kill me, I'm going to die in my innocency. They had a level of understanding that they got from those seventy books. We are not learning about regeneration and certain things today, but they were far past that back then.

They understood things that we are just starting to figure out piece by piece today. That is why we will never say we understand everything or have one hundred percent truth: “now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.” Our flesh cannot contain some of these things, and when Christ returns we will know.

precepts.label: 2 Chronicles 33:19
precepts.why:
“His prayer also, and how God was intreated of him, and all his sin, and his trespass, and the places wherein he built high places, and set up groves and graven images, before he was humbled: behold, they are written among the sayings of the seers.” So there is a book called the sayings of the seers, the same name as Captain Horab's show, and we don't have it today.

The Lord took those books away. Why? Because some things in them we are not to understand today. He wants us to just trust in him. Some of the things he did back then, he does not want us to have in these last days. And some books were taken away so that the white man could come and lie on the earth and spread all these lies, because some things in those other books were too plain for us to understand. Even though the Vatican took those books and hid them, the Lord allowed that.

One of those missing books is the heart of this class: “Wherefore it is said in the book of the wars of the Lord”. The Lord there is Christ. He is not only going to war in the future; he has been warring since the beginning. We don't have that book, but we can go into the scriptures and see its record in parts, as here in Joshua 10, where the sun stood still until Israel had avenged themselves upon their enemies.

thread.label: 1 Samuel 10:6
thread.text: And the Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man.

classes.title: The Bottle, the Battle, and the Bible

precepts.label: John 3:3
precepts.why:
A lot of us are not finding comfort in the scriptures because we lack faith. You don’t believe the Bible can transform you. You don’t believe it can turn you into another man, that you could become a whole different person. But 1 Samuel 10:6 says it: “And the Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man.”

John 3:3 says the same thing to Nicodemus: “Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.”

Being turned into another man is being born again. The brother who drank a whole fifth in one night, the one who says, I can’t put it down, it’s a part of me, is not stuck being that man. Except he be born again, turned into another man, he cannot see the kingdom. The bottle is the battle, and the Bible is how you are turned into another man and win it.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 14:34
precepts.why:
1 Samuel 10:6 says you “shalt be turned into another man.” 2 Esdras 14:34 tells you what your part is in that turning.

“Therefore if so be that ye will subdue your own understanding, and reform your hearts, ye shall be kept alive and after death ye shall obtain mercy.”

Subdue your own understanding and reform your heart. We have to be transformed in the renewing of our minds. Transformed.

That is what the brother with the addiction runs from. He comes to the table having drunk a whole fifth in one night and says he is not an alcoholic. Even the white man knows the first step of recovery is to admit it: you have to realize you need help, that you are sick. Has he watched the classes on alcohol the Bishops and Deacons go over all the time? No. Why not? Because he is running away from his issues, and you cannot run away from that thing. You have to subdue your own understanding, reform your heart, and let the word turn you into another man, and then you shall be kept alive and after death obtain mercy.
