thread.label: 1 Samuel 15:32-33
thread.text: Then said Samuel, Bring ye hither to me Agag the king of the Amalekites. And Agag came unto him delicately. And Agag said, Surely the bitterness of death is past.

classes.title: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 12:10-11
precepts.why:
Agag was not supposed to be kept alive in the first place. King Saul trusted the enemy; Samuel did not. “Then said Samuel, Bring ye hither to me Agag the king of the Amalekites. And Agag came unto him delicately.” He came crouching and speaking softly: “Surely the bitterness of death is past.” And Samuel still carried out the word of the Lord: “Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before the Lord in Gilgal.”

This is the wisdom Samuel applied, and the wisdom we have to learn to apply: “Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.”

“Though he humble himself, and go crouching”: is that not exactly what Agag did, coming delicately? “Yet take good heed and beware of him, and thou shalt be unto him as if thou hadst wiped a lookingglass, and thou shalt know that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away.”

The things that were written aforetime were written for our learning. Esau does not forget, but we do, because we are not tapped into the scriptures. When we apply what the scriptures show us, we learn that our enemies have been the same from day one, and they are not going to change. That is the perpetual hatred we never learned.

thread.label: 1 Samuel 17:45-47
thread.text: Then said David to the Philistine, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the Lord of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.

classes.title: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.label: Psalms 144:1
precepts.why:
David said to Goliath, “Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the Lord of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel”. When we fight and when we war, we war in the name of our God. Then Psalm 144 shows where David's fighting came from: “Blessed be the Lord my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight”.

This is David, and he says God is his strength, and it is God that teaches his hands to war. David understood that the Lord was with him in every fight and every battle he was in, and the Lord was the one teaching him how to fight. David didn't go to no kung fu school. The Lord was literally teaching David how to fight. David chased a lion and killed it; David was fighting with bears. How was he able to do that? The Lord was with him.

“and my fingers to fight”: and my fingers to punch a dude and break his teeth. Y'all don't be doing that to nobody today, unless you are defending yourself.

So the Lord is our strength, brothers. Always remember that. That is how you learn to war and fight: the Lord is with you, and you can't war without the Lord warring with you. That is why David could tell the Philistine, “This day will the Lord deliver thee into mine hand”, “that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel”, and that “the Lord saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the Lord’s”. Anytime you go to war, it's the Lord that's with you fighting.

precepts.label: 2 Samuel 5:22-24
precepts.why:
“And the Philistines came up yet again, and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.” “And when David enquired of the Lord”: David sought counsel of the Lord. David used to talk to the Lord: Lord, should I go up now? Should I do this? Should I do that?

We have to learn to do that. Before you make a decision, talk to the Lord: I want to do this, but show me what's right, show me should I do this or not; and if it's not right, Lord, shut it down. Sisters, do that when you are marrying some of these brothers: Lord, if this brother ain't right, shut it down. Brothers, do that too: Lord, if this sister is a demon, make me see it. You can talk to the Lord. He does hear you; you are not talking to yourself.

The Lord answered, “Thou shalt not go up; but fetch a compass behind them, and come upon them over against the mulberry trees.” Don't go up right now; go around them and come up behind them, behind the mulberry trees. This goes back to the Lord teaching David how to war.

“And let it be, when thou hearest the sound of a going in the tops of the mulberry trees, that then thou shalt bestir thyself: for then shall the Lord go out before thee, to smite the host of the Philistines.” See in your mind what is taking place: when you hear me running on top of the mulberry trees, the Lord running on top of the trees, then rush yourself. I am going out before you. I'm there fighting with you, David, and we are going to smite the host of the Philistines.

That is the wars of the Lord, and it is what David meant before Goliath: “for the battle is the Lord’s, and he will give you into our hands.” The Lord goes out before his people and fights with them. When you read the Maccabees, angels came down and fought with Judas Maccabeus too, shielding him so nobody could hit him.

precepts.label: Sirach 33:17
precepts.why:
Solomon’s mind was on the people. He did not ask for four hundred women or chariots, or to be a king of 4,000; he asked for “an understanding heart to judge thy people”, “for who is able to judge this thy so great a people?” Because he had a mind for the people, the Lord elevated him and gave him more than he even desired for himself. Likewise with us: when we have a mind for the people, the Lord will bless that thing beyond measure.

Sirach says it plainly: “Consider that I laboured not for myself only, but for all them that seek learning.” In this truth we are not doing this for ourselves. Captains left at four in the morning, driving, so they could be here to help teach the class. A captain drove down and got here at five in the morning to check the congregation, to check on the saints of the Most High. The bishops travel all over the world; the deacons travel. This is not for ourselves; this is for the nation of Israel, because we understand the kingdom that is at hand.

“but for all them”: this is a nation. You must be nation-minded. A lot of times we are not like that: me, me, me, me, me, and that is all you are concerned with. But all through the Bible the greatest leaders were focused on the nation of Israel and how to move the nation further ahead.

That is the mindset of a leader and the action of a king: like Solomon, labour not for yourself only, but for all the people, and the Lord gives more than you asked.

precepts.label: 2 Kings 6:15-17
precepts.why:
“for the battle is not yours, but God’s.” Why does the battle belong to the Lord? Because the Lord is always there fighting with you, even though you cannot see him. Even when you are doing evil, the angels are right there watching and writing down everything you do; the eyes of the Lord are open on all of us. For those who do not believe the Lord is with them and fighting with them, for those with weak faith, look at Elisha.

“And when the servant of the man of God was risen early, and gone forth, behold, an host compassed the city both with horses and chariots. And his servant said unto him, Alas, my master! how shall we do?” A whole army surrounded the city, and they came for this one prophet, this one brother.

“And he answered, Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them.” As men of God you have to realize the Lord is always with you, and those with you are stronger than those with the enemy. “And Elisha prayed, and said, Lord, I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see. And the Lord opened the eyes of the young man; and he saw: and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.” Chariots of fire: angels, just waiting for the word. A man’s army surrounded Elisha, and the Lord’s army surrounded that army, waiting to set it off.

You cannot see things spiritually, but understand: the Lord is with us, his angels are with us, and the Lord is fighting with us. There is no way we could do what the Lord sent us to do on this earth, and no way you would see the growth of IUIC and of Israel, if he were not with us. And it will be the same in the future: they came for one prophet, and federal agents will surround the houses of some of you who teach the word of God. That is the mind you have to have. So be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of the great multitude.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 4:1
precepts.why:
Do not be afraid of armies and people; teach the word of God no matter what they threaten you with. You are not going to be a servant of God and have everything be good. You are not going to be a soldier in Christ and not suffer.

“Forasmuch then as Christ hath suffered for us in the flesh, arm yourselves likewise with the same mind”. The same way Christ suffered for us in the flesh, when the Romans crucified him, lynched him and beat him, you have to arm yourself with that same mind. If your mind is not ready to suffer the same way Christ suffered, you are not a soldier in Christ. The Bible is telling you what is going to happen, but some of you are in la-la land.

Eventually an army is going to surround my house, and they are going to lie on me and call me a terrorist or something stupid like that. I already know that is what they will do, so I prepare my mind. Federal agents are waiting to set you up. Do you think the American government is going to let us keep teaching and waking Israel up and just leave us alone? Read about COINTELPRO. Do you think that stopped? We are going up against a wicked, evil people who will put you away for the rest of your life and lie on you, knowing you did not do it, because of the teachings of Christ.

“for he that hath suffered in the flesh hath ceased from sin”. That is how you become perfect: you have to go through things and suffer in the flesh. Those of you who want a comfortable life, this truth is not for you. The battle is the Lord’s, and he fights with us, but we arm our minds to suffer as Christ did.

thread.label: Ezra 7:10
thread.text: For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments.

classes.title: America At War With Iran: Preparation For Conflict

precepts.label: Psalms 10:17
precepts.why:
“For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments.” What is the heart? The mind. Ezra had prepared his mind to seek the Lord his God. We are in captivity, always working and tired; some days you get stressed. But the Most High has to remind us that we are living in the last days. So brothers, prepare your minds; sisters, prepare your minds.

David shows who the Lord prepares: “Lord, thou hast heard the desire of the humble: thou wilt prepare their heart, thou wilt cause thine ear to hear”. We are the humble. We are supposed to humble ourselves to whatever the Bible says we ought to do.

And when we humble ourselves, the Lord hears our desire and prepares our hearts. We will prepare our minds. That is what Ezra did before he went to teach Israel, and that is what is required of us now, as we watch Iran and Israel go to war and America get involved, and more of our people wake up and repent.

precepts.label: Sirach 2:17
precepts.why:
Why prepare our minds and our spirits? Because war is imminent. We are seeing Iran and Israel at war and America getting involved, and the wars are only going to get worse. What we see right now is a birthing pain. Yet all of us are supposed to rejoice, because the scriptures already told us this was going to happen.

Sirach says: “They that fear the Lord will prepare their hearts, and humble their souls in his sight”. All of us that fear the Lord will prepare our minds, so that whatever evil comes upon the earth, we will remain faithful in serving the Lord.

That is Ezra's example: a heart prepared, and a soul humbled in the Lord's sight, ready to seek the law, do it, and teach it, whatever comes.

precepts.label: Sirach 33:3-4
precepts.why:
Ezra prepared his heart to seek the law and to teach it. Sirach shows why: “A man of understanding trusteth in the law; and the law is faithful unto him, as an oracle.” We must trust in the laws of God, and the law will be faithful unto us.

“Prepare what to say, and so thou shalt be heard”. We have to prepare what to say. Prepare what to say in prayer when we speak to the Most High, and we will be heard. Prepare what to say and teach in the streets, and we will be heard. We must prepare to lead, guide and organize blacks and Hispanics.

“and bind up instruction, and then make answer.” Bind up the instruction first, and then make answer. That is how Ezra could teach in Israel statutes and judgments: he had prepared his heart before he opened his mouth.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 3:17
precepts.why:
This is to the brothers who teach, the up-and-coming soldiers in the MOV program. Ezra prepared his heart to teach in Israel, and the Lord says: “Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me.”

Who is speaking? The Most High said, I have made thee a watchman. It is not the Bishop that made you a watchman. It is not the deacons, and it is not the captains. The Lord called you to be a watchman. That is why you were called into this truth: to warn our people, to warn Israel that they need to repent.

Habakkuk shows the watchman's posture: “I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower”. He is awake and paying attention. As watchmen we must be faithful and pay attention to the signs of the times, hear the word at the Lord's mouth, and give Israel warning from him.

thread.text: Now when these things were done, the princes came to me, saying, The people of Israel, and the priests, and the Levites, have not separated themselves from the people of the lands, doing according to their abominations,

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 8:11
precepts.why:
The people of Israel, the priests and the Levites “have not separated themselves from the people of the lands, doing according to their abominations”. They married the nations' daughters, and the holy seed was mixed. It is like that today: the pollution of the Gentiles is evil-ass Christmas. And it is the brothers with an affinity for the white woman, the Japanese, the Moabitess, the Arab; the brothers secretly dealing with prostitutes and escorts; the brothers wasting the holy seed that could have been a prophet, an avenger, your son, and shooting him in a sock and down the drain. You either kill the old man within you, or you are going to catch an STD and be killed. That is the judgment of the Lord.

Why do men keep rolling the dice? Solomon says it: “Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.” The judgment of the Lord for the evil you do in the dark, outside of this congregation, is not executed immediately on brothers and sisters, so the heart, which is the mind, is fully set to keep doing it over and over again.

But things lie dormant. The Lord may let it manifest, bubble and marinate in you, and then say: this brother or sister gives not a damn about my laws; I showed him mercy and longsuffering; now I have to execute him. A slow death: AIDS, HIV, gonorrhea, syphilis. The Lord says, I'm going to get you one way or the next; I gave you a chance to repent, but you are hardheaded. And a hard head makes a soft ass. Then you are crying out to God, and he is not hearing you.

So the delay of the sentence is not permission; it is time to repent. Kill that old man before you are killed.

thread.text: So built we the wall; and all the wall was joined together unto the half thereof: for the people had a mind to work.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 11:16
precepts.why:
“So built we the wall”: all through our history, the forefathers were building. What we are doing today is nothing different from what they always did, and Ezekiel shows the kind of building the Lord gives us while we are scattered.

“Although I have cast them far off among the heathen, and although I have scattered them among the countries, yet will I be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they shall come.” Israel was cast far off and scattered, and the Lord still gave them little sanctuaries in the lands where they came.

When Paul went to Galatia, to Colossae, to Corinth and to Thessalonica, those were sanctuaries, just like the ones you see today. The schools are those little sanctuaries in the countries, and each and every one of us put a hand into building each and every one of them.

So the wall of Nehemiah and the little sanctuary of Ezekiel are the same work. The people built because they had a mind to work, and that mind to work is what leadership has to put into the people now.

precepts.label: Matthew 6:22
precepts.why:
The people built the wall because they “had a mind to work.” This is how a leader’s mindset must be, and Christ shows it: “The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.”

A single eye is being locked in, what they call laser focus. Whatever you are locked in on, that is what you are going to see. That is all you are going to see, and that is all that matters.

And when the leader is like that, guess who else is going to be like that? Everybody underneath him. The single eye of the one at the head fills the whole body with light, so the whole camp takes on his focus.

That is why the wall got built. The mind to work in the people starts with the mind of the one leading them.

precepts.label: Sirach 10:1-2
precepts.why:
“A wise judge will instruct his people; and the government of a prudent man is well ordered. As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers; and what manner of man the ruler of the city is, such are all they that dwell therein.” However the leader is, that is how the men under him are going to be.

So when you see these other camps that look disorganized, that are talking about rape, that have not built anything in years, find their leaders, and that is what you will see. When you see us traveling all over the world, building institutions, organizations within the organization, look at our leaders. We are the representation of our leadership.

When we go to Chicago we are not on film eating chicken and pizza in the hood at midnight. How is that a leader of a congregation? You will never see a bishop or a deacon put out a video like that. When we went to Chicago, we went to O’Block teaching the word of the Lord.

Everything rises and falls on leadership. There are cities where the leader was changed and the camp took off, and other places where the leader left and everything fell apart. You are who your leader is. That is why everybody wants to ask the Bishop for the secret sauce, but what they do not understand is that Christ is at the head and we are all following Christ. The Most High is building 144,000 leaders, sealed with the law of God, and nothing they try can stop it.

That is why the people of Nehemiah had a mind to work: the wall reflects the ones leading the building.

precepts.label: 1 Samuel 9:1-2
precepts.why:
Esther 2:5 gives Mordecai’s line: “a certain Jew, whose name was Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite.” Mordecai, and Esther with him, were of the tribe of Benjamin. Go back to 1 Samuel 9 and see who Kish is.

“Now there was a man of Benjamin, whose name was Kish, the son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Bechorath, the son of Aphiah, a Benjamite, a mighty man of power.” Kish was a mighty man of power.

“And he had a son, whose name was Saul, a choice young man, and a goodly: and there was not among the children of Israel a goodlier person than he: from his shoulders and upward he was higher than any of the people.”

So Saul and Mordecai come out of the same line, the line of Kish. This was not a regular line; this was a mighty Benjamite line. Keep that in mind for what follows, because the enemy Saul was sent against in his day, the Amalekites and their king Agag, shows up again in Mordecai’s day. The hatred is perpetual, and it runs down the same lines.

thread.label: Job 1:1-12
thread.text: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job; and that man was perfect and upright, and one that feared God, and eschewed evil.

classes.title: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.label: 1 Kings 22:19-23
precepts.why:
In Job, “the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came also among them. And the Lord said unto Satan, Whence comest thou?” But I thought he got kicked out of heaven and was one of the fallen ones? No. He is there because he works for God. God created good angels and bad angels, and Satan’s job is to tempt us; he is only allowed to do what God allows. The prophet Micaiah saw the same court of heaven.

“I saw the Lord sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing by him on his right hand and on his left.” The angels on the right hand go forth for righteousness, and the ones on the left go forth for evil, for judgment.

“And the Lord said, Who shall persuade Ahab, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth–gilead?” One said one thing and another said another. “And there came forth a spirit, and stood before the Lord, and said, I will persuade him.” “I will go forth, and I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And he said, Thou shalt persuade him, and prevail also: go forth, and do so.”

God gave that spirit the authority to do it, the same way he gave Satan the authority in Job 1 to tempt Job: destroy everything, but do not touch Job himself. Even the lying spirit stands before the throne and goes out only when the Lord sends it. That is why the fallen angel doctrine is crap, and why it is a shame to hear black pastors, not only Edomite pastors, repeating that same garbage rhetoric and defiling the minds of the people.

precepts.label: Psalms 103:20-22
precepts.why:
“Bless the Lord, ye his angels, that excel in strength, that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word.” That do his commandments. I thought he kicked them out of heaven because they were disobedient and tried to overthrow him, and now they are fallen? No: they do his commandments. We just read about the spirit sent forth in 1 Kings 22, and about Satan working for the Most High in Job 1. The angels hearken unto the voice of the Most High.

“Bless ye the Lord, all ye his hosts; ye ministers of his, that do his pleasure.” Keep that word ministers in mind. They minister unto the Most High, doing his pleasure, and they also minister unto us.

“Bless the Lord, all his works in all places of his dominion: bless the Lord, O my soul.” Every angel in every place of his dominion is under his rule, carrying out his commandments, which is why Satan could only go as far as the Lord allowed him with Job.

precepts.label: Hebrews 1:14
precepts.why:
The psalm calls the angels “ministers of his, that do his pleasure.” They minister unto the Most High, but they minister unto us as well: “Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?”

Who is going to be heir of salvation? Us, if we keep the commandments. So the angels work on our behalf. They are ministering spirits, sent forth by God for his people.

So the angels that come before the Lord in Job 1 are not rebels running loose. They are sent forth at his word, whether to try a man like Job or to minister for the heirs of salvation.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 39:28-31
precepts.why:
This shows how the angels do what the Most High tells them. “There be spirits that are created for vengeance, which in their fury lay on sore strokes; in the time of destruction they pour out their force, and appease the wrath of him that made them.” Those are the angels on the left hand of God, and they minister unto God and to us.

“Fire, and hail, and famine, and death, all these were created for vengeance; Teeth of wild beasts, and scorpions, serpents, and the sword punishing the wicked to destruction.”

Here is the point: “They shall rejoice in his commandment, and they shall be ready upon earth, when need is; and when their time is come, they shall not transgress his word.” They do what God tells them to do. They do not have free will to say, let’s go down and sleep with some human women today. That is not what goes on in the heavens.

So when Satan went forth to touch all that Job had, he was doing what God allowed and no more. Even the spirits made for vengeance do not transgress his word.

precepts.label: Psalms 34:7
precepts.why:
The angels minister unto the Most High, and they minister unto us. “The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.” These are the good angels. They encamp around them that fear him and deliver them from all evil, like it says in the Lord’s prayer.

Our forefathers never looked at the angels as some demonic thing that came down to earth to persecute and kill them. When three men stood by Abraham in the plains of Mamre, he ran to meet them, bowed himself, had water fetched to wash their feet and prepared a calf for them to eat. When two angels came to Sodom, Lot rose up to meet them, bowed with his face to the ground and made them a feast, and they did eat. They look like us.

The angel in Revelation told John, I am thy fellow servant and of thy brethren; the angels have tribes too. Raphael presented the prayers of the saints. They are our brothers, working on our behalf. Calling them demons and fallen angels is Esau’s popular persuasion. The angel of the Lord camps round about them that fear God, just as the Lord set a hedge about Job, and delivers them.

precepts.label: Job 42:5-6
precepts.why:
Job ends where chapter 32 began. There the three men ceased to answer him “because he was righteous in his own eyes”, and Elihu was angry “because he justified himself rather than God.” Here Job says, “I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee. Wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.”

Job hated himself and repented. He repented for justifying himself and not God, for being righteous in his own eyes. He had said, I am righteous, this is not supposed to happen to me; I made a covenant with mine eyes, I don't look at other women, I am not weak like Adam, I don't hide sin in my bosom. That was his flaw. He was over-righteous, and the Lord did not like it.

In his own eyes Job did not look at it as though there was a reason God was doing this, that God was trying to make him better. In his mind it was, I am righteous, I am not like this person or that person. So the Bible says, “Be not righteous over much; neither make thyself over wise: why shouldest thou destroy thyself?” That person who tries to act over-righteous just ends up looking fake; nobody knows everything and nobody is perfect.

This is the war within, the war nobody sees. Everything Job suffered before was physical, but Satan was attacking his mind too. The Lord used what Job went through to show him what was inside himself, and that is what Satan's attacks do: they show you things inside yourself. Through all of it Job was made perfect, and he came out of it repenting in dust and ashes, justifying God instead of himself.

precepts.label: Isaiah 6:8
precepts.why:
Job 33:23 speaks of “a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand”. You are the interpreter, brother, and you are that one among a thousand. When you are one among a thousand, that makes you a leader, and you have to have the mind of a leader. Any place you step into, your mindset shouldn't be to fit in; you should be figuring out how to make it better. Joseph didn't go into Egypt and just sit there; he asked how we are going to solve the problem. The Lord gave us wisdom, discretion, judgment and skill sets.

The first thing in the mindset of a leader is that he believes he can get the job done. That is what separates you from everybody else. When an issue arises, you don't run. You raise your hand, you volunteer, you figure out a solution to the problem.

Isaiah shows it: “Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” Who is going to go on our behalf? “Then said I, Here am I; send me.” That's the mindset of a leader.

That is the same thing David did. Everybody kept crying about the situation, and David said, where is Goliath at? Show me. The first thing you have to have is a willingness and a belief in completing the task, whatever it may be, and that mindset alone sets you apart. That is what the Lord has put in your spirit to do: not an unsure mind that says maybe I can, but send me.

precepts.label: Psalms 37:32
precepts.why:
Esau “hath said in his heart, I shall not be moved: for I shall never be in adversity.” The white man's mouth is full of cursing, deceit and fraud. “He sitteth in the lurking places of the villages: in the secret places doth he murder the innocent”: that is Mossad and the CIA, the black sites where they would put us and kill us. And “his eyes are privily set against the poor”: the eye on the back of the dollar bill, and the social media and technology set up to monitor us. Every porn video you watch, every site you go on, the white man knows. The ADL monitors bank accounts, and even the police can see all that information. Everything is coming under one system.

David says it plainly: “The wicked watcheth the righteous, and seeketh to slay him.” Brothers and sisters, they are watching you. With the system they have set up they can tell everything you are doing. They are watching those of us who keep the commandments, who call ourselves Israelites. They know there are more than a million people in America who identify as Israelites and agree with these teachings.

And they seek to slay him: they want to destroy us. “He lieth in wait secretly as a lion in his den: he lieth in wait to catch the poor.” He wants to catch you slipping, clicking on the wrong thing. “He croucheth, and humbleth himself, that the poor may fall by his strong ones”: the government, the police, the military.

So walk right and be an example. Build yourselves up. If the wicked is watching the righteous, let him find nothing on you but the commandments of God.

precepts.label: Psalms 56:5-6
precepts.why:
The wicked sits in the secret places and “his eyes are privily set against the poor.” David describes how they watch: “Every day they wrest my words: all their thoughts are against me for evil. They gather themselves together, they hide themselves, they mark my steps, when they wait for my soul.”

They mark your steps: they watch everywhere you go. When you download TikTok now, you have to agree to terms that let them check your immigration status and follow your location wherever you go. The new terms are set up to monitor you and follow you. They want to destroy our soul.

Christ went through the same thing: “And they watched him, and sent forth spies, which should feign themselves just men, that they might take hold of his words, that so they might deliver him unto the power and authority of the governor.” They watch us through these devices; even YouTube lets our channels stay up so they can monitor us. And they send spies who act righteous and act like they want to learn, sent by the federal government to set us up, plant something and lie on us, as they did in France, where conversations among the brothers showed up in the court case against a brother put out of the country.

That is why anything you say has to be scriptural; none of you should be saying dumb, stupid stuff, because they are waiting to wrest your words and deliver them to the government. And the one who takes that work for a little house and a little bank account condemns his soul forever. But the Lord “disappointeth the devices of the crafty”, and “he saveth the poor from the sword, from their mouth”: from the lies of their media.

precepts.label: Malachi 1:4
precepts.why:
“But unto the wicked God saith”. Who is the wicked? Malachi gives the name: “Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places”. Edom is Esau, Mount Seir; it is the same subject.

But “thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” They shall call Edom the border of wickedness. And note it says the people, not the person. The apologists like to play word games and say it is talking about the person Esau. No: people is plural, meaning all of them. And how long is the Lord's indignation against them? For ever.

So the psalm is speaking to Edom: “What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?” Esau said in Ezekiel 35:10, “These two nations and these two countries shall be mine”: the kingdoms of Judah and Israel, and the two countries America and Israel. They took America as Christians and the land of Israel as Jewish people.

One group of Esau took the new covenant as Christians and took the land. The other group, in 1948, took the old covenant and said, we are the Jews. Whether they call themselves Jewish or Christian, they hate instruction and cast God's words behind them. They are the wicked, the border of wickedness.

thread.text: For it was not an enemy that reproached me; then I could have borne it: neither was it he that hated me that did magnify himself against me; then I would have hid myself from him:

precepts.label: Psalms 55:21
precepts.why:
“For it was not an enemy that reproached me; then I could have borne it.” It was not the enemy that set David up, or he would have been ready, because he knows who the enemy is. “But it was thou, a man mine equal, my guide, and mine acquaintance. We took sweet counsel together, and walked unto the house of God in company.” It was the man he trusted, the man he went fishing with, and that took him by surprise. Later in the same psalm David describes that man: “The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart: his words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords.”

A man mine equal: an officer of ten, of twenty, of fifty, just like me. We took sweet counsel together: Deacon, I need counsel; Captain, what do you think about this? But while he was taking counsel, he was plotting. Some are plotting to take your wife: she is too beautiful for him. Some are plotting to take your position at the job you brought them into, telling the white man, give me his position. I picked him up every Sabbath and every Wednesday, and when he came to betray me he had no problem doing it.

“Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.” Christ was betrayed that way: “Judas, betrayest thou the Son of man with a kiss?” Today we do not kiss, but we dap: Shalom, Captain, Most High bless. That smooth greeting can be the betrayal. In 2018 a man who sat in another man's house, barbecued and travelled with him, came and took all his furniture and put his children to sleep on the cold floor.

Jeremiah warns: “Take ye heed every one of his neighbour, and trust ye not in any brother: for every brother will utterly supplant, and every neighbour will walk with slanders.” Supplant means betray, plot. Other camps slander our members and leadership, because they know our people believe anything without proof; they are Esau in black skin, who “have taught their tongue to speak lies.” They come asking to fellowship, but we are not stupid.

It was not the enemy that killed Thomas Sankara; it was his best friend, who grew up with him. It was Maduro's own handpicked bodyguards who stood down and handed him over, taking American money instead of a bullet for him. That is war in the heart behind smooth words. David is telling you: do not fall asleep.

thread.label: Psalms 55:20
thread.text: He hath put forth his hands against such as be at peace with him: he hath broken his covenant.

precepts.label: Psalms 58:3
precepts.why:
“He hath put forth his hands against such as be at peace with him: he hath broken his covenant.” Venezuela is a peaceful country. America put an embargo and sanctions on Venezuela for twenty years to destroy its economy; the money goes down, everything goes down. Then twenty years later: he is a drug dealer, he is this, he is that; people of Venezuela, we can change your lives. America did that. “The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart.”

Only the simple will believe it was about drug trafficking. Trump pardoned one of the biggest drug dealers a couple of months before, and Mexico, on America's border, has more drug cartels than any place in the world. Then the story shifted to oil. They use the same stupidity because they know some black people will believe that garbage. Ninety-nine point nine percent of the words that come out of the Trump mouth are a lie. He lies even when he is not talking; he is blinking and lying, and every person who works for him too.

David shows why: “The wicked are estranged from the womb: they go astray as soon as they be born, speaking lies.” The little baby is born, he does not even talk yet, and he is looking at you lying. That is Trump: before he can say a word he already starts lying. All of them. God said it, not me: it is in them to be liars. And our people believe them, because they are white. Who told you the white man cannot lie?

Habakkuk describes the same man, whose “soul which is lifted up is not upright in him.” Esau is not right: “he is a proud man, neither keepeth at home”: he is in everybody's business, with bases around the world used to overthrow any government that does not do what he says. He destroys the economy with sanctions, sends in CIA agitators and propaganda to raise the people up, and then comes back as the good guy offering to help. Like a man who rapes a woman and then offers to take her to therapy.

That is putting forth his hands against such as be at peace with him. The wicked go astray from the womb speaking lies, and his smooth words always have war in his heart.

thread.text: Cast thy burden upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee: he shall never suffer the righteous to be moved.

classes.title: The Bottle, the Battle, and the Bible

precepts.label: Matthew 11:28
precepts.why:
The bottle says, forget your pain; the Bible says, “Cast thy burden upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee.” The bottle says, numb your sorrow. Christ answers that lie: “Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.”

The bottle offers to carry your burden for you. It talks to you like scripture in a dark room with one light over the table: drink me, I can take away thy sorrows; you're depressed, don't worry about it; you're stressed out, put the kids to bed early and drink me. That is a spirit having a conversation with you.

Christ is the one who actually takes the weight. The labouring and heavy laden are told to come to him, not to the liquor store, and he gives rest. The bottle only numbs the sorrow until tomorrow; casting the burden on the Lord is how he sustains you and keeps the righteous from being moved.

precepts.label: Romans 8:1
precepts.why:
The bottle says, you are a failure. You ain't nothing. You're going to be the same person you always were. The Bible says: “There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.”

Guess what? You can repent. The bottle says you're a failure; the Bible says you can repent and become a new man.

But it starts with acknowledging it: I'm an alcoholic. I'm a fornicator, an adulterer, a liar, a thief; I deal with envy, covetousness, idolatry. That is where the change happens. And acknowledging it is not enough; you have to work on fixing those things. You can't say, I'm an alcoholic, and keep going out drinking.

No condemnation belongs to those who walk after the Spirit and not after the flesh. The man chained to the bottle is walking after the flesh; the man who casts his burden on the Lord and walks in the Spirit is free of the condemnation the bottle keeps whispering over him.

precepts.label: Psalms 19:7
precepts.why:
The bottle says, you can't change. You're the same; you're going to be that same person. The Bible says, “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul.”

The law of the Lord converts the soul: it changes a man. So the lie that you can't change is answered by the perfect law of God. You can repent and become a new man.

That is the other side of casting your burden on the Lord. You don't just hand him the weight; you take on his law, and his law turns you into somebody different. The bottle keeps you drunk and stupid, the way the enemy wants it, with a liquor store in every black neighborhood and weed stores everywhere to keep you high, drunk and stupid. The law of the Lord makes the simple wise and converts the soul out of that.

precepts.label: Ephesians 5:18
precepts.why:
The bottle says, take another drink. You can handle it; drink some more. The Bible says, “And be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess; but be filled with the Spirit.”

The bottle wants to fill you: drink me and be filled with my love. It says, you're alone, nobody understands us, I love you more than anybody. I love you more than water. You don't need to eat today; I'll make the food taste better. You can't sleep; I can put you to sleep so fast you won't even realize it. The bottle starts talking like scripture: I am that I am, the comfort of them all.

That is excess, and it destroys the body too. Alcohol builds fat around your organs and your belly, raises your risk of heart disease, high blood pressure and type two diabetes, makes you hungrier and drives you to fast food. Four or five shots a drink every day is thousands of calories a week, and then you wonder why you can't lose weight or climb a flight of stairs.

The command is to be filled with something else: the Spirit. Cast your burden on the Lord and be filled with his Spirit, not with the bottle.

The most powerful pen in the world, with a stack of bills beside it, is the president of the United States, and every nation bends the knee. When he promised to lock up the criminal illegal immigrants, you thought thieves and murderers; but by their law, anyone here without papers is a criminal. That is framing mischief by a law.

Micah shows how they work: “Woe to them that devise iniquity, and work evil upon their beds! when the morning is light, they practise it, because it is in the power of their hand.” When the morning is light means in broad daylight, because they can frame it by law, and he says his own morality is the only limit. It is in the power of their hand because they are after the working of Satan, given authority to set kings up and take them down.

“And they covet fields, and take them by violence; and houses, and take them away: so they oppress a man and his house, even a man and his heritage.” It is not just the resources; they want the identity too. Venezuela's vice president said the country was attacked by Zionists seeking to enslave the nation. Netanyahu, whom he calls his boss, visited before the attack. Machado, who won the Nobel Peace Prize and then gave it to Trump, promised to open the oil to their companies and move Venezuela's embassy to Jerusalem, because everybody has to bow the knee to the impostors.

Maduro said he is a Jew in his blood, from the twelve tribes, and that the man over there is not a real Jew. That is the heritage they are after. The ADL says it has analysts monitoring 24 hours a day and trains law enforcement, and in Patagonia Israeli tourists were caught setting fires in a protected preserve they cannot buy unless it is damaged. Their eye is on the land and on the lost tribes. They practise it in the light, because it is in the power of their hand.

thread.label: Psalms 144:1
thread.text: Blessed be the Lord my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight:

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 2:3
precepts.why:
“Blessed be the Lord my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight.” We serve a God of war, the God that formed the light and created darkness, and that God of war is Christ. David is speaking of how the Lord equipped him with his mighty fighting skills, and the same man of war teaches his soldiers to do the same. Paul says it: “Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ. No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.”

The God of war handpicked every one of us to be soldiers in his mighty army. We are in a boot camp, a training camp, and he is teaching us how to war. Some brothers think they are here just for the unleavened bread, just to be around the brothers. No. Everything going on in the earth, in your household and in the congregation is a teachable moment, because there are spirits in all of it, and we are being built up to deal with those spirits.

It is a process. You start with yourself, subduing your own body, and that is ongoing until you go in the grave. Then your household, then the congregation, as a leader helping other brothers and sisters do the same. Even when you hear somebody else being corrected, it is about you, because at some point you will stand in that same position.

Judges shows why the nations are here: “Now these are the nations which the Lord left, to prove Israel by them”, “to teach them war.” The nations are the Lord's sword to teach us war. If you think that means go get your Glock, you are being simple. “For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh.” At Ai the Lord said, “I have given into thy hand the king of Ai”, and still told Joshua, “lay thee an ambush for the city behind it.” The victory is already ordained, but you must go about it the way the Lord commanded. The spiritual side of the war is obedience.

So endure hardness. Some send emails saying, I am no longer with IUIC, I am going to take a break. Taking a break from the Lord? That will not work. A good soldier does not entangle himself with the affairs of this life; he stays in the fight to please the one who chose him.

thread.label: Psalms 147:1-7

precepts.label: Mark 7:21
precepts.why:
The psalm says the Lord “gathereth together the outcasts of Israel. He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds.” Who are the broken in heart? We are the ones broken in mind and spirit, because the heart is the mind. Christ shows it: “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts”. Thoughts come out of the heart, so the heart is the mind.

The broken in heart are the broken in mind: the twelve tribes, the outcasts of Israel. And it is the Lord who “bindeth up their wounds”. Everything we went through in captivity, it is the Lord that will minister the ointment to fix and heal his nation. These other nations cannot fix you with their philosophies and doctrines; they don't care about us and do not want to restore us, because restoring us means giving back everything they spoiled from the children of Israel.

Many of our brothers and sisters feel the only way we will come together is by the hands of these other nations. But it is Christ who is coming to restore this glorious nation, build up Jerusalem, gather the outcasts, and heal the broken in mind.

thread.label: Proverbs 11:21
thread.text: Though hand join in hand, the wicked shall not be unpunished: but the seed of the righteous shall be delivered.

precepts.label: 1 Maccabees 1:11
precepts.why:
“Though hand join in hand, the wicked shall not be unpunished.” The hands joined together are the black pastors holding hands with Amalek, encouraging the African-American churches to defend Israel, and even naming the Hebrew Israelites in their articles. The white man is not worried about them; they do not know the Bible and they teach heresies.

Maccabees shows this is nothing new: “In those days went there out of Israel wicked men, who persuaded many, saying, Let us go and make a covenant with the heathen that are round about us: for since we departed from them we have had much sorrow.” And “So this device pleased them well.”

Amongst our people there are wicked men, and they persuaded many. Let us make a covenant with the Greeks, with the white man. We have always had certain men among us who are wicked, who made covenants and agreements with the white man.

So the black pastors joining hands with the fake Israelis are the same wicked men of Maccabees, and the Most High says they shall not be unpunished. But the seed of the righteous, the twelve tribes of Israel, shall be delivered.

precepts.label: Isaiah 28:15-20
precepts.why:
The wicked join hand in hand by covenant, and Isaiah names that covenant: “Because ye have said, We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come unto us: for we have made lies our refuge, and under falsehood have we hid ourselves.” That is the black pastors and politicians.

“Therefore thus saith the Lord God, Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation.” This is Christ. “he that believeth shall not make haste”: you will not be confounded; you will not leave this truth.

“Judgment also will I lay to the line, and righteousness to the plummet: and the hail shall sweep away the refuge of lies.” The Lord is bringing judgment. The hail, the destruction, shall sweep away the refuge of Christianity and all its lies, and Islam as well. “And your covenant with death shall be disannulled, and your agreement with hell shall not stand.” All the blacks that made a covenant with the white man, with these fake Israelis, shall have it disannulled; the agreement with hell is this low condition our people are in. “when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, then ye shall be trodden down by it”: those black pastors shall be trodden down.

“From the time that it goeth forth it shall take you”: from the time the teaching goes forth. “for morning by morning shall it pass over, by day and by night: and it shall be a vexation only to understand the report.” Morning by morning, day and night, you are going to hear the proper teaching, and it vexes you, because you already made that agreement for the financial gain.

“For the bed is shorter than that a man can stretch himself on it: and the covering narrower than that he can wrap himself in it.” Whether you are in Christianity or politics, you are trying to get comfortable after hearing the vexing report. You know it is true, but you made that agreement. The bed is your lies and there is not enough room; you try to wrap yourself in your Christian lies, but you already heard the report. That is why the wicked, hand in hand, shall not be unpunished.

precepts.label: Ephesians 2:20
precepts.why:
The wicked join hands in a covenant with death, but the righteous have another foundation. Isaiah says, “Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation”, and that stone is Christ.

Ephesians proves it: “And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone; In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord.” Christ is the chief corner stone. We are built upon Christ and the holy apostles.

That is the difference between the two sides of Proverbs 11:21. The black pastors and politicians built on lies, their refuge of lies that the hail will sweep away. The seed of the righteous is built on the tried stone, and “he that believeth shall not make haste”: he will not be confounded and will not leave this truth. That is why the seed of the righteous shall be delivered.

precepts.label: Zechariah 11:5
precepts.why:
Latino and black pastors join hands to support Babylon and not God, not the Most High. Zechariah shows what those they join with have done to us: “Whose possessors slay them, and hold themselves not guilty: and they that sell them say, Blessed be the Lord; for I am rich: and their own shepherds pity them not.”

The ones that possess us now are the white man, and he slays us: Rasheem Carter, Kendrick Johnson, Breonna Taylor, Philando Castile, Sandra Bland, George Floyd. We found out they were hunting us on Epstein’s island. And they hold themselves not guilty.

“and they that sell them say, Blessed be the Lord; for I am rich.” They got rich from selling us into slavery. The majority of the wealth America has came from four hundred years of free chattel slavery.

“and their own shepherds pity them not.” Our own shepherds are our pastors and our congressmen and women. They pity us not because they are getting a piece of the American pie. They do not give a damn about our brothers and sisters being shot down in the street, about Rasheem Carter, about Kendrick Johnson, whose case was dismissed again though he had taser marks and cut marks and the school footage disappeared.

Those shepherds are the wicked joined hand in hand with our possessors, and they shall not be unpunished.

thread.label: Proverbs 14:25-26
thread.text: A true witness delivereth souls: but a deceitful witness speaketh lies.

precepts.label: Titus 1:13
precepts.why:
“A true witness delivereth souls”: a true prophet, a true servant, delivers souls. Paul shows how a true witness does it: “This witness is true. Wherefore rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith.”

It is our job, brothers, to rebuke our people sharply. Why? That they may be sound in the faith; that they may repent. That is how souls are delivered.

So whose soul have you been delivering? You have been sitting here five years, seven years, ten years; some of you cannot even deliver your own soul, because you forgot the mission. Who are you working for, spiritually: Messiah or Satan? Some of you are agents working for Esau.

“but a deceitful witness speaketh lies.” Our people love lies, and the deceitful witness feeds them lies. That is why you see ten thousand, twenty thousand in the Christian churches: they do not want the truth. They say Christ cannot be black, Christ cannot come only for the Israelite. The truth to us is a foreign language. That is why the true witness has to rebuke sharply: sharp rebuke is what brings a people who love lies to repentance.

precepts.label: Romans 8:29
precepts.why:
“In the fear of the Lord is strong confidence.” Some of you have no confidence and low self-esteem because you have no fear of God, sitting in the same seat for seven years. Romans shows what God called you for: “For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.”

What does it mean to be conformed? To change. We must change to the image of Jesus Christ. Some of you have not changed yet, and we can see it.

We can see the potential on you: this brother has the spirit to do great things in Israel. But you have to see it. My job as a deacon is to push your spirit and to build you up, but no matter how much I build you up, if you cannot see it, I cannot make you see it. You have to get up and see it yourself.

There is a lot of work to do while you are waiting for the kingdom, and the kingdom does not come by observation. When temptation and tribulation come, the one who has not been conformed will run, because mentally and spiritually he is not strong enough to endure it. Being predestinated to be conformed means you have to do the changing.

precepts.label: Ephesians 1:5
precepts.why:
“Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will.” The same God who foreknew us and predestinated us to be conformed to the image of his Son predestinated us unto the adoption of children, by Jesus Christ, to himself.

That calling is what the class carried straight into Paul: “For though I preach the gospel, I have nothing to glory of: for necessity is laid upon me; yea, woe is unto me, if I preach not the gospel!” Paul understood he was a servant, sent to serve the people and deliver souls. Destruction unto me if I do not do what I was sent to do.

“For if I do this thing willingly, I have a reward.” You have to do it willingly, not because somebody forced you; a brother forced to do something has no spirit in it. Yet some of you get up at four in the morning and willingly give the white man eight or twelve hours without complaining, while coming here on the Sabbath is a burden.

So being predestinated as children by Jesus Christ is not a reason to sit and wait. God did not call you here just to sit and listen. It is a call to be the true witness that delivers souls, and in the fear of the Lord is the strong confidence to do it.

precepts.label: Luke 22:48
precepts.why:
“Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.” The last part is the point: the kisses of an enemy are deceitful. And Luke shows the kiss: “Judas, betrayest thou the Son of man with a kiss?” Judas betrayed Christ with a kiss. The man betrayed him with the very sign of love.

Today we do not greet each other with a kiss like that, but we have our own greeting: Shalom, Captain, Most High bless. That is the betrayal. The embrace, the salute, the Shalom, and then the knife. That is the kiss of an enemy.

We saw it in 2018. A man who had been in another man’s house, greeting him with Shalom, barbecuing together, traveling together, came to that same man’s house, took all his furniture and put his children on the cold floor to sleep. He did not care. Not only did he betray the man, he betrayed all his children.

There is nothing worse than a traitor. And some of you think once you betray your brother or your sister, that is the end of it. It is not. The one who betrays with a kiss will be dealt with too. That is why the kisses of an enemy are called deceitful: Judas is the pattern of the familiar hand that destroys.

thread.label: Ecclesiastes 7:26
thread.text: And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.

classes.title: The Divine Orchestration and Purpose of the People You Encounter

precepts.label: Sirach 25:26
precepts.why:
“whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.” A wicked woman is given as a portion to a wicked man. But what about the man who complains of a wicked woman and claims he is not wicked himself? If that is true, he will find a way to escape. Sirach shows the way: “If she go not as thou wouldest have her, cut her off from thy flesh, and give her a bill of divorce, and let her go.”

This is the brother in the world trying to repent, trying to get his house in order and straighten it out, while his wife keeps up the traps of Ecclesiastes 7:26: her heart snares and nets, her hands as bands, creating chaos and assignments so he can't get to camp, to the brothers, to the meetings. She doesn't want to listen. Then let her go. And it goes both ways; it is about you men too.

But understand: this is not talking about a biblical marriage. Once you get married in this truth, she is yours for life, unless she commits adultery. There is no divorce in the Bible, and we don't dissolve marriages up in here; it is written in our rules. This is for those coming in from outside this truth, with all kinds of situations.

So the man who pleases God escapes from her. But if you allow yourself to be destroyed, you were indeed wicked, and the woman sent to you was your portion for real.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 7:15
precepts.why:
Paul speaks to the same case: “But if the unbelieving depart, let him depart. A brother or a sister is not under bondage in such cases: but God hath called us to peace.”

The man was wicked and inherited a wicked woman. Why? God orchestrated it, to see whether he would stay there, and to reflect what is in us so that we can change. The Lord is interested in the elect, so he puts us through trials and temptations to see if we will overcome them.

The bondage is the worldly marriage. When the spouse says, I don't care what you do, I want nothing to do with that Bible, and makes it plain and won't bend, still cooking pork and ham hocks on one side of the stove, this half is for you since you're keeping those laws, we're going to keep eating chitlins and hog maws, the house smelling like butt: if the unbelieving depart, let them depart. That is the woman of Ecclesiastes 7:26 whose heart is traps and nets, and whoso pleases God shall escape.

But those coming out of these situations have a lot of work to do before they can even think about properly marrying, and brothers and sisters are impatient. Leadership are the fathers of the men and women, and we have the records. When we tell you to lean back and let the brother or sister work on themselves, it is for a good reason, because the backdoor marriage stories are horrible, and they get worse every time a new one pops up.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 3:1-4
precepts.why:
Before anyone walks away, look at the other side. At a Passover panel years ago a sister asked when she could walk away from her husband in the world. They had been together about ten years, through Africanism, through Islam, through different things. In his mind this truth might be just another fad. Wait, sister. Lean back.

“Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives; While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear.” He is worldly, but he isn't telling you to break the laws of God, so still deal with him properly. Chaste means with discipline: you aren't cursing him out. He watches the change in you, sees the fear of the Lord in you, and sees it is serious, not a phase.

“Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel; But let it be the hidden man of the heart”, “the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price.” She puts on proper clothing, and tells him: my husband, I want you to come in and take command, so I can deal with you as a proper wife. He comes home from catching hell at work and she knows how to pull him out of it, and he asks, where are you learning this wisdom? If he is righteous, he comes in behind you; we have seen it many times.

Men do the same: a brother who was in sin with his wife last week wants to turn the house upside down this week. Give her a chance to see you're serious. Wives have said, I didn't know he was this serious; he was willing to let me go, and they came in behind him. That is the Most High giving righteousness to righteousness.

thread.text: Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters: they have forsaken the Lord, they have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward.

classes.title: Wars Are Here: Seek Good Not Evil

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 15:24
precepts.why:
Isaiah cries, “Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity”. We are laden: like a ladle dipped in soup, we are soaked and drenched with iniquity. A sinful nation means we break God's laws. So what is sin? Ezra answers: “Woe to them that sin, and keep not my commandments! saith the Lord.”

Sin is when we don't keep God's commandments. Brothers, put this in your arsenal. We always go to 1 John 5:3, of course, but we have to understand that it is precept upon precept, and Ezra says the same thing.

And who are the people that were given God's commandments? The twelve tribes of Israel. That is who Isaiah is calling the sinful nation. He was never talking about the Hittites or anybody but the Israelites.

This matters now because wars are here, and it is no time to think you are ready. You may wear your fringes, keep your beard right, keep the Sabbath and put the pork down, but still battle with patience, anger, a brawling spirit, an evil eye, or the weed you won't put down. Woe to them that sin. The whole head is sick: you're sick and I'm sick, and we have to keep getting right.

precepts.label: Psalms 147:19-20
precepts.why:
Isaiah says the sinful nation has “provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger”. To prove which nation that is: “He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel.” Jacob was the forefather of the twelve tribes, and his name later became Israel. The statutes and the judgments were given to the nation of Israel.

“He hath not dealt so with any nation”. So for modern-day Christians to say that God is dealing with all nations and all people, they don't know the Bible.

Then: “and as for his judgments, they have not known them.” The Israelites are the ones that get judged. That is why Black people went into slavery, in the trans-Saharan slave trade and the trans-Atlantic slave trade, and many other times in history we have served our enemies in slavery.

So Isaiah was never talking about anybody but the Israelites. We are the seed of evildoers who call evil good and good evil, led astray by Christian pastors and the leaders in the mosques. From 1865 to 1965 we lived under more overt racism, but we had civility, women had a dress code, and there was an order to talk to a sister. Since 1965 we have gained almost twenty million abortions by Black women alone and the dumbest generation of children with the smartest technology. We provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, and that is why we went into slavery.

precepts.label: Isaiah 58:1
precepts.why:
“The burden of Babylon, which Isaiah the son of Amoz did see. Lift ye up a banner upon the high mountain, exalt the voice unto them, shake the hand.” The high mountain is the government, America. The banner we lift up upon it is the Bible. So in the midst of all this chaos, Isaiah sees the prophets still going out teaching.

“Exalt the voice unto them”: that is what we do, and Isaiah 58 says how. “Cry aloud, spare not, lift up thy voice like a trumpet, and shew my people their transgression, and the house of Jacob their sins.” We exalt the voice, we spare not, we lift up our voice as a trumpet.

“Shake the hand”: warn our people, “that they may go into the gates of the nobles.” The nations have drunk Babylon's wine, her lies and philosophies, what Daniel calls her policy, and therefore the nations are mad. War is coming, and in the midst of all that war, the prophets are still crying aloud, showing our people their transgression so they can be saved.

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 5:11
precepts.why:
Isaiah sees the war coming on Babylon and the prophets still lifting up the banner and exalting the voice. Paul says why we do it: “Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord, we persuade men.” In Job he is called the king of terrors. We know what the Lord is going to do. The Lord set us up as watchmen, and since we know the terror of the Lord, we must persuade men.

“But we are made manifest unto God; and I trust also are made manifest in your consciences.”

Who are we trying to persuade? Our people, in the midst of all kinds of sin. So brothers, we must be studying, so that when we come across our people we are able to help them. The scripture says the whole head is sick: we are sick individuals ourselves. But we must learn to discipline ourselves, and we must learn how to persuade our people to change their lives.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 1:9-10
precepts.why:
These are the kind of people we are trying to persuade to change: “Knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane.” It is for our people who are lawless.

“For murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers.” If you knew a brother murdered his father or his mother, you would not treat him the same; your instant reaction is, bro, you cold, who does that? “For manslayers”: imagine being cool with a brother and not knowing the whole time he had bodies on him. But there is repentance for those spirits. These are the spirits we are trying to win over and get to submit to the Lord.

“For whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind”: women with all kinds of men, men with all kinds of women, and homosexuality. There is repentance for all of these sins. Some of us are struggling with one, two, three, four, five of these. God damn. We have demons on us.

The only way to get it out is to have one counsellor of a thousand and open up. That is the problem: some of you don't want to open up, and by the time we find out what you are struggling with, it's too late to help. It doesn't mean you can't repent, but it is a lot harder because you kept it secret so long, and by the time you tell us you are already having sex and we have to throw you out. Repent, submit yourself to the Lord, and stay close with the pack.

“For menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine.” How many of us lie? We all lie. Why didn't you come to the Sabbath? My back, I was tired: a lie. Why didn't you come to the new moon? I got off work late: a lie, because in your mind you already said, I'll go next time.

Can you persuade a murderer, a lesbian, a homosexual to change their life? Can you turn a liar or a thief into a soldier? You can, and the proof is that you are sitting in the building. Don't say only Deacon Eythan or Black Rhino knows how to talk to people.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 16:63-64
precepts.why:
We are to persuade our people, but this is what we have to overcome: “Surely he knoweth your inventions, and what ye think in your hearts, even them that sin, and would hide their sin.” That is what we do. We sin, and we hide our sin.

The Lord says, I know your inventions. I know why you watch HBO at night; I know why you like Spartacus, why you like Power. I know you love to smoke weed and spray yourself with cologne right before you come to the Sabbath, and then security says, that brother smells like weed. Keep smoking weed and you will end up face down in the street like the man in the video, calling the officer papi.

Some brothers are tied to unbelieving wives who cook pork on the same grill next to your lawful food, still go to the club and don't respect you, and you refuse to leave. Sisters are tied to unbelieving men. There is no love among our people, and we are caught up in these sins, lawless, like 1 Timothy 1:9.

You can hide it from the brothers and the sisters, but you cannot hide it from the Lord. He knows your inventions and what you think in your heart. So before we can persuade our people, we have to get ourselves right.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 7:61
precepts.why:
“That there should not be such heaviness in their destruction, as shall be joy over them that are persuaded to salvation.” We must persuade men to salvation. We see the wars going on with Iran; we see the prophecies coming to pass and escalating. But the Lord told us, go persuade my people to salvation, go bring them into the sanctuary.

How do we do it? Proverbs 25:15: “By long forbearing is a prince persuaded, and a soft tongue breaketh the bone.” To forbear is to patiently restrain. A prince is a very high rank, and with long patience you can persuade even princes. And what does Israel mean? Prince of the power. We have to be patient with the Israelites.

As teachers, be patient and strategic. When you are having that conversation, don't think they are just wicked as hell; they might actually repent, but you were not patient enough. Be diplomatic, learn how to reason. When people come up to you in the street, don't hit them with the first death scripture. You were once in that spot, and the only reason we are in this building is that the Lord opened our eyes.

A soft tongue breaks the bone: somebody can be pissed with you, and you respond with peace. You from Brooklyn, from DC, from PG County, want to respond even more aggressive. But the joy over one of our people persuaded to salvation is greater than the heaviness over the destruction of the rest.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 15:28-30
precepts.why:
Isaiah says, “Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them, which shall not regard silver; and as for gold, they shall not delight in it.” Before the 70s Iran was always known as Persia; that is the Medes and Persians, the second of Daniel's beasts counting from Babylon. God is going to stir them up against the United States of America, Babylon, and all the bombs, the warfare and the destroying of their economy that America and Israel are doing is what will make them rise up. They will not care about money or gold.

“Their bows also shall dash the young men to pieces; and they shall have no pity on the fruit of the womb; their eye shall not spare children.” They will even kill children. That is the third woe: it starts in the land of Israel and ends with America destroyed. “And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms” … “shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.” That is nuclear destruction.

Ezra shows who sets it off: “Behold an horrible vision, and the appearance thereof from the east: Where the nations of the dragons of Arabia shall come out with many chariots, and the multitude of them shall be carried as the wind upon earth, that all they which hear them may fear and tremble.” The dragons of Arabia are the Arabs, the sons of Ishmael. They are the ones who will fully set it off, with the Israelis in the land over there. It will not be Iran first.

“Also the Carmanians raging in wrath shall go forth as the wild boars of the wood.” The Carmanians are Iran, the Persians. Why are they raging in wrath? Because of all the oppression, the sanctions, the bombing of their cities, the killing of their leaders. In the following years Iran will be under heavy sanctions and bombed a lot by the United States, and America and Israel are trying to back a coup against the Iranian regime. Everything Trump is doing is just fulfilling Bible prophecy: he is making the Persians mad.

We don't give a crap about the Arabs or the Iranians. Those people enslaved us, and God is bringing judgment on them. America is the hammer of God, and God is using America to judge the Arabs and the Persians. Then in the end that same cup America is pouring on them is going to be poured on America.

America is about to turn up affliction on everyone on this earth, including us, and it will get worse and worse, like a woman in travail. So this is not the time to be in la-la land or in the midst of sin. It is the time to prepare ourselves and get our spirit right for what is about to take place.

precepts.label: Lamentations 2:1
precepts.why:
“How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer”: before we can know who Lucifer is, we have to know what heaven is. Lamentations shows it: “How hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger, and cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel.”

Heaven is dominion and rulership. That was the high standard, the high estate Israel held, and the beauty of Israel was cast down from it to the earth. We were set down to a low state. No one thinks Israel was literally thrown out of the sky; we fell from rulership.

So it is with Lucifer. Esau takes Jude and Isaiah 14, mixes them up and comes with this fallen angel teaching. But keep it in context. Lucifer, the lightbearer, is the king of Babylon of verse 4, the oppressor, the one who “smote the people in wrath with a continual stroke.” It is talking about a nation: this so-called white man, America, whom everybody looks at as god and all knowing because he controls communication everywhere.

He is falling from heaven the same way Israel did: he is losing his dominion and his rulership. “They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble”: not a fallen angel, not the Nephilim, but the man, the one who made the earth tremble by dropping atom bombs everywhere. The angels are not falling out of heaven; they take their directive from the Most High God.

precepts.label: Daniel 7:27
precepts.why:
Daniel shows again what heaven means: “And the kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High.” That is rulership. The greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven is dominion over the nations, and it is given to the saints of the Most High, Israel.

So when Isaiah says “How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!”, it is the fall of a ruler from his dominion. How did you fall from rulership? Lucifer is the king of Babylon, the oppressor who weakened the nations with his bombs, his lies and his fornication.

He said in his heart, “I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God: I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north”, North America, and “I will be like the most High.” “Yet thou shalt be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit.”

Put the two together. The rulership he grasped at, he loses, and the kingdom and dominion under the whole heaven is given to the people of the saints of the Most High. It is not an angel cast out of the sky; it is the man, this so-called white man, America, brought down, and Israel lifted up to rule.

precepts.label: Isaiah 13:19
precepts.why:
“How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!” Lucifer is another name for Esau, alongside Tyrus and Edom, and further up the chapter he is called the king of Babylon. How did he weaken the nations? Through war. A US destroyer took down two fighter jets in ninety-three seconds, having calculated seventeen ways to kill them before they reached altitude. Venezuela’s defenses, its bases and its president were taken in thirty minutes. That is why his pride is lifted up, and why the ignorant say he must be God.

Isaiah 13 names what he is: “And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms.” The Space Command headquarters moving to Huntsville, Alabama, now to be called Rocket City, means more weaponry, the smith and the waster that God created. Babylon is the glory of kingdoms: all these nations want to come to Babylon and get a piece of it. They call it the American dream.

The world is amazed at the beast: “Who is like unto the beast? who is able to make war with him?” But that same verse of Isaiah 13 says the glory of kingdoms shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah. The Lord “hath broken the staff of the wicked, and the sceptre of the rulers. He who smote the people in wrath with a continual stroke”, primarily God’s people, is brought down.

So the glory of kingdoms falls from heaven like Lucifer, and then “The whole earth is at rest, and is quiet: they break forth into singing.” When these devils fall, the whole earth will finally be at rest.
