precepts.label: Luke 21:24
precepts.why:
“In that day shall his strong cities be as a forsaken bough, and an uppermost branch, which they left because of the children of Israel: and there shall be desolation.” We were moved out of the land. Why? “Because thou hast forgotten the God of thy salvation, and hast not been mindful of the rock of thy strength.” We have not been mindful of him. “Therefore shalt thou plant pleasant plants, and shalt set it with strange slips.”

What is a slip? A cutting from a plant, a branch or twig. Strange slips are strange branches: Esau. They are strange, not the people of the book, not the people of the covenant, set into the land. Christ said the same thing about strange slips coming into the land.

“And they shall fall by the edge of the sword”: the real Israelites fell by the edge of Rome's sword. “And shall be led away captive into all nations”: captive means slaves, carried into all nations.

“And Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.” Christ is telling you the Gentiles are going to take over the land. That is what Isaiah said about the strange slips, the strange people who would take the land while the real children of Israel were scattered. And these leaders who bring out that they are not the real Jews disappear and die; we are the last ones standing.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 7:24
precepts.why:
Isaiah says the land would be set “with strange slips”, and Christ says Jerusalem would be “trodden down of the Gentiles.” Ezekiel gives another precept on who those strangers are.

“Wherefore I will bring the worst of the heathen, and they shall possess their houses.” God calls them the worst of the heathen, and they will possess our houses. Those are the Gentiles Christ was speaking about in Luke 21:24, the strange slips planted in our land.

“I will also make the pomp of the strong to cease; and their holy places shall be defiled. Destruction cometh; and they shall seek peace, and there shall be none. Mischief shall come upon mischief, and rumour shall be upon rumour.”

That is what we see now. America and Israel fund rebel forces and put a former al-Qaeda commander, Abu Mohammad al-Jolani, once with a ten-million-dollar bounty on his head, in as president of Syria, because Assad said they are not even real Jews and shouldn't be in the land; now Trump shakes his hand in the White House. precepts.label: Revelation 11:8
precepts.why:
“The burden of Egypt.” Egypt was before Isaiah’s time, so what Egypt is this speaking about? Revelation answers it: “their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.”

It says spiritually. Sodom is not around anymore; it is destroyed, those cities of Sodom and Gomorrah near Ein Bokek are nothing. But spiritual Sodom is here. It goes on even in the landmass of Israel among the Israelis, but prominently and predominately here in America, with all types of switcheroos: men acting like women and women acting like men, committing things contrary to the laws of God. And it is spiritual Egypt, the house of bondage. So replace Egypt with America: the burden of America.

“where also our Lord was crucified.” They crucify Christ in his image, in his message, and in denying that you men are the greatest thing on the face of this earth. They say, hell no, all people, God loves everybody.

“And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city.” America is that great city, and our people are spiritually dead here. They are fearful of freedom; there is no spirit in them to rebel with the laws of God.

So when Isaiah says the Lord rides upon a swift cloud and comes into Egypt, it is the Lord coming with his chariots and angels to bring wrath and destruction upon America. Its idols shall be moved at his presence, and its heart, the mindset, doctrines and mentality of the oppressive kingdom, shall melt in the midst of it. He will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: militia against militia, civil war, brother against brother, city against city. This place is divided; the stars are falling and the stripes are broken. That is Esau rising against himself, and it is not our fight.

precepts.label: Isaiah 31:3
precepts.why:
“Now the Egyptians are men, and not God; and their horses flesh, and not spirit.” That is the war of gods. On one side is the god still sitting in our minds, the image of white supremacy that was forced into our spirits; on the other side is the God of this Bible. The Egyptians set themselves up as gods, but they are only men, and all their weaponry is flesh.

Their weapons are not only for warring with other people. They are there to force a thought into our minds, to force white supremacy into our spirits. So the war is first in the mind, and the ignorance of our people is the battlefield.

“When the Lord shall stretch out his hand, both he that helpeth shall fall, and he that is holpen shall fall down, and they all shall fail together.” That is what Isaiah 19 shows: the Lord sets “the Egyptians against the Egyptians”, “city against city, and kingdom against kingdom”, and “the spirit of Egypt shall fail in the midst thereof.” There is going to be civil war, and there will be wars from outside as well.

And when it comes, “they shall seek to the idols, and to the charmers, and to them that have familiar spirits, and to the wizards.” They will cry out to the images they revered as gods, talking to those Jesus pieces, asking them to come save them. They will run back to the news outlets that lied for years, to Christianity, to every version of white supremacy. But men are not God, and none of it will hold them up.

So the Lord is teaching us war tactics, because there are going to be wars in the flesh. We have to keep strong in the war we already have in our spirit, knowing the ones who made themselves gods over us are only flesh.

precepts.label: Revelation 11:8
precepts.why:
Revelation 11 shows everybody where Egypt is: “their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.” This place, America, is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt. So when Isaiah says “I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians”, he is speaking of civil war in this land, city against city and kingdom against kingdom.

That is why Isaiah 19 goes on: “The Lord hath mingled a perverse spirit in the midst thereof: and they have caused Egypt to err in every work thereof.” God put a perverse spirit here, and it causes this place to be in error in everything it does. Everything that America does is in error, because there is a perverse spirit here.

You can see it in the news. Trump went to the Ford plant, a worker called him a pedophile protector, and he shot the man the bird and said “F you”. The man was suspended, and the union is fighting to get him off suspension. Somebody called out the perverse spirit, and even when they are shown their errors, they flip you the bird and make sure you lose your job.

So Sodom and Egypt is not a far-off place. It is the land we are in, and the land that the Lord will turn against itself.

precepts.label: Joel 2:15-20
precepts.why:
Isaiah says “they shall cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors.” What will the oppressors be doing? The same thing 2 Esdras 16, Revelation 12:17, Matthew 10 and Matthew 24 say: Jacob's trouble. Joel shows the crying.

“Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly: Gather the people, sanctify the congregation, assemble the elders, gather the children, and those that suck the breasts.” This is going to be a major fast, because there will be so much devastation to our people. “Let the bridegroom go forth of his chamber, and the bride out of her closet”: when this fast goes out, we are not doing weddings or planning weddings. Weddings are finished. We have to pray to the Lord because our people are dying.

“Let the priests, the ministers of the Lord, weep between the porch and the altar, and let them say, Spare thy people, O Lord.” That is the cry of Isaiah 19, crying bitterly because there is going to be death. “And give not thine heritage to reproach, that the heathen should rule over them: wherefore should they say among the people, Where is their God?”

“Then will the Lord be jealous for his land, and pity his people.” He answers, “I will send you corn, and wine, and oil” and “I will no more make you a reproach among the heathen: But I will remove far off from you the northern army.” That is the great multitude after us in 2 Esdras 16. He will “drive him into a land barren and desolate, with his face toward the east sea, and his hinder part toward the utmost sea.” The east sea is the Dead Sea and the utmost sea is the Mediterranean: the land of Israel between them, what they call the Middle East. The Lord is going to cause things to pop off there.

“And his stink shall come up, and his ill savour shall come up, because he hath done great things.” The Lord is going to destroy them over there: tribulation, World War III, Armageddon. It is all laid out for us. Yes, you are dying, but you are not dead; the Lord takes the northern army down, and then he sends us “a saviour, and a great one”, Christ, to deliver us.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 49:20-22
precepts.why:
Joel says the Lord will remove the northern army far off and drive it into the land between the Dead Sea and the Mediterranean. Jeremiah shows what happens there.

“Therefore hear the counsel of the Lord, that he hath taken against Edom; and his purposes, that he hath purposed against the inhabitants of Teman.” Teman is still Edom. “Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out”: the least of the flock is these Israelis, the fake Israelis. That whole area on the map is where it is all going to go down. “Surely he shall make their habitations desolate with them.”

“The earth is moved at the noise of their fall, at the cry the noise thereof was heard in the Red sea.” The ships in the Red Sea are going to hear about this fall.

“Behold, he shall come up and fly as the eagle, and spread his wings over Bozrah.” Bozrah is Jordan, that area on the map. America is going to come to Israel's rescue, so they think. “And at that day shall the heart of the mighty men of Edom be as the heart of a woman in her pangs.” They are going to be afraid, because they don't realize it's a trap: NATO turns against them, and everybody is against America and Israel.

That is how the Lord takes the northern army down over there, while he tells us, don't worry, you are dying but you are not dead. Jacob's trouble is great, “but he shall be saved out of it.”

Wherever you go, whatever church you sit in, whatever continent, country or island, they all think the white man is God and that Christ is white. Now the same persuasion is being pushed that the UFOs, the chariots, are demonic fallen angels, to turn the minds of the people to fight against Christ.

How did he spread this veil over all nations? His media, his network, his communication, because he is the prince of the power of the air; he controls the airwaves. And how will the covering be destroyed? The Most High is using us to do it: lifting up the banner, the Bible, upon that high mountain, exalting the voice, casting down the lies and revealing the lies Esau has been telling our people.

precepts.label: John 8:58
precepts.why:
“Trust ye in the Lord for ever: for in the Lord Jehovah is everlasting strength.” Jehovah has three syllables, and there is no J in Hebrew, so what was there originally is Yah-ha-wah, three syllables: not Jehovah, and not Yahweh, which is two. Then Christ gives us a heavy secret about who that Lord is.

“Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am.” He is letting them know he is the I AM of Exodus: “And God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: and he said, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you.” That is Christ. He is saying, that Yah you were praying to, that was me back then.

Philip said, “Lord, shew us the Father, and it sufficeth us.” And Christ answered, “Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip?” You want to see the Father that created you? I am the Father that created you. Isaiah calls the child that is born and the son that is given “The mighty God, The everlasting Father.” And John says, “All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.”

Now we know Christ is not the Father. But the God that was dealing with us in the Old Testament was Christ; that is why he said he comes in the volume of the book, and it is written of him. He is the only begotten of the Father: the Father only created Christ, and then said, this is your world, you create it. Proverbs 8 speaks of it, how he was daily the Father's delight, brought up with him.

So the Lord Jehovah of Isaiah 26, who “bringeth down them that dwell on high” and lays the lofty city low even to the dust, is Christ. They get mad online and say stop misleading the people, but that is the God in whom is everlasting strength, the one we are to trust for ever.

thread.label: Isaiah 26:3
thread.text: Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.

precepts.label: Jude 1:20-21
precepts.why:
Isaiah says the Lord keeps him in perfect peace “because he trusteth in thee.” That is the key part. You trust in the Lord, you trust in his words, and you build yourself up. Jude says it: “But ye, beloved, building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost”.

It is the leaders' job to build the man, but once you have the foundation, it is on you to take the notes from the classes, apply them to yourself and add to them. Do a serious checkup from the neck up. Take an erasable dry marker to your mirror and write your issues with the scriptures next to them, what you need to fix, and at the top write: execute. Those are your orders for the day. If you don't see it, you're never going to fix it. Too many brothers and sisters don't write anything down: notes done, Bible closed the rest of the week, and then they're stressing, when the fix to what they were dealing with last week and what they will face this week came out in the class. We don't examine ourselves.

Don't ask the captain what he sees in you. What do you see in you? Leadership has the blessing of discernment, but that only goes so far; we can't see through you or know all the deep recesses of what you're dealing with. You have to go before the Lord, explain it, confess it, and ask him in sincerity to remove those things from you.

Don't play with what you know you are dealing with. The spirits on brothers and sisters who could care less can rub off even on leadership; a lot of brothers and sisters are spiritual vampires, and it takes a toll on leaders who love our people. God has this hospital set up for you to get the help, and the medicine is the laws. You have a headache, you don't throw the Tylenol in the trash, you take it. So why throw away the medicine when it concerns your soul and your salvation? Why be fearful of freedom?

“Keep yourselves in the love of God, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ unto eternal life.” Keep yourselves in the love of God, not in the crosshairs of his anger, his rage, his wrath. It is our job to keep ourselves there. I can't save you, and you can't save me. It ain't going to be easy; you have to go through this fiery trial to get the kingdom. So do your part. You have the keys to freedom, and that is the trust that keeps the mind stayed on the Lord in perfect peace.

precepts.label: Joshua 1:8
precepts.why:
What actually brings us peace? Not enlisting in this war, and not hoping America goes back to the old ways. “Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee”. The mind that is stayed on the Lord is the mindset of Joshua 1:8: the book of the law does not depart out of your mouth, and you meditate on it day and night.

That is your four chapters a day. That is you not separating yourself, and having that godly conversation consistently, as in Malachi, where they thought upon the Lord's name and a book of remembrance was written. That is making sure the sick among us in the congregations are well taken care of. That is you men doing the blitz, traveling, doing your due diligence by all manner to get out of that black shirt and get out here and teach your people, to become men of valor and soldiers of the Lord, and put in your brick.

You establish yourself on the laws of God. That is your meditation, your chief joy. You're not worried about what is played on the radio, and you could give a damn about what's on the internet unless it is funneled through the Bible so you can keep up with the times.

Then the news, the destruction and the chaos won't worry you. You'll have a Coke bottle smile from one ear to the next, because you know the mysteries. You're not fearful of freedom. The mind that meditates on the law day and night is the mind the Lord keeps in perfect peace.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 35:6-7
precepts.why:
“Let favour be shewed to the wicked, yet will he not learn righteousness: in the land of uprightness will he deal unjustly.” The land of uprightness is the land of Israel, and the abomination of desolation, the robbers of God's people, are in it dealing unjustly with everyone over there, killing and decapitating babies. “Yea, the fire of thine enemies shall devour them”: God's enemies are the Europeans and the Persians, and that fire is nuclear destruction. Ezekiel shows why their end is blood.

“Therefore, as I live, saith the Lord God, I will prepare thee unto blood, and blood shall pursue thee.” God is going to prepare Edom, the white man, unto blood: he is preparing the place where his blood will be shed. The time is coming when blood will pursue America, the Israelis and the Europeans.

Why? “Sith thou hast not hated blood, even blood shall pursue thee.” Because they don't hate blood. They love murdering and killing. You love blood, you like eating blood, you like shedding blood; you bloody man, so blood goes and pursues you. Even the name Amalek, in their own rabbinical tradition, is taken from am, a nation or people, and lak, to lick: a people who lick blood.

“Thus will I make mount Seir most desolate.” The Lord is going to destroy them. That is a dark sentence, a parable. It is not talking about the past, because people still travel through that place today; it is talking about the future.

They will not learn righteousness no matter what favour is shown them, and what they are doing in that land will cause all the Arabs to unite against them, and the Persians will join after them. That is the blood that will pursue them.

precepts.label: Habakkuk 2:7-8
precepts.why:
“Shall they not rise up suddenly that shall bite thee.” The ones who rise up are the people being oppressed, the nations. “And awake that shall vex thee”: that is the sleeper cells. “And thou shalt be for booties unto them?” After Trump is finished with the Persians, they will go into secret vengeance, building all types of things in secret and waiting for the right time.

“Because thou hast spoiled many nations, all the remnant of the people shall spoil thee.” You spoiled Venezuela, you are spoiling Cuba right now, you are spoiling Iran. Trump has bombed at least seven countries in one year since he came into power, Nigeria among them, and it is just the beginning.

“Because of men’s blood, and for the violence of the land.” Because you love blood, blood will follow you, as Ezekiel 35 said. Because you love war, because of the people you murder, because you are violent people. How are you trying to negotiate? They negotiate with you, and while you are negotiating they come and bomb you and kill you, and they don't care who is there. It wasn't just the Ayatollah killed: his children, nephews and brother-in-law were killed too.

Now it is the Department of War and the secretary of war; you are not about defense anymore. They are trying to program AI machines to kill humans, and to use that same AI to surveil the citizens. These things are the beginning of sorrows. America has spoiled many nations, and all the remnant of the people shall spoil it.

precepts.label: Isaiah 59:9-15
precepts.why:
“Lord, in trouble have they visited thee, they poured out a prayer when thy chastening was upon them.” The only time we cry to the Lord is when we are chastised; as Hosea says, “in their affliction they will seek me early.” Isaiah 59 is that cry.

“Therefore is judgment far from us, neither doth justice overtake us: we wait for light, but behold obscurity; for brightness, but we walk in darkness.” Obscurity is confusion. “We grope for the wall like the blind, and we grope as if we had no eyes.” Black people and Latin people act as if we have no eyes. We see the evil, and then we say, some of them are good, they ain't all like that.

“We stumble at noonday as in the night; we are in desolate places as dead men”: we are like the walking dead. “We roar all like bears”: that is us crying and screaming in the streets, “and mourn sore like doves: we look for judgment, but there is none; for salvation, but it is far off from us. For our transgressions are multiplied before thee, and our sins testify against us.”

“And judgment is turned away backward, and justice standeth afar off: for truth is fallen in the street, and equity cannot enter. Yea, truth faileth; and he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey.” The judgment we seek in this wicked kingdom is always turned backward, and the truth of God fails out here.

We are watching it on the screen. Young Black men found hanging from trees in Charlotte, Albany, Oakland, Albuquerque, Brookfield, Marietta, and on the campus of Delta State with the back of his head smashed in, every one ruled a suicide with no foul play. Keith Porter shot by an off-duty ICE agent on New Year's Eve; Dr. Linda Davis killed by a driver fleeing ICE. A sixteen-year-old boy in Houston shot on a porch while holding up a wallet he was trying to return, the shooter released, and the boy's family ordered to pay $20,000. No justice, no peace.

We had sixty years of a little liberty that Esau gave us, and we could have done astronomical things, but we dropped the ball. We wanted to sin and be like the other nations, twerking and dancing while the Bible warned us. Now the white man is undoing it, done pretending he is not the devil, and the hangings of the '40s and '50s are starting all over again. So be careful with your children. That is why we cry now: because of our sins.

thread.label: Isaiah 26:20-21

precepts.label: Revelation 20:11-15
precepts.why:
“For, behold, the Lord cometh out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity: the earth also shall disclose her blood, and shall no more cover her slain.” Revelation 20 shows that day of judgment.

“And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away; and there was found no place for them.” That is Christ, in full power, and nobody opens their damn mouth against him. We thought it was the Father judging us, but it is Christ: “we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad.” And “the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son.”

“And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened”: this is everybody, and the books are the Bible. “And another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.” As Ecclesiastes says, “God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.” We are judged according to our works, whether we were in God's laws or against God's laws.

“And the sea gave up the dead which were in it; and death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them.” That is what Isaiah 26 said: the earth shall no more cover her slain. Hell is the grave; those that died in the graves were given up, “and they were judged every man according to their works.”

“And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death.” Death is finished at that point. And what goes with death and hell? The nations: “whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.” That includes all the nations. The Lord comes out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth, and this is where that punishment ends.

precepts.label: Daniel 12:1
precepts.why:
Revelation 20 says whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire. So who is written in the book of life? Is it the Chinese, the white man, or the Arabs? Daniel answers.

“And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time.” That is the indignation of Isaiah 26, when God's people must “enter thou into thy chambers” and hide “until the indignation be overpast.” There will be so much devastation that we will be fearful.

“And at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.” Who is written in the book of life? Israel, Daniel's people. Not everybody.

Jeremiah says the same, and they hate this one: “Fear thou not, O Jacob my servant, saith the Lord: for I am with thee; for I will make a full end of all the nations whither I have driven thee: but I will not make a full end of thee, but correct thee in measure; yet will I not leave thee wholly unpunished.” God is correcting us in measure, but he will not destroy us.

And Ezra: “Let the multitude perish then, which was born in vain; and let my grape be kept, and my plant; for with great labour have I made it perfect.” All the nations were born in vain; the Israelites are the grape and the plant that is kept. So when the Lord comes out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth, Israel written in the book is delivered, and all the nations go into the lake of fire.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 9:10
precepts.why:
Isaiah gives an analogy of a farmer: “Doth the plowman plow all day to sow? doth he open and break the clods of his ground?” He breaks the dirt, makes the ground flat, and casts abroad his seeds. But is Isaiah really talking about farmland?

Paul answers it: “Or saith he it altogether for our sakes? For our sakes, no doubt, this is written: that he that ploweth should plow in hope; and that he that thresheth in hope should be partaker of his hope.” It wasn't really talking about farms. The plowing and the threshing were not about growing seeds.

The plowing represents teaching. We are to plow in hope: to teach, instruct, and give hope to our people. You brothers are fishers of men, and the field is our people. That is how Isaiah 28 applies to you.

So the fitches, cummin, principal wheat, appointed barley and rye are the different people we plow for, and the farmer's instruments are the different ways we must deal with them to persuade them to salvation. By long forbearing even a prince is persuaded, and Israel is a prince: we have to be patient with our people.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 3:1
precepts.why:
The farmer casts “the principal wheat and the appointed barley” in their place, and there is a time to grow barley: you have to know when to show mercy, when to be strong and assertive, when to be diplomatic, and whom to talk to. “his God doth instruct him to discretion”: careful and circumspect in speech and action, to avoid causing offence or to gain an advantage. You know how to speak, and you know when to speak.

You may say, I'm putting my time in teaching this brother and he won't come to the school. Read this: “To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven”. Not to some things, not to little things: to every thing there is a season.

So when we're fishing, there is a time to talk about the truth with that brother. Sometimes you're talking out of season. He was stressed from work, things were going on, his mind just wasn't open, and you didn't discern it. But if you pay attention and watch, the moment comes: Leroy calls and says, I was watching this documentary about the space landing, and I'm starting to think this world isn't what I thought it was. Got him. You waited two years for Leroy, and Leroy opened up.

At the end of the day the Lord brings them in. But we are at war, Russia and China are about to get involved, and it's only going to get worse. We have to be better fishermen, and be patient with our brothers and sisters.

precepts.label: Luke 9:52-55
precepts.why:
The fitches are not threshed with a threshing instrument, nor the cummin under a cart wheel; each seed has its own instrument. Even the disciples used the wrong one. The Samaritans “did not receive him, because his face was as though he would go to Jerusalem. And when his disciples James and John saw this, they said, Lord, wilt thou that we command fire to come down from heaven, and consume them, even as Elias did?” Let's go get the death scriptures; let's pray the Lord takes them out.

“But he turned, and rebuked them, and said, Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of.” Brothers, you have to know what manner of spirit you're supposed to be in when you deal with the people in the street. Sisters, the same way. Sometimes the brothers do the work, the people come in, and the sisters undo the work by not saying hello, shalom, or Christ bless. Sisters need to learn how to fish too.

Always represent this truth with the utmost professionalism, because we have a job: to win souls, and we don't have much time. As soon as you step into a room or a store, map out whom you think you can bring the truth to. You don't have to be a soldier to do that. Brother O'Shea in New York is 83; he hands out his fifty flyers a week, and the home health aide who came to him from the nursing home started wearing dresses.

We must be fishers of men, because war is imminent and danger is coming. Knowing the right spirit for each person is the discretion God instructs the plowman in.

precepts.label: Hebrews 10:7
precepts.why:
Isaiah says, “Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read.” The book of the Lord is the Bible, and whose book is it? Hebrews answers: “Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God.”

Christ comes in the volume of the book. Everybody has to understand that. The Lord comes in the volume of the book, and it is written of him. When you read the Bible and it says the Lord said this and the Lord did that, it is talking about Christ. He is the one who was speaking right through the scriptures, and he is the one who was dealing with us right through the scriptures.

So tie it back to Isaiah: seek ye out of the book of the Lord, the book of the Lord. What we read there is written of him; that is him, the Lord, right there. And because it is his book and his word, “no one of these shall fail.” Nothing written in it will fail. Everything we read about in it is going to come to pass, whether you believe or not, and you cannot mate the Bible with any other book.

“for my mouth it hath commanded, and his spirit it hath gathered them.” The words on those pages are the Lord’s spirit, the words of Christ, who came in the volume of the book to do the will of God.

precepts.label: John 5:46-47
precepts.why:
Christ says, “For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me.” Moses wrote of Christ. When you read it in Genesis, in Exodus, in Numbers, in Deuteronomy, right through the scriptures, the one Moses was talking about when he wrote “the Lord said” and “the Lord did” was always Christ. That is why Christ can say that if you believed Moses you would have believed him.

“But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words?” The writings of Moses and the words of Christ stand together; to reject one is to reject the other.

This is the book Isaiah sends us to: “Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read.” Read with Hebrews 10:7, where Christ says “in the volume of the book it is written of me”, it shows that the whole book of the Lord, from the writings of Moses on, is written of Christ. So when we seek out of that book and read, we are reading of him, and “no one of these shall fail”: everything written there is going to come to pass.

thread.label: Isaiah 42:22
thread.text: But this is a people robbed and spoiled; they are all of them snared in holes, and they are hid in prison houses: they are for a prey, and none delivereth; for a spoil, and none saith, Restore.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 30:16
precepts.why:
Isaiah calls Israel “a people robbed and spoiled.” We are robbed of our nationality, robbed of the understanding that we are the twelve tribes of the children of Israel. Jeremiah shows how we are spoiled, and what the Lord will do about it.

“Therefore all they that devour thee shall be devoured”: that is going to take place upon the oppressors of our people. “and all thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity”: the adversaries are all the nations outside of the children of Israel, and every one of the nations that oppress us shall go into captivity.

How do they spoil us? Over a multitude of captivities the children of Israel have gone into, every single nation has had its hand in the oppression of the twelve tribes. That includes the Arabs, that a lot of brothers and sisters want to cry over when they see what is going on in Palestine. Those people had our people oppressed too; they were spoiling the hell out of us. What we are seeing overseas right now is the righteous judgment of the Lord, prophecy fulfilling right now.

Yet brothers and sisters are so damn fearful to escape this captivity and get themselves together, even as the prophecies come to pass. Many are called, but few are chosen, so self-examine. With bombs dropping and rumors of war, men are still catting around, committing fornication, letting their wives rule over them and hide their folly, paying for prostitutes, hooked on marijuana and controlled by the porn system. Our people are sick; they are afraid of freedom, because sin controls them.

“and they that spoil thee shall be a spoil, and all that prey upon thee will I give for a prey.” The nations that spoiled us shall in turn be a spoil for us, because the tables are turned. We serve a just God. So Isaiah’s people “for a prey” and “for a spoil” will not stay that way: those that prey upon Israel are given for a prey themselves.

thread.label: Isaiah 43:3-11
thread.text: For I am the Lord thy God, the Holy One of Israel, thy Saviour: I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee.

precepts.label: Revelation 18:4
precepts.why:
“I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee.” The Lord gave other nations for us: he brought blood and destruction on their heads on our behalf. “Since thou wast precious in my sight”, not yellow, black and white all precious in his sight like the Christian song says, but the twelve tribes, “therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.” He didn't say he would spare the little Arab kids or the Israeli kids planted in the land. Revelation shows how much he loves us in the middle of that.

He has put it in front of us in prophecy: what is about to go down, where it is going down, who is involved and who is conspiring against Israel, and the parts they will play. He has told us not to meddle with them, and he has told us what to do to secure our salvation.

“And I heard another voice from heaven, saying, Come out of her, my people.” Who are his people? According to Isaiah 3:12, children are their oppressors and women rule over them; only the southern kingdom and northern kingdom have that problem. So he is letting you know it is only Israel.

“That ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.” Don't be part of the sins and the plagues coming on this place, the land of the north where Esau dwells, or in the valley of decision where everybody is gathering for the great day of Armageddon. Don't receive the death and destruction on the way when the Most High shows up.

So your fight is not with the nations. Your fight is with getting yourself together, working on your salvation, so you can see the promise made to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

precepts.label: Isaiah 3:12
precepts.why:
Isaiah 43 says, “Since thou wast precious in my sight, thou hast been honourable, and I have loved thee: therefore will I give men for thee.” Who is the “thee” the Lord loves and gives other nations for? Revelation 18 says “Come out of her, my people”, and Isaiah 3 identifies who his people are.

“As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them.” There is only one people with that problem: the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom, Israel. We are the only ones living under it.

So “my people” is Israel, not all nations. The fools who want to engraft all the nations say, what about all nations? But if you acknowledge that we are the twelve tribes of Israel and still want to engraft every other nation in, when are you going to acknowledge that they have to give us back our land and everything that belongs to us? You won't. It's hypocrisy.

The Lord has not dealt with any other nation. “Even every one that is called by my name: for I have created him for my glory”, and “Ye are my witnesses, saith the Lord.” All the destruction coming on the other nations is to set the twelve tribes of Israel, those keeping the commandments and striving, back in their rightful place.

thread.label: Isaiah 45:4
thread.text: For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name: I have surnamed thee, though thou hast not known me.

precepts.label: Exodus 15:3
precepts.why:
In Isaiah 45 the Lord says, “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name: I have surnamed thee, though thou hast not known me”. God surnamed us, and even though he revealed himself to us and delivered us numerous times, we kept turning our backs on him. “I am the Lord, and there is none else, there is no God beside me”. Some set themselves up as gods, and some create gods in their minds and as idols, but there is none with him. “I form the light, and create darkness: I make peace, and create evil: I the Lord do all these things”.

Exodus 15:3 fills in the picture: “The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name”. The same Lord that forms the light, creates darkness, makes peace and creates evil is also a man of war. That is the overall picture of the Lord our God.

Psalms 46 shows what that looks like: “Come, behold the works of the Lord, what desolations he hath made in the earth”. Pharaohs were worshipped as gods, Xerxes thought he was a god, and Antiochus Epiphanes thought he was God manifest on earth; rulers rise in power and rise in pride. But “He maketh wars to cease unto the end of the earth; he breaketh the bow, and cutteth the spear in sunder”. The man on the thumbnail who has claimed for two years that he will stop the war between Ukraine and Russia has not stopped anything. When the Iron Dome in Israel failed and the rockets came through, that was no technical glitch; the Lord ripped it open. He makes the prideful instruments of man fail, because he decides where war happens and when it ceases.

And that God of war, who formed the light and created darkness, is Christ. He is our refuge, and he teaches his soldiers to do the same: “Blessed be the Lord my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight”. He handpicked us to be soldiers in his army.

thread.label: Isaiah 46:8-10
thread.text: Remember this, and shew yourselves men: bring it again to mind, O ye transgressors.

precepts.label: Habakkuk 3:16
precepts.why:
God is “declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done.” Only the God of Israel can do that, and he shows the end to the prophets. Look at the videos of the missiles coming down at night: don't they look like stars falling from heaven? The prophets had never seen a missile, an Iron Dome, a supersonic missile or a nuclear weapon. They described what they saw to the best of their ability, and it is our job to put it together. Put yourself in the prophet's shoes, because you are the prophets; you just don't remember.

Habakkuk describes how it hurts when these missiles hit, because when they hit they bring destruction. You don't want to be around when a missile hits the ground; you don't even want to be ten feet away.

“When I heard, my belly trembled.” That kind of fear is an anxiety sitting inside you, in your chest. He cannot believe what he is watching, but the Lord had to show it to him. “My lips quivered at the voice”: he was shaking, he couldn't even talk straight. “Rottenness entered into my bones, and I trembled in myself.” He could not believe the damage this thing was doing, the number of people it killed when it hit.

“That I might rest in the day of trouble.” He is saying, I don't want to be alive to see this. It is so bad I don't want to be around to see it. That is what Psalms 91 means by a thousand falling at thy side and ten thousand at thy right hand: he saw the bomb drop and ten thousand people die right there.

That is the end God declared from the beginning, and “My counsel shall stand.” The media say Hamas is finished, Hezbollah has no weapons, Iran is weak; yet Hezbollah fired a hundred missiles into Israel the other day, and Israel cannot destroy Hamas under its nose while Iran is seven times bigger than Israel. We are going with the Bible. If you want the kingdom of heaven, you must accept what comes with it: war, tribulation and death.

precepts.label: Amos 3:6
precepts.why:
“Remember this, and shew yourselves men: bring it again to mind, O ye transgressors. Remember the former things of old: for I am God, and there is none else.” Only God is “Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done, saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure.” Where do you find God’s counsel? The Bible. Whatever the scripture says, the prophecy is going to happen. Forget the dumb pastors and dumb Christians who do not know anything.

Amos shows who is behind what is happening: “Shall a trumpet be blown in the city, and the people not be afraid? shall there be evil in a city, and the Lord hath not done it?” The trumpet is the Bible. And yes, there is evil in America, and the Lord has done it.

“Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.” We are the prophets. Our job, brothers, is to prepare our people for what is coming. Our job is not to pick up guns and knives thinking you can do something to the white man; this man will wipe you out just like that. Our job is to bring the people back to Messiah and prepare their minds for the second coming of Jesus Christ, the black Messiah, revealing the Bible plainly so they may repent. Wait on the Lord.

“come, and let us declare in Zion the work of the Lord our God.” We are Zion, and our job is to declare in Zion the work of the Lord: what is coming, and how to fix your spirit and build yourself up. To our brothers and sisters in Venezuela: repent. You cannot stop the white man; let him do what he was supposed to do. The evil in the city is the Lord’s counsel standing, and it is revealed to his prophets.

thread.text: And now, saith the Lord that formed me from the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob again to him, Though Israel be not gathered, yet shall I be glorious in the eyes of the Lord, and my God shall be my strength.

precepts.label: Romans 10:14-15
precepts.why:
Isaiah says the Lord formed his servant from the womb “to bring Jacob again to him”, “to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel”, “that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth.” That you may be a saviour. A lot of times we, the prophets, don’t understand the magnitude of our calling. The Lord said he would send us as saviours, and our people’s salvation will come no other way than by the prophets, the saviours God sent, and through his word. Paul shows why.

“How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard?” This shows the importance of the prophets, the saviours: there is no way for the people to be saved unless the saviours are sent. “and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent?”

We have been sent, throughout the four corners of the earth, and from the beginning, to be saviours. By going forth and teaching God’s word, salvation comes here on earth. “as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace.”

That is why the prophets of God are “glorious in the eyes of the Lord.” There is no higher calling than being a prophet of the Most High God, once he has revealed his son in you at the appointed time. Some of us used to be athletes, and once Christ was awakened in us we let all that go. None of it compares to what we do now in these last days as watchmen of Israel. This is the true glory, glorious not to man but to God, and our God is our strength to raise up the tribes of Jacob.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 1:21
precepts.why:
Romans 10 asks, how shall they hear except they be sent? We have been sent to the four corners of the earth, sent from the beginning to be saviours, to “raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel.” And Paul shows the way God chose to do it: “For after that in the wisdom of God the world by wisdom knew not God, it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe.”

Our people may see what we do as foolishness. Someone may say, I’ve just been called to do this to fold. No. God says it pleased him by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe.

That is our purpose. Preach God’s word. To be sent to preach God’s word, to save the believers, to save the elect. That is our goal and our mission, and you have to take pride in it.

So when Isaiah says the servant shall be “my salvation unto the end of the earth”, this is how: not by the wisdom of the world, which never knew God, but by the preaching of the prophets whom God formed from the womb and sent. Standing on the corner looking like a fool preaching his word is exactly what pleases him, and it is how Jacob is brought again to him.

The Bible says sin is the transgression of the law, the breaking and violating of God's laws. So was Christ wrong? Peter answers: “Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps: Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth.” He did no wrong at all.

Yet a pastor will get up and speak against Christ, and you never hear him speak against Babylon, America, never against homosexuality, never against the idolatrous festivals out here. That is the blind watchman, the dumb dog that cannot bark. So the prophets have to go out and proclaim among the Gentiles, “Prepare war”, and our own people need to know war is coming too.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 7:7

precepts.label: Leviticus 25:45-46
precepts.why:
Isaiah 60 is the true third temple. Solomon built the first; Zerubbabel and Joshua rebuilt the second during the Persian captivity; and here is the third. “And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls”. The third temple is built by the other nations, because the other nations will be our slaves. That makes some nervous, but that is what it says.

Here is the law behind it, for anyone struggling: “Moreover of the children of the strangers that do sojourn among you, of them shall ye buy, and of their families that are with you, which they begat in your land: and they shall be your possession.” Those are the same strangers Isaiah speaks of in verse 10. We shall own them, possess them as slaves.

“And ye shall take them as an inheritance for your children after you, to inherit them for a possession; they shall be your bondmen for ever”. For how long? For ever. Then: “but over your brethren the children of Israel, ye shall not rule one over another with rigour”.

So when Isaiah says “their kings shall minister unto thee”, it is that law being carried out in the kingdom. God was angry with us and smote us, and we went into slavery: “in my wrath I smote thee”. Then: “but in my favour have I had mercy on thee”: that is why he sent Christ. Now the order is turned back to what the law always said: the strangers serve, and Israel is not ruled with rigour.

precepts.label: Isaiah 14:1-3
precepts.why:
What about the strangers? Are they going to be in the kingdom? Yes, but read how. “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land”. He is not having mercy on everybody on the planet. He said Jacob: the twelve tribes of Israel. That's us. He will set them in their own land: not the League of Nations, not the UN.

Then: “and the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob”: joined to obey us. “And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place”. All nations will be put where they rightfully belong. The Arabs in North Africa are not supposed to be there; that belongs to Ham, and they will be moved out. The white man in Australia does not belong there, and the white man in South Africa will be removed out of that land.

Then: “and the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids: and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors”. That is the law of Leviticus 25 just read: the laws will be re-implemented.

“And it shall come to pass in the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve”. That is why Christ said come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. People say rest from sin; not just sin. Slavery is the result of sin, and oppression is the result of sin. That is the rest Christ was talking about.

Back in Isaiah 60, that is why “the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls”: we will possess them, as servants and handmaids. The Bible does not contradict itself; Christianity contradicts the Bible.

precepts.label: Revelation 20:4
precepts.why:
Still on the third temple: “And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them”. Power was given unto them.

Then: “and I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God”: the martyred. Then: “and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands”: the mark of sin, that lets you know it is somebody in these last days, who would not support the beast.

Then: “and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years”. Notice the top of it: thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them. This is the third temple being built up. We are going to reign with Christ for a thousand years.

That is why Isaiah 60 ends with the ones who afflicted us bowing: “all they that despised thee shall bow themselves down at the soles of thy feet; and they shall call thee, The city of the Lord, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel.” It is the same thing Revelation 3:9 said. The third temple is under Christ, not what the Christians make of Daniel 9.

precepts.label: Revelation 21:24-27
precepts.why:
“And the nations of them which are saved shall walk in the light of it: and the kings of the earth do bring their glory and honour into it.” Saved here does not mean what people get confused about. It means left over: “every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem”. Those that are left walk in the light of it: they obey the commandments, and come up to worship the King of kings and keep the feast of tabernacles.

“And the gates of it shall not be shut at all by day: for there shall be no night there.” That is the third temple, the same gates of Isaiah 60: “thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles, and that their kings may be brought.” Forces means wealth, and their kings are brought in chains. “For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish”.

“And they shall bring the glory and honour of the nations into it. And there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth, neither whatsoever worketh abomination, or maketh a lie: but they which are written in the Lamb’s book of life.” So the nations themselves are not walking in. They are bringing their glory and honour up to the men of God at the gates. Those written in the Lamb's book of life are the Israelites. Only the Israelites get in.

precepts.label: Zechariah 14:16
precepts.why:
When Revelation says “the nations of them which are saved”, Zechariah gives the thought: “And it shall come to pass, that every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.”

Everyone that is left. Christ is not killing everybody. There are going to be remnants of people left over from the nations that came against Jerusalem. Those are the “saved” of Revelation 21: the ones left.

And what they do is go up every year to worship the King and keep the feast of tabernacles. That is walking in the light of it: obeying the commandments. That is how the nations serve in Isaiah 60, bringing their wealth and their kings to the gates while Israel is inside. “For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.”

precepts.label: 2 Thessalonians 2:4
precepts.why:
If they want to use any scripture about a third temple, this is where you go. If they build that temple, this is what we are going to use: “Who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God, or that is worshipped; so that he as God sitteth in the temple of God, shewing himself that he is God.”

Who is that? The white man, who opposes everything the Bible says. Before 70 AD, before they destroyed it, Rome entered our temple and sat their rusty butt down. And after Titus destroyed Jerusalem, Rome built Aelia Capitolina on its ruins, named for the emperor Hadrian, whose clan name was Aelius, and for Jupiter, Juno and Minerva: that is the trinity, where Christianity got that doctrine. A sanctuary to Jupiter, that is Zeus, the devil, was built on the Temple Mount, statues of Roman gods were set up in intentional violation of Old Testament law, and the real Jews were forbidden the city. The walls of the old city today follow the Roman walls: the wailing wall they hump on nowadays.

Now they are trying to build on the Temple Mount again. If the Lord allows them to be successful, one will sit there saying I am God, and everybody will cheer. No. That is the man Paul warned of.

The true third temple is the one in Isaiah 60, under Christ: the strangers build its walls, the nations bring their wealth to its gates, and those who despised us bow at the soles of our feet and call it “The city of the Lord, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel.”

precepts.label: Job 19:19
precepts.why:
“Take ye heed every one of his neighbour, and trust ye not in any brother: for every brother will utterly supplant, and every neighbour will walk with slanders.” To supplant is to betray, to plot. Job knew what it is to be betrayed by those closest to him: “All my inward friends abhorred me: and they whom I loved are turned against me.”

Those were our people, the northern kingdom, and they handed him over. And Esau planned it for more than a year, studying who could be turned: one with a sick daughter, one bitter that others were promoted over him, one disillusioned.

The same spirit is among us. Other Israelite camps want to destroy IUIC by slandering the members and the leadership, because black people will believe anything without proof. They slander the Bishop, the deacons and the captains every chance they get, and then come to the door asking to fellowship. We are good. We don't believe the same thing, and we will never come together with them.

And inside: the brother who says, why is he a captain, I know more scripture than him, why do the young men always travel with the Bishop? Maybe the young men are thirstier for the word than you. They know they don't know everything; you think you know it all. Fix that spirit, or you will be the next traitor, the inward friend turned against those who loved him. God hates a traitor.
