thread.label: Jeremiah 25:15-16
thread.text: For thus saith the Lord God of Israel unto me; Take the wine cup of this fury at my hand, and cause all the nations, to whom I send thee, to drink it.

thread.label: Jeremiah 28:8
thread.text: The prophets that have been before me and before thee of old prophesied both against many countries, and against great kingdoms, of war, and of evil, and of pestilence.

classes.title: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.label: Isaiah 34:16
precepts.why:
Jeremiah says the prophets of old “prophesied both against many countries, and against great kingdoms, of war, and of evil, and of pestilence.” All the prophets made sure to speak of these things. It is bad news for everybody else but good news for Israel, because when we see these signs we see the time hastening for the Lord's people, his heritage. They are not uncertain; they are an assurance and an establishment of our faith. This is not a time to prophesy peace in the earth. The peace is among us: the middle wall of partition broken down between the northern and southern kingdom, no more alienation from Christ, his laws and our identity.

Isaiah tells us where to see it: “Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read: no one of these shall fail, none shall want her mate”. We must read and understand so we can see these things. Too many of our people, even those repenting, are caught up in other things and do not think what is happening warrants their attention. Go back and read your scriptures more. The warnings and the shortening of days are there to put a fire under us so we seek out our own salvation with fear and trembling.

No other book gives this understanding. It has survived countless attempts to burn, destroy and alter it, and Christianity minimizes it to a book of love, hugs and kisses. That is a slap in the face, because most of the book is doom, destruction, war, judgment and recompense, and the people waiting on prophecy are always the oppressed.

“for my mouth it hath commanded, and his spirit it hath gathered them.” Christ's spirit gathered these things together so they would be plain to those who keep the commandments and be preserved for us to use in these last days. None of the prophecies of war, evil and pestilence will fail.

thread.label: Jeremiah 28:8-9
thread.text: The prophets that have been before me and before thee of old prophesied both against many countries, and against great kingdoms, of war, and of evil, and of pestilence.

thread.label: Jeremiah 30:1-7
thread.text: The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying,

precepts.label: Joel 3:1
precepts.why:
“Write thee all the words that I have spoken unto thee in a book.” That book is called the Bible today. Then pay attention: “For, lo, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will bring again the captivity of my people Israel and Judah”.

Joel 3:1 confuses some brothers: “For, behold, in those days, and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem”. Read that alone and you think it means he is bringing us back into slavery. That is not what it means.

Go back to Jeremiah 30:3. Notice the same words, except Jeremiah explains them: “and I will cause them to return to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they shall possess it.” When he says he will bring again the captivity, he is speaking of bringing us back from captivity, not into captivity. Jeremiah explains Joel.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 9:2-3
precepts.why:
“We have heard a voice of trembling, of fear, and not of peace.” We are coming up on that moment now. And yet our people cheer the movies on Martin Luther King and Malcolm X. You may not agree with Martin's method, but how many of us would walk down the street knowing we would be beaten, jailed and have dogs sicced on us? Their stand ended Jim Crow, and in sixty years of that liberty, how have we used it? We shoot each other, besmirch one another and hate each other.

Jeremiah said, “Oh that I had in the wilderness a lodging place of wayfaring men; that I might leave my people, and go from them!” He wanted to leave black people. Why? “for they be all adulterers, an assembly of treacherous men. And they bend their tongues like their bow for lies”. Black people love to use their lips for lies.

“but they are not valiant for the truth upon the earth”. They are valiant in the movie theatre. They cheer on Nat Turner in Birth of a Nation, cheer on Malcolm X and Martin Luther King, cheer the resistance in The Hunger Games and Star Wars, but they do not have that spirit and do not have the balls to do what those men did. They would never have joined Malcolm or Martin, and many will not join us out of fear. Two young boys got shot in the face in Georgia, instigated by a gaggle of other black men who scattered like cockroaches and played innocent when the cops came. So-called revolutionary brothers on podcasts call us a cult while including homosexuality and transgenderism; they have never left the couch.

“for they proceed from evil to evil, and they know not me, saith the Lord.” That is why, in the time of Jacob's trouble, there is a voice of trembling and fear and not of peace.

precepts.label: Matthew 10:22-23
precepts.why:
“Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it: it is even the time of Jacob’s trouble; but he shall be saved out of it.” That is the great tribulation. Jeremiah does not go into much detail on how he is saved out of it, so Christ fills it in.

“And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.” Christ prophesied we would be hated of all men for his sake, so we have to endure the hatred. Brothers and sisters on TikTok, YouTube and Instagram ask why the white man hates us so much. Because we are the sons and daughters of God, the people of Christ.

“But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another”. So when you brothers go to these other countries, check out the real estate, find out whether you can get citizenship or residency, question and research, because if something pops off here we have to be able to move. One city may pop off and the next city may not have the same persecution.

“for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come.” We will not have reached all the twelve tribes before Christ comes; we are not going to reach every Israelite. Christ says the same in Matthew 24: they shall deliver you up to be afflicted and kill you, many shall be offended and betray one another, but he that endures unto the end, either your death or Christ's return, shall be saved.

precepts.label: Isaiah 66:19-21
precepts.why:
How do we know we will not reach all the Israelites everywhere before Christ comes? Isaiah shows the rest are gathered after: “And I will set a sign among them, and I will send those that escape of them unto the nations”. Those that escape are the 144,000.

They are sent “to Tarshish”, Spain, “Pul”, Libya, “and Lud”, Lydia, “that draw the bow, to Tubal”, Turkey, “and Javan”, Greece, “to the isles afar off”, like the Melanesian isles. When we went to Papua New Guinea and looked at the map, there are thousands of islands there. These are places “that have not heard my fame, neither have seen my glory”: they have not heard the gospel. “and they shall declare my glory among the Gentiles.” The 144,000 collect the Israelites that are in these other nations.

“And they shall bring all your brethren for an offering unto the Lord out of all nations upon horses, and in chariots, and in litters, and upon mules, and upon swift beasts, to my holy mountain Jerusalem”. The kingdom is already set up at this time, and the third temple is built.

“And I will also take of them for priests and for Levites, saith the Lord.” The brothers and sisters gathered from among those nations, the Lord will make those men priests and Levites. That is how Jacob is saved out of his trouble and all Israel is brought again to the land.

thread.label: Jeremiah 30:5-7
thread.text: For thus saith the Lord; We have heard a voice of trembling, of fear, and not of peace.

thread.label: Jeremiah 30:7
thread.text: Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it: it is even the time of Jacob’s trouble; but he shall be saved out of it.

thread.label: Jeremiah 30:8-11
thread.text: For it shall come to pass in that day, saith the Lord of hosts, that I will break his yoke from off thy neck, and will burst thy bonds, and strangers shall no more serve themselves of him:

precepts.label: Hosea 3:4-5
precepts.why:
“In that day”, “I will break his yoke from off thy neck, and will burst thy bonds, and strangers shall no more serve themselves of him”: that's Christ's return. “But they shall serve the Lord their God, and David their king, whom I will raise up unto them.” Uh-oh. Did you notice? David is alive.

Hosea says the same: “For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod, and without teraphim”. Many days without a king. “Afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek the Lord their God, and David their king; and shall fear the Lord and his goodness in the latter days.”

We are returning now. We are seeking the Lord our God. And it is telling you David is going to be alive in these last days, in the latter days, when Israel returns. That is the day of Jeremiah 30, when the yoke is broken off our neck and the Lord raises David up unto us.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 1:11
precepts.why:
If David is alive in these last days, “David their king, whom I will raise up unto them”, why doesn't anyone know it? Solomon says: “There is no remembrance of former things; neither shall there be any remembrance of things that are to come with those that shall come after.”

David will not remember who he is, and neither do you. Our minds are wiped, everybody. We don't know who's who. That is why it says love your neighbour as you love yourself: you don't know who is who.

And that is a good thing. In the old school we used to say, oh, this one's David, and that caused a lot of partiality and a lot of problems. Don't do that. Don't try to guess who anybody is either. Little brother calling himself Samson: you don't know, brother. Just stop it. The Lord will raise up David; it is not ours to name him.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 34:23
precepts.why:
Jeremiah says Israel “shall serve the Lord their God, and David their king, whom I will raise up unto them.” Ezekiel says the same of the last days: “And I will set up one shepherd over them, and he shall feed them, even my servant David; he shall feed them, and he shall be their shepherd.”

One shepherd over the whole nation, and that shepherd is David. After Israel has abided many days without a king, the Lord himself sets David up over them, to feed them.

That is part of the promise that comes at the end of the exile and tribulation: the yoke broken from our neck, the strangers no longer serving themselves of us, Jacob returned to rest and quiet with none to make him afraid, and one shepherd, David, raised up over Israel under the Lord their God.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 9:22
precepts.why:
“though I make a full end of all nations whither I have scattered thee, yet will I not make a full end of thee”. Why is he going to make an end of all nations? Ezra says it: “Let the multitude perish then, which was born in vain”.

All these nations were born in vain. In a movie they are the extras; they're not the stars of the movie. We are. And Esau is the villain, the antagonist, the bad guy.

But the stars are not spared from correction: “I will correct thee in measure, and will not leave thee altogether unpunished.” The Lord makes a full end of the nations, but only corrects Israel in measure. So “fear thou not, O my servant Jacob”. What he says will happen would make anyone afraid, and nobody wants to go through tribulation, so we increase our faith by reminding ourselves that this body is just a shell; the real us is within. He will save us from afar, and Jacob shall return and be in rest, and none shall make him afraid.

thread.label: Jeremiah 30:12-17
thread.text: For thus saith the Lord, Thy bruise is incurable, and thy wound is grievous.

precepts.label: Isaiah 1:4-6
precepts.why:
“Thy bruise is incurable, and thy wound is grievous. There is none to plead thy cause, that thou mayest be bound up: thou hast no healing medicines.” None stands up on our behalf, and we have no healing medicine. Every Negro that just popped out of his mama's behind has a new idea for how to save black people, and it is always economics or voting. Those medicines don't work. What is the wound? Our sins. Isaiah says the same thing.

“Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters: they have forsaken the Lord, they have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward.” We are that sinful nation, a people laden with sin; iniquity is sin. He calls us a seed of evildoers.

“Why should ye be stricken any more? ye will revolt more and more”. Our people get punished and revolt more and more against God. Then: “the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint”: the whole head of the Israelites is sick.

“From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment.” Neither mollified with ointment means no medicine: there is no healing for us that way. That is Jeremiah's “no healing medicines.”

The only one who can save us is the Saviour, Jesus Christ, our master, our king. Yes, he is our rabbi, and rabbi means master. The wound Jeremiah calls incurable is incurable by any remedy of men; only the Lord can say, “I will restore health unto thee”.

precepts.label: Job 2:7
precepts.why:
What Isaiah and Jeremiah say of the nation is the same thing Job went through. People read Job and think that was only him, but Job's real life symbolizes the nation of Israel. This was the fifth judgment on Job: “So went Satan forth from the presence of the Lord, and smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown.” Didn't we just read that in Isaiah 1? “From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it”.

Job's life is Deuteronomy 28. He lost his businesses, his family, everything. And “There is none to plead thy cause”: Job had friends who would not stand up on his behalf. They were always telling him he was wrong, evil, the devil. There was no cure; God had to intervene and heal Job. That is why the Lord sent Christ to heal the twelve tribes of Israel.

Even Job's wife turned on him in his darkest moment, when he had lost everything. That is how these black women do with us: in this state, the black woman turned on us.

But at the end of Job's life he was blessed. That is what is going to happen to us if we endure to the end: the incurable wound of Jeremiah 30 ends with “I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds”.

precepts.label: Leviticus 26:41
precepts.why:
“I have wounded thee with the wound of an enemy, with the chastisement of a cruel one, for the multitude of thine iniquity; because thy sins were increased.” Our sins are increased: the Houston rodeo, black men and women whoring themselves out, filthy and wicked, so bad a dress code had to be put in place; and in Delta State in Nigeria, a festival where women are openly raped in the streets. That is evil. Then: “because thy sins were increased, I have done these things unto thee”.

Moses said it would be so: “And that I also have walked contrary unto them, and have brought them into the land of their enemies”. God walked contrary to us because we kept breaking his laws, and he brought us into the land of our enemies. Then what we must do: “if then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they then accept of the punishment of their iniquity”.

As we repent, we have to accept that God is right and we are wrong. We have always been wrong. God was just when he punished us. When your child plays in the street or with the light socket, you beat that behind, not because you hate him but so he learns he'll die playing in traffic or with electricity. Some talking doesn't do any good for some kids; you have to rile up on them so they know it's serious. That is what God did with us.

The three holy children did exactly this. In the midst of the fiery furnace, cast in because they would not worship Babylon's god, Azarias prayed: “Blessed art thou, O Lord God of our fathers”, “For thou art righteous in all the things that thou hast done to us: yea, true are all thy works, thy ways are right, and all thy judgments truth.” Then: “for according to truth and judgment didst thou bring all these things upon us because of our sins. For we have sinned and committed iniquity, departing from thee”. Everything God has done to our people is justified, because we revolted against him. They said it because of what Moses said in Leviticus, and what happened to them is a reflection of what will happen to us.

Christianity has taught our people the opposite: to mock a God who got angry at his own people for worshipping a golden calf. But accepting the punishment is the way back, because the next verse is: “Then will I remember my covenant with Jacob”.

precepts.label: Luke 9:11
precepts.why:
“For I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds, saith the Lord”. The Lord is the only one who can restore health; that goes back to verses 12 and 13, “thou hast no healing medicines.” There is no magic voting right and no economic situation to save us.

Luke shows who the healer is: “And the people, when they knew it, followed him: and he received them, and spake unto them of the kingdom of God, and healed them that had need of healing.” Christ spake of the kingdom and healed them that had need of healing. He is the only one who can heal us of all these things. He is the Saviour; he is the physician.

That is how the incurable bruise of Jeremiah 30 is cured. Not by any medicine of man, but by the Lord who received the people, taught them the kingdom of God, and healed them.

precepts.label: Mark 2:17
precepts.why:
Christ is the physician: “When Jesus heard it, he saith unto them, They that are whole have no need of the physician, but they that are sick”. If you think you're good, that you know everything, you don't need the son of God, you don't need the Saviour.

You have to admit you're sick: that we are in the midst of sin, and that all we have done has been wrong. That is the same thing as accepting the punishment of our iniquity.

“I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.” He did not call us righteous. He came for sinners. That is the healing Jeremiah promises Israel, whose “sorrow is incurable for the multitude of thine iniquity”. The sick nation is the one he came to heal.

The churches are the opposite: they say they don't need that Bible, they are already whole. Isaiah 65 shows them saying so, “I am holier than thou.” The ones who think themselves whole will not come to the physician.

precepts.label: Isaiah 65:1-5
precepts.why:
This goes with Christ saying he came not for the righteous but for sinners. “I am sought of them that asked not for me; I am found of them that sought me not”. Like the disciples, we didn't wake up one day as kids searching for the Lord of heaven and earth. The word was introduced to us and woke us up.

“I said, Behold me, behold me, unto a nation that was not called by my name.” We are called African-Americans, Haitians, Jamaicans, Puerto Ricans. That is a nation not called by his name.

“I have spread out my hands all the day unto a rebellious people, which walketh in a way that was not good, after their own thoughts”. We are that rebellious people, walking in Christianity and Islam, our people following their own thoughts in these religions. “A people that provoketh me to anger continually to my face; that sacrificeth in gardens, and burneth incense upon altars of brick”: the churches and mosques. Then: “which eat swine’s flesh, and broth of abominable things is in their vessels”. You know that's the church: there was always a swine fest at the end, pig feet and all of that; possum soup, turtle soup.

“Which say, Stand by thyself, come not near to me; for I am holier than thou.” That is what the churches say to the Israelites on the street preaching: stand by yourself, I don't need no black Jesus, I'm washed in the blood of Jesus, I'm water baptized, I'm holier than thou. “These are a smoke in my nose, a fire that burneth all the day.” God can't stand them.

That is the people Jeremiah calls an Outcast, “This is Zion, whom no man seeketh after.” Those who think they are whole push away the physician; the sick who admit it are the ones he heals.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 2:24
precepts.why:
How does the Lord restore health unto us? “Who his own self bare our sins in his own body on the tree, that we, being dead to sins, should live unto righteousness: by whose stripes ye were healed.”

Christ bare our sins in his own body on the tree, which is the cross; the cross was made from a tree. We, being dead to sin, should live unto righteousness. We are healed by Christ's punishment, his crucifixion.

That is the prophecy of Jeremiah 30:17: “For I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds, saith the Lord”. How? When he sent Christ to die on the cross. By his stripes we are healed.

Then: “because they called thee an Outcast, saying, This is Zion, whom no man seeketh after”. Outcast means African-American: made-up names they gave our race. Nobody gives a damn about you, blacks and Latinos; no man seeks after you. But the Lord does. The wound no medicine could close is healed by his stripes, and then “all they that devour thee shall be devoured; and all thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity”: every one of them, not some.

thread.label: Jeremiah 30:18-24
thread.text: Thus saith the Lord; Behold, I will bring again the captivity of Jacob’s tents, and have mercy on his dwellingplaces; and the city shall be builded upon her own heap, and the palace shall remain after the manner thereof.

precepts.label: Numbers 1:52
precepts.why:
Just before this, the Lord says, “I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds”, and that healing came when he sent Christ to die on the cross: by his stripes we are healed. “because they called thee an Outcast”: outcast means African-American, made-up names for our race, a Zion “whom no man seeketh after”. Nobody gives a damn about blacks and Latinos. Then: “Behold, I will bring again the captivity of Jacob’s tents”.

What are Jacob’s tents? “And the children of Israel shall pitch their tents, every man by his own camp, and every man by his own standard, throughout their hosts.” Every man by his own camp: Judah is going to be with Judah, Ephraim with Ephraim, Benjamin with Benjamin. That is the restructuring, the restoration of a nation.

And every man by his own standard: Judah had the standard of the lion, Benjamin the wolf, Naphtali the deer, Ephraim the bull. When the Lord brings again the captivity of Jacob’s tents, all of this is being restored again: the tribes set back in order, each under its own standard.

precepts.label: Numbers 24:5
precepts.why:
All of this is being restored again: “How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, and thy tabernacles, O Israel!”

The tents of Jacob, pitched every man by his own camp and his own standard, are goodly in the eyes of the Lord. These are the same tents Jeremiah speaks of when the Lord says, “I will bring again the captivity of Jacob’s tents, and have mercy on his dwellingplaces”.

So the promise of Jeremiah 30:18 is that the goodly order Israel had in the wilderness, the tribes camped in their tents, is brought back out of captivity. What was taken captive, the Lord returns, and Jacob’s tents are goodly again.

precepts.label: Psalms 78:55
precepts.why:
“He cast out the heathen also before them, and divided them an inheritance by line, and made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tents.” He cast out the heathen before us, divided the land to the tribes by line, and set each tribe in its tents.

That is what it means for the Lord to bring again the captivity of Jacob’s tents. The tents of Jacob are the tribes of Israel dwelling in their own inheritance, and to bring them again is to cast out the heathen once more and set the twelve tribes back in their inheritance.

Then Jeremiah goes on: “and the city shall be builded upon her own heap”, because that land is going to be destroyed and built again, and the tribes dwell in it again as the Lord made them to dwell at the first.

precepts.label: Isaiah 60:10-13
precepts.why:
“the city shall be builded upon her own heap, and the palace shall remain after the manner thereof.” It says heap because that land is going to be destroyed and built again; the palace means the temple that is going to be built. Isaiah 60 goes with Jeremiah 30:18.

“And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls, and their kings shall minister unto thee: for in my wrath I smote thee, but in my favour have I had mercy on thee.” The strangers build the walls when Jerusalem is built again on her own heap.

“The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary”. That is the palace. “and I will make the place of my feet glorious”: the Lord is going to make Jerusalem glorious again.

precepts.label: Isaiah 60:21-22
precepts.why:
Jeremiah says, “I will multiply them, and they shall not be few; I will also glorify them, and they shall not be small.” That is why we go to Isaiah 60.

“Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified.” Then: “A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation: I the Lord will hasten it in his time.” We shall not be small.

There is more in that verse than what it is saying on the surface. Look at the little bodies we have now. We are not going to have these little bodies. We are not going to be all frail and skinny, and the little fat brothers are not going to be like that either. The Lord multiplies and glorifies Israel, in number and in body.

precepts.label: Isaiah 1:25-26
precepts.why:
“Their children also shall be as aforetime, and their congregation shall be established before me”. The Lord is going to return it all back to the way it was.

Isaiah says the same: “And I will turn my hand upon thee, and purely purge away thy dross, and take away all thy tin:” “And I will restore thy judges as at the first”. He purges the dross out of Israel and restores the judges as at the first, the way it was in the beginning.

That is what Jeremiah 30:20 is saying: our children as aforetime, our congregation established before the Lord, everything returned to our glorious state. And it answers verse 21 too, “their nobles shall be of themselves”: our own judges, restored as at the first.

precepts.label: Zechariah 12:7-8
precepts.why:
“The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.” These are the same tents of Jacob that the Lord brings again out of captivity.

“In that day shall the Lord defend the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and he that is feeble among them at that day shall be as David”. The feeble Israelites are going to be like King David. “and the house of David shall be as God, as the angel of the Lord before them.” The house of David is the 144,000; they shall be as God.

That is our children being as aforetime and our glorious state being restored: the Lord saving Judah’s tents first, and the weakest of Israel made as strong as David.

precepts.label: Psalms 72:4
precepts.why:
At the bottom of Jeremiah 30:20 the Lord says, “I will punish all that oppress them.” He said all, not some. All that have oppressed us shall be punished.

The precept is Psalms 72: “He shall judge the poor of the people, he shall save the children of the needy, and shall break in pieces the oppressor.” Break in pieces the oppressor.

There is no coming together and joining with the oppressor. The Lord did not say he would reconcile Israel with the ones who oppressed them; he said, I am going to break them. That is the punishment of all that oppress us.

precepts.label: Matthew 2:6
precepts.why:
“And their nobles shall be of themselves, and their governor shall proceed from the midst of them”. Our nobles are going to come from our own people. We are not going to have nobles of another race, like the mayor they have now in New York, Mamdani. That is not our people.

Christ is our governor, and he came from the midst of us: “And thou Bethlehem, in the land of Juda, art not the least among the princes of Juda: for out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel.” That is Christ right there.

So the governor that proceeds from the midst of Israel is Christ, born in Bethlehem of Judah, ruling his people Israel. “I will cause him to draw near, and he shall approach unto me”, and then, “ye shall be my people, and I will be your God.”

thread.label: Jeremiah 47:1-7
thread.text: The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah the prophet against the Philistines, before that Pharaoh smote Gaza.

classes.title: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.label: Psalms 17:13-14
precepts.why:
Jeremiah cries, “O thou sword of the Lord, how long will it be ere thou be quiet?” What is the sword of the Lord? David shows it: “Arise, O Lord, disappoint him, cast him down: deliver my soul from the wicked, which is thy sword: From men which are thy hand, O Lord, from men of the world, which have their portion in this life, and whose belly thou fillest with thy hid treasure”.

“Therefore rejoice, ye heavens, and ye that dwell in them.” That is not the sky; the sky doesn't go woo. It is men living in dominion, in rulership: Edom today, America, Germany, France, Great Britain, Australia, Canada. Those are the heavens, and those that dwell in them.

Who is in the heaven that is going to rejoice? Isaiah 34:5: “For my sword shall be bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea, and upon the people of my curse, to judgment.”

Christ's sword shall be bathed in heaven and come down upon heaven. Look up Idumea: pertaining to Edom, the Greek and Roman name for Edom. That is what the heavens are. Edom today is America, Germany, France, Great Britain, Australia, Canada.

Don't let anybody tell you Edom was already destroyed. If he were, then who is Christ coming back to kill here in Isaiah 34? The people of his curse are still standing in the heavens, and that is why Daniel's king of fierce countenance “shall be broken without hand” in the last kingdom.

precepts.label: Revelation 13:2-7
precepts.why:

Revelation 13: “And the beast which I saw was like unto a leopard”, like the Greeks, “and his feet were as the feet of a bear”, like the Medes and Persians, “and his mouth as the mouth of a lion”, similar to Babylon, “and the dragon gave him his power, and his seat, and great authority.”

Daniel says the king of fierce countenance “shall destroy the mighty and the holy people.” Haven't we been destroyed? We have been destroyed as a people. Watch the wording of Deuteronomy 28:48.

“and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” Here is the part we want: until he have destroyed us. The yokes of iron have been taken off. What does that prove? That we have been destroyed, exactly what Daniel 8:24 says.

And Daniel goes on: “by peace shall destroy many.” Donald Trump calls himself the president of peace and set up a board of peace, yet he has bombed Yemen, Somalia, Iraq, Iran, Syria, Nigeria and Venezuela. We are living in that time right now.

precepts.label: Numbers 14:34
precepts.why:
Edom twists Daniel 9, so here is the code to break it down. Write it down: each day represents one year, each week represents seven years, and seventy weeks is 490 years. How do we know? Start with why Israel spent forty years in the wilderness.

“After the number of the days in which ye searched the land, even forty days, each day for a year, shall ye bear your iniquities, even forty years”. The spies searched the land forty days. Because Israel sinned, they bore their iniquity forty years in the wilderness, a year for every day. “and ye shall know my breach of promise”: the Lord told them not to go up there, and they went up anyway.

That is the Lord himself counting a day for a year. So when Daniel is told “Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city”, those weeks are counted the same way: seventy weeks of seven days, every day a year, 490 years.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 4:6
precepts.why:
The Lord gives the same count a second time, to Ezekiel: “thou shalt bear the iniquity of the house of Judah forty days: I have appointed thee each day for a year.” Each day for a year. With Numbers 14 that is two witnesses to the code: a day in prophecy is a year.

Now Daniel 9 opens up. “Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people”: seventy weeks equals 490 years. “from the going forth of the commandment to restore and to build Jerusalem unto the Messiah the Prince shall be seven weeks, and threescore and two weeks”: seven weeks plus sixty-two weeks is sixty-nine weeks, 483 years. That commandment started with Cyrus, when God told the Persians to let his people go to rebuild; Israel was hindered two years, then came Darius and Artaxerxes, and the building went on under Zerubbabel, Joshua, Ezra and Nehemiah, with Haggai and Zechariah. “the street shall be built again, and the wall, even in troublous times”: our forefathers caught hell from the nations and built with a sword in one hand and a brick in the other.

“after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself”: Christ crucified, not dying for himself but for the twelve tribes of Israel. “the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary”: Rome, in 70 AD. Then the last week: “he shall confirm the covenant with many for one week: and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease”, and “for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate”, the abomination in the temple Christ warned about.

The total of seventy weeks has been fulfilled. Amalek tells Christians that last week has not happened yet and belongs to a rebuilt temple today, counting on blacks and Latinos not understanding the scriptures and going along with whatever they say because they are white. Counted a day for a year, the way the Lord counts it, all seventy weeks are done.

precepts.label: Acts 10:38
precepts.why:
Seventy weeks are determined “to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.” To make an end of sins is Christ coming to die, and the reconciliation for iniquity is all through Christ.

And who is the most Holy that is anointed? “How God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Ghost and with power: who went about doing good, and healing all that were oppressed of the devil; for God was with him.” Christ is the anointed one.

So the bottom of Daniel 9:24, “to anoint the most Holy”, is Christ, anointed as the most Holy. That is why the seventy weeks run unto “the Messiah the Prince”: the whole prophecy is counted to him and fulfilled in him.

precepts.label: 1 Maccabees 3:48
precepts.why:
The robbers of thy people did not start with the Herodians. When the Greeks started to conquer us, look what they did: “And laid open the book of the law, wherein the heathen had sought to paint the likeness of their images.”

The book of the law is the Bible. Daniel wrote during the time of Babylon; after that came the Persians and the Medes, and then the Greeks. Even from the time of the Greeks the heathen started to paint their images in our book and say that they are Moses, they are Joshua, they are Samson.

That is the same spirit as Daniel 11:14: “the robbers of thy people shall exalt themselves to establish the vision”. First they painted themselves into our book as our fathers. Then the Herodians, Herod and Agrippa, robbed our culture and our heritage and became Jews in the time of Christ. And in 1948 they got the land again, set up schools throughout Israel and taught a new form of Hebrew, a Hebrew that was extinct from 70 AD and made up by fusing French, Arabic, Aramaic, Spanish and German words, which Negroes argue about today. They got the land, made up a new language, and called themselves Jewish. But the prophecy says, “they shall fall.”

precepts.label: Job 9:24
precepts.why:

“he covereth the faces of the judges thereof”. The judges are God, Christ, the angels, and the Israelites, the Jews. He covers all their faces with his own: he puts his images everywhere as the people of God. “if not, where, and who is he?”

That is how the robbers of thy people exalt themselves to establish the vision. They are the ones ruling the earth, so they cover the faces of God's people with their own and put themselves in the place of the Jews, the same way they painted their likeness into the book of the law. And Daniel says of them, “but they shall fall.”

precepts.label: Job 24:15
precepts.why:
This one is rarely read, but it says the same thing as Job 9:24. “The eye also of the adulterer”: that is this white man; he is the adulterer. He rapes and robs and pillages women. That's what they do.

“waiteth for the twilight, saying, No eye shall see me: and disguiseth his face.” He disguises his face as the Jews. He disguises his face as Jesus. He disguises his face as the angels. And everybody goes, no, nobody could believe that this man did all this.

So the robbers of thy people in Daniel 11:14 establish the vision in disguise. They exalt themselves as the Jews wearing a face that is not theirs, thinking no eye shall see them, and that is why the world cannot believe what they have done.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 35:12-15
precepts.why:
Here God shows what those robbers said when they took the land. “I have heard all thy blasphemies which thou hast spoken against the mountains of Israel, saying, They are laid desolate, they are given us to consume.” They said, the real Jews are gone, the Israelites are finished, the land is ours now. “Thus with your mouth ye have boasted against me, and have multiplied your words against me: I have heard them.” God said, I have heard them.

“When the whole earth rejoiceth, I will make thee desolate.” That is when they shall say peace and safety. “As thou didst rejoice at the inheritance of the house of Israel, because it was desolate”: they rejoiced over the land because the twelve tribes were gone and put in captivity. “so will I do unto thee: thou shalt be desolate, O mount Seir, and all Idumea, even all of it”.

Idumea is the Greek and Roman name for Edom. It does not say some of Idumea; it says all Idumea, even all of it. That is who the robbers of thy people are: Edom, which is Amalek over there, set themselves up as the Jews. Their plan is to make believe Iran shot a missile and blew up the Al-Aqsa Mosque so they can rebuild the third temple. But when the whole earth rejoices, God makes them desolate: “but they shall fall.”

precepts.label: Ezekiel 36:5
precepts.why:
“Surely in the fire of my jealousy have I spoken against the residue of the heathen, and against all Idumea, which have appointed my land into their possession”. This verse, along with Ezekiel 35:12, identifies the race that would live in the land. It doesn't say Japheth. There is no biblical text that says Japheth lives in the land. The Bible says Idumea would take and live in the land.

“with the joy of all their heart”: they were happy to steal, to spoil the land. “with despiteful minds”: they took the land despite knowing the land doesn't belong to them, despite the fact they're not the Jews.

“to cast it out for a prey”: they called their fellow Idumeans from Poland, Russia, Germany, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Ukraine and said, come, take a part, and a lot of them came. That is why, if you listen to them speak, they speak German, Polish and Russian with those accents. They are not the people of the land.

That is the vision the robbers of thy people exalt themselves to establish in Daniel 11:14, and God has spoken against all Idumea in the fire of his jealousy. They shall fall.

precepts.label: Daniel 9:27
precepts.why:
“the robbers of thy people shall exalt themselves to establish the vision”. Who are the robbers of God's people? Daniel 9:27 shows what they do: “And he shall confirm the covenant with many for one week: and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease”. This is what Antiochus did: he stopped us from sacrificing and serving God.

“and for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate”: he set up abomination and made our people desolate, meaning he destroyed our people, “even until the consummation”. That is why the Greeks, and the white man after them, are called the abomination of desolation, the abomination that maketh desolate. They are the robbers of God's people.

The Greeks wanted to conquer and take the land of Israel, and not only the land. First Maccabees 3 shows they took the book of the law and painted their likeness and their images in it, robbing us of our culture too. Judas Maccabeus rose up and fought against them.

And it is not only the Greeks. Christ said, “When ye therefore shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, stand in the holy place”. In the time of the Greeks the abomination was the Greeks; in the time of Christ it was the Romans; and Europe is an extension of Rome. In 1949 Europeans from Germany, Poland, Russia and Ukraine went into the holy land saying, we are the people of God. Today the abomination of desolation is those people in the land calling themselves Jews and they are not: the Europeans, the Edomites. Why are they called that? Because they destroy everything; ask the Palestinians.

When they stand in the holy place, “then shall be great tribulation, such as was not since the beginning of the world to this time, no, nor ever shall be.” They are the ones who will instigate it. But Daniel 11:14 ends, “but they shall fall.” The same way they fell back then is the same way they are going to fall today.

precepts.why:

precepts.label: 1 Kings 8:47
precepts.why:
Hosea says the children of Israel shall be “as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered”: dispersed, so that we could be preserved. And “in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” We are hearing that now and seeing it now. Our teachers tell us these things, we identify with them, and that is how we regain our identity.

Solomon’s prayer shows the steps: “Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness”.

First we have to bethink ourselves: remember ourselves and reclaim our identity, right here in the land of our captivity. That is part of the strangeness of our salvation. Then we repent and make supplication, and then God will acknowledge us, be for us and fight for us.

This is not a time of peace but a time of war. Not physical war: there is nothing we can do against these powers and nations physically. What we can do is unite as a people, come back together, keep God’s laws in solidarity, and wait on our Redeemer. In the place where we were called not his people, we remember who we are, we repent, and we are called the sons of the living God.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 1:21
precepts.why:
How do we bring about that change? How do you fight a nuke? How do you fight powers that can turn off your lights, run your economy and take your resources right under your nose while you say thank you? With something small and simple: “For after that in the wisdom of God the world by wisdom knew not God, it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe.”

It was God’s wisdom that the world would not know him, that they would purposely not be able to understand. It is given unto us to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God; he made everything a mystery so that only his elect can unseal what the Bible says. And just as it pleases him to see a man lifted up in power so that he can take him down, it pleases him to save by the foolishness of preaching. That is how we get our identity back. That is how we come back.

So look at the brothers in the streets. Don’t think those efforts are small; they are making an impact. Even if your camp doesn’t have a lot of foot traffic, none of it is in vain, none of it is void. You go out, you preach, you gather, you fish. Even if there are scarce fish in that water, if you know there is a spot where fish be, you stay there until you catch at least one. You are not trying to come home empty.

It starts with preaching and then it escalates. First we repent, then we get the honor. We do not fight physically now: we repent now, we fight through preaching, and God fights for us later. Then comes the honor of Psalm 149, “a twoedged sword in their hand; To execute vengeance upon the heathen”, for “this honour have all his saints.” When he shall roar, “the children shall tremble from the west”, the western hemisphere, “and I will place them in their houses, saith the Lord”: our tribes, our royal heritage and our identity given back to us, the sons of the living God.

precepts.label: 1 Esdras 8:69
precepts.why:
“Ephraim, he hath mixed himself among the people”, sometimes willingly, sometimes not. You have knuckleheads who say that is only talking about their customs. It was biological and it was symbolic, dummy. The Bible defines the Bible, and Ezra shows what mixing means: “The nation of Israel, the princes, the priests and Levites, have not put away from them the strange people of the land, nor the pollutions of the Gentiles.”

We did not put away the strange people from the land. We sought after them, because of the ideology of whitening, of bettering the race. The pollutions of the Gentiles are their idolatry and their doctrines, and we became corrupt in our merchandise and commerce. All Israel had that propensity, but here the focus is the northern kingdom.

Read on: “For both they and their sons have married with their daughters, and the holy seed is mixed with the strange people of the land.” When it says mixed himself among the people, it means the seed gets mixed. What is the seed? Sperm, semen. So when somebody comes to you with that BS, this is the scripture to put there: mixing means mixing.

It goes on: “and from the beginning of this matter the rulers and the great men have been partakers of this iniquity.” All of us partook of that, and it is a sin to mix with the other nations. That is why Ephraim is a cake not turned: light on one side and dark on the other, all the different shades among the northern kingdom, and some of our own people with blonde hair and blue eyes whose father is Israel.

precepts.label: Psalms 106:35
precepts.why:
“Ephraim, he hath mixed himself among the people.” Ezra already showed that the holy seed was mixed with the strange people of the land. David gives the other side of it: “But were mingled among the heathen, and learned their works.” It was not just ideological, dummies, and some of the ones saying it went to seminary school and call themselves theologians. When you look up the definition of mingled, it goes into mixing, just like First Esdras. And they learned their works too.

So Hosea is talking about ideology, and it is also talking about the seed, like we just proved. Scholars know the whitening was both ideological and biological. “Ephraim is a cake not turned. Strangers have devoured his strength.” The cake not turned is the colours, light and dark: some of us light, some in between, some dark.

The strangers devoured more than the strength of the royal seed. Our strength lies in the Lord, the joy of the Lord is our strength, and the ideology cut us away from him. We cannot fight the United States; our countries cannot do any of that. It is time we come back to God. Strangers devoured his strength, “and he knoweth it not: yea, gray hairs are here and there upon him, yet he knoweth not.” Many of our older people are not hearing it; the gray hairs are upon them and they cannot accept it.

And this goes with Matthew 13 and Amos 9, especially for you northern kingdom brothers. Southern kingdom, learn northern kingdom history with the same vigour and zeal that we learn yours. If you are a fisher of men, you fish all the different kinds of fish that pertain to Israel and Christ.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 12:9
precepts.why:
Ephraim mixed himself among the people and became “a cake not turned”, light and dark. Jeremiah shows how the Lord sees that mixed people: “Mine heritage is unto me as a speckled bird, the birds round about are against her; come ye, assemble all the beasts of the field, come to devour.”

We are a speckled bird, and the birds round about against her are the enemy. They know who we are because of the caste system. Though we are mixed, they know who we are. In Panama they call the light-skinned ones one name and the darker ones, some of whom are Benjamin, another, and the lady at the hotel sized each of us up by our shade the same way.

But the Lord had a way to fix that, because the Israelite seed is that strong: go back to the Israelite line, and it does not matter how mixed the daughter was. And Hosea says Ephraim would “bring forth his children to the murderer”: Cain, Esau, Edom, the Spaniards, the United States. For those who willingly tried to whiten the race: “give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts.” Many of those babies died.

So the speckled bird is still his heritage. “How shall I give thee up, Ephraim? how shall I deliver thee, Israel?” Though he struck us with these curses, he will not make us as Admah and Zeboim, the cities round about Sodom and Gomorrah that were utterly destroyed. Our job is to give the word, go to the chief places where our people resort, and let God do the separating.

thread.label: Hosea 9:13
thread.text: Ephraim, as I saw Tyrus, is planted in a pleasant place: but Ephraim shall bring forth his children to the murderer.

classes.title: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:45
precepts.why:
Ephraim was “planted in a pleasant place”, the blessings, but “Ephraim shall bring forth his children to the murderer.” The murderer is Cain, Esau, Edom: the Spaniards, the United States. That was the whitening, el blanqueamiento, sometimes done willingly and sometimes not. So God said “give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts.” Many of the babies of those who tried to whiten us out died, and what is left behind is largely not European; many who look European there came over later. Our job is to give the word, go to the chief places where our people resort as Christ taught, and let God do the separating.

How could a people fall so low, go through so much, and still rise and reconnect to their identity? People are baffled by it; to them it is ignorant and even offensive for us to know who we are. Deuteronomy 28:45 answers it: “Moreover all these curses shall come upon thee, and shall pursue thee, and overtake thee, till thou be destroyed; because thou hearkenedst not unto the voice of the Lord thy God.” And “they shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder, and upon thy seed for ever.”

Those curses became our identity, and our redemption. They are the way we acknowledge who we are and make our way back. If not these curses, then who is it? The Bible always said Israel would come back to its identity, and now that we are back, the world is bugging out. Where are the lost tribes? They are here now.

It is God's grand plan. If we were all together in one spot, they could have wiped us out. By dispersing us into the four corners of the earth he also preserved us, like the worm in the movie Swordfish, broken up and scattered to the four corners of the internet so no one could get it back without the one who hid it. What was our curse, God meant for good, so that now we can come back together. As Hosea said, the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, and “in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.”

thread.text: How shall I give thee up, Ephraim? how shall I deliver thee, Israel? how shall I make thee as Admah? how shall I set thee as Zeboim? mine heart is turned within me, my repentings are kindled together.

precepts.label: Zechariah 9:13
precepts.why:
“How shall I give thee up, Ephraim? how shall I deliver thee, Israel?” God is saying, how am I going to turn away from you, my son, and deliver you forever to the heathen? Admah and Zeboim were the cities round about Sodom and Gomorrah that were utterly destroyed, and he cannot do that to us. Though he strikes us with righteous judgment in these curses, he has not forgotten us. “I will not execute the fierceness of mine anger”: all the horror of these curses we deal with is mercy.

What comes after the repentance is the honor, and Zechariah shows it: “Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope”, that is, repent, and “even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee”. Then: “When I have bent Judah for me, filled the bow with Ephraim, and raised up thy sons, O Zion, against thy sons, O Greece, and made thee as the sword of a mighty man.”

This is talking about a weapon. Judah is bent first, like the bow, and then he fills the bow with Ephraim, like an arrow. It is the same order as Hosea 11:10: he roars like a lion because the tents of Judah are raised first, and the northern kingdom sees that example and follows it, and the children tremble from the west, from the western hemisphere. Thy sons, O Greece, goes into Edom, Esau, Cain, all these countries that rule with a fist of iron.

“And the Lord shall be seen over them, and his arrow shall go forth as the lightning”. That arrow is us. Christ leads the charge, and we get to move like that too, with the two-edged sword in our hand to execute vengeance upon the heathen, the honor all his saints have. “they shall drink, and make a noise as through wine; and they shall be filled like bowls, and as the corners of the altar”: we partake in the vengeance, like the blood of the sacrifice filling the bowls thrown on the altar. We don't just stand by and watch it.

So we don't fight physically now; we repent now and fight through preaching, and God fights for us later. He will place us in our houses, tell us, you're from Asher, you're from Ephraim, from Simeon, Issachar, Zebulun, Naphtali, and give us back our royal heritage and our identity.

thread.label: Joel 3:1-8
thread.text: For, behold, in those days, and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem,

precepts.label: Jeremiah 30:3
precepts.why:
Joel opens with “in those days, and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem”. Jeremiah shows what that means: “For, lo, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will bring again the captivity of my people Israel and Judah, saith the Lord: and I will cause them to return to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they shall possess it.”

To bring again the captivity is to bring us back to our homeland, the land given to our fathers, and to possess it. That is the evidence. Now we know what Joel 3:1 is saying.

And it ties the whole chapter together. The Most High gathers all nations into the valley of Jehoshaphat, in Israel, at the place called Har-Megiddo, where the name Armageddon comes from, to plead with them for his people and his heritage Israel, whom they scattered among the nations while they parted his land between the Arabs and the Edomites.

Joel ends the same way it begins: “Behold, I will raise them out of the place whither ye have sold them”. The Most High raises up the Israelites out of the places they were sold into, back to verse 1, and brings us home to our land in freedom.

precepts.label: Amos 1:9-10
precepts.why:
Joel asks, “what have ye to do with me, O Tyre, and Zidon, and all the coasts of Palestine?” and charges them: “The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Grecians”. Amos says the same of Tyre: “For three transgressions of Tyrus, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they delivered up the whole captivity to Edom, and remembered not the brotherly covenant”.

The same people delivered us to Edom, whom Joel calls the Grecians: the white man. Tyre and Zidon were the Hamite nations of Canaan back then, and the coasts of Palestine, the ancient Philistines, is the modern name for the modern people there, the Arabs. They cast lots for our people, bid on us the way it is still done in the Arab countries, gave a boy for an harlot, making the men into breeders, and sold a girl for wine. They took our silver and gold and robbed our temples.

“But I will send a fire on the wall of Tyrus, which shall devour the palaces thereof.” The wall of Tyrus is the land, and you see that land catching hell today, and the Arabs are there too.

That is the recompence Joel speaks of: what you did to my people, I will have done to you. They recompensed the Most High by selling us as slaves, so he will sell their sons and daughters into the hand of the children of Judah, and they shall sell them to the Sabeans, to a people far off. Eye for eye, tooth for tooth. “For the Lord hath spoken it”, and Christians cannot change this Bible.

precepts.label: Psalms 17:13
precepts.why:
Amos says, “And though they go into captivity before their enemies, thence will I command the sword, and it shall slay them”. Who is the sword? The wicked at the time. David shows it: “Arise, O Lord, disappoint him, cast him down: deliver my soul from the wicked, which is thy sword”, and he goes on, “From men which are thy hand, O Lord”.

God wields the wicked as his sword. The wicked today is the United States. He is going to use them to bring in all these wars you are seeing, and we have to get right.

That is why we can't bug out or get caught up in everything going on. Nobody wants to see Arab children losing limbs; nobody wants to see destruction. But we understand why it is happening, and we understand what we have to do, so that when the final war comes, he that endureth to the end shall be saved. That is what we want: deliverance.

So it was with us. The twelve tribes went into captivity after captivity before our enemies, because God allowed every bit of it. He commanded the sword and it slew us, and he set his eyes upon us “for evil, and not for good”, because we did not keep the commandments. The Iranians don't get a pass; they had us in captivity too, as did the princes of Ishmael. There is slavery happening right now in parts of Africa, and it is not Black Americans or Israelites running it, but Arabs and Caucasians with financial power. Wars are here: seek good and not evil.

precepts.label: Isaiah 46:10
precepts.why:
Amos says “the Lord God of hosts is he that toucheth the land”. When Iran is being touched right now, and Israel, the Lord is involved in all of it; by his counsel the land gets touched. Isaiah shows that counsel: “Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done”.

This is the power we have: understanding that the Most High God from the very beginning planned every war, including the third world war to come. Ancient times means way back when Adam and Eve walked. From then he declared it. As his sons and daughters, the Israelites, we have to know our Father has this covered and his Son is coming back. Right now we have to rehearse the righteous acts and get right.

That is how we can make the bold statement that God is behind the Israelis doing what they do in the US government, and behind the Iranians spending twenty years building huge, elaborate tunnel systems and storing munitions and advanced rocketry. All of it was set up from ancient times. They send drones that cost fifteen to twenty thousand dollars, and the other side fires interceptor missiles that cost a million or more to take them out. You see how they will not be able to keep up. God put all that in these leaders.

“My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure”. It was his pleasure when we went into chattel slavery, through Jim Crow and through civil rights. We had to learn the lesson.

Jeremiah shows the same counsel: “Therefore hear ye the counsel of the Lord, that he hath taken against Babylon”. “Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out”: Israel, the least of Esau's flock, draws the United States out into the Middle East, and “At the noise of the taking of Babylon the earth is moved”. Amos lived way before anything could melt the land. Today thermonuclear ICBMs can, and it is all by his counsel.

precepts.label: Obadiah 1:3
precepts.why:
The vision of Obadiah is a prophecy concerning Edom, a time to come, and we must be occupied in prophecies. The Lord says, “Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art greatly despised.” Edom will be greatly despised. Then he shows why: “The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee”. They are so prideful that they themselves are deceived.

“Thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock”: they are the cavemen. So Karen has nerve telling you don't park there, you don't belong here, being black while in Starbucks. You was in a cave. Now their pride has deceived them into thinking they are the wise of the earth, the most civilized of the earth. No: they are the most demonic of the earth.

“Whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” They ask that question as though they are God. Ezekiel shows the same prince of Tyrus, for Edom was also called Tyrus: “thou hast said, I am a God, I sit in the seat of God, in the midst of the seas; yet thou art a man, and not God”. Their bases sit in the midst of the seas. “Behold, thou art wiser than Daniel; there is no secret that they can hide from thee”: through all their technological advances they listen through your smart TV and your phone, and by that wisdom and traffic they got riches and lifted up their heart.

That pride grows from the weaponry given to that line from Tubal-cain and Lamech down to Esau, who by his sword would live. The Lord created the smith and the waster. In Isaiah the same one is called Lucifer and the king of Babylon, who weakened the nations through war: “I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the most High.” With all this military might they feel like they are the Most High, and people see it and say he must be God or God must be with them.

But the answer to “Who shall bring me down to the ground?” is the Lord. “How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer”. He is going to fall because his pride has reached up unto heaven, and when these devils fall, the whole earth will finally be at rest.

precepts.label: Psalms 140:11
precepts.why:
“The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” There is a set time for the times of the Gentiles to be fulfilled, with Esau at the top, that same spirit of Cain in rulership. But it is temporary. Waiting generation after generation for his judgment, the pride of his heart has deceived him. He forgot what his judgment is and thinks he is untouchable, especially after seeing what his weapons did to the air defences of Russia and China.

Now Trump is talking like that. On Air Force One after capturing Maduro he names the countries he will come after: Colombia, run by a sick man; Mexico, where the cartels are running things. He says the vice president of Venezuela will face a situation probably worse than Maduro, and emphasises how fast and violent it was: it was very violent. That office once had prestige, and though they did their evil, they at least spoke well. He is not even bothering with appearances anymore.

David shows where that ends: “Let not an evil speaker be established in the earth: evil shall hunt the violent man to overthrow him.” You reap what you sow. What he puts out is the exact same way his demise is going to come.

That is the lineage of Cain: Tubal-cain was “an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron”, and where others saw tools his mind saw weapons. Murder led to industry, hatred to technology, and violence to institutional power. Esau was told, “by thy sword shalt thou live.” But who shall bring him down to the ground? It is prophesied: first all those he dealt with will turn against him, and then Christ and his elect will have the glory and the honour to take him down.

precepts.label: Isaiah 30:12-13
precepts.why:
Micah says, “Arise ye, and depart; for this is not your rest: because it is polluted, it shall destroy you, even with a sore destruction.” America, Babylon the great, all the lands we have been enslaved and colonised in, are not our rest. Isaiah shows why staying in them destroys us: “Wherefore thus saith the Holy One of Israel, Because ye despise this word, and trust in oppression and perverseness, and stay thereon”.

We despise God's word and trust in oppression. It was a sin for us to trust in this oppression and to stay and believe in it. “Therefore this iniquity shall be to you as a breach ready to fall, swelling out in a high wall, whose breaking cometh suddenly at an instant.” There is no comfort and no protective covering in this society, in assimilating into America, Babylon the great. Our brothers and sisters that love this society and this world, it is our downfall as a people.

That is the pollution Micah speaks of. When you forget where you come from and get comfortable in the land of your captivity, it destroys you, because you begin to take on the attributes of your oppressor. That is not for us. We are God's children, and trying to make the oppressor's ways work for us always backfires. The white man has had the sword and the power to rule the world, but God will not let his children follow after him like the rest of the world and prosper.

So the wall breaks suddenly. In every place we have been, oppression, death and destruction follow behind us, and there is no peace there. Look at the families of Nolan Wales, of Kendrick Johnson, of the young woman found hanging from a tree in Mississippi: they never have rest again. And look at how we think as a people on social media and in all these podcasts: from the aged man and aged woman down to the children, we are in a sore destruction, because we have gotten comfortable in our captivity, “forgotten their restingplace”, and do not even want to go back to our homeland.

precepts.label: Obadiah 1:1-4
precepts.why:
Habakkuk describes the man who “transgresseth by wine, he is a proud man”. The wine he transgresses by is his Christianity and his democracy, which are virtually the same thing: his policies, his religions, his politics. Obadiah names the proud man: “Thus saith the Lord God concerning Edom”.

“We have heard a rumour from the Lord, and an ambassador is sent among the heathen, Arise ye, and let us rise up against her in battle.” Someone is going to rise up among the nations and say, let's go against America, let's go against Israel in battle. “Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art greatly despised.”

“The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high”. Edom is the prideful man. They come from the Caucasus Mountains and dwelt in the clefts of the rock through the Middle Ages; in Obadiah's time it was the place called Petra today, and look at the architecture, just like Rome, just like Washington D.C. Their high habitation now is their skyscrapers. “That saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” To say that you have to have power: they are saying nobody can beat us.

“Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars”. Their symbol is the eagle: take out your dollar bill. Who is sending satellites and doing space travel? America. So Edom is not the Arabs: the Arabs are not doing space travel, and their symbol is not the eagle. Nor is it the American Indian, who uses the eagle, because if they had had power they would have blown the white man off the face of the earth. People throw these things out to confuse the new converts.

“Thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord.” That began when the truth started to come out in the 1960s. And Habakkuk shows how: he “neither keepeth at home”, a busybody in every nation, destabilising country after country by economic or conventional war and gathering the residue of those peoples to America and England. “Shall they not rise up suddenly that shall bite thee”: terrorism from within, slowly but surely, “Because thou hast spoiled many nations”.

precepts.label: Zechariah 9:13
precepts.why:
Habakkuk sees Christ coming: “Thy bow was made quite naked, according to the oaths of the tribes, even thy word.” The oaths of the tribes is the Bible. A bow in hand means you are coming for war, so according to the oaths of Jacob, Christ is coming for war. Zechariah shows what that bow is: “When I have bent Judah for me, filled the bow with Ephraim, and raised up thy sons, O Zion, against thy sons, O Greece”.

The Lord bends Judah for himself like a bow and fills the bow with Ephraim: Judah and Ephraim are the bow and the arrow. He raises up the sons of Zion, the rest of the twelve tribes, against the sons of Greece: against the Greeks, the white man. That is war.

That is why this tribulation will not be like any other we have gone through. There will be wars like we have never seen, and in the midst of world war Christ comes: Armageddon. “Thou didst march through the land in indignation, thou didst thresh the heathen in anger.” Indignation is righteous anger, and he beats the nations in it. The arrows and the glittering spear are the missiles being shot.

And the war is for his people alone: “Thou wentest forth for the salvation of thy people, even for salvation with thine anointed”. He is only coming to save the twelve tribes of Israel. “Thou woundedst the head out of the house of the wicked”: that is the white man, and America is the head, discovered “unto the neck” to make sure it is finished. Judah and Ephraim in his hand are how he does it.

precepts.label: Sirach 25:1
precepts.why:
“In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.” The Lord puts the unity of brethren first. Then the love of neighbours: the charity, the long-suffering.

Then “a man and a wife that agree together.” Agree on what? The commandments. That is not talking about arguing over the curtains. Brother, when did you become a fashion designer, an interior decorator? Let your wife handle that. The agreement God counts beautiful is agreement in keeping his law.

This is what the gathering of Zephaniah 2:1 has to look like. “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired”: the nation hated upon the earth has to come together in the last days. But as we gather, we have to fix our character flaws, show ourselves friendly, and endeavor to keep the unity, and endeavor is an enduring word, not one to be taken lightly.

Unity of brethren does not mean you cannot correct one another or admonish one another. It means you expect highly of each other. We need correction, admonishment, counsel and advice amongst each other. Those who push you toward hard things, who tell you the harsh truth when a lie would be easier, are your people. That is how the gathered nation stands up beautiful before God and men.

precepts.label: Leviticus 19:17
precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him.” Love for one another means we are not supposed to suffer sin on one another.

So if I see my brother or my sister in the midst of sin, I might have to give them that rough talk. And it is to do what? To put them back in the righteous mindset. Real admonishment and love, being able to correct your brothers, comes with a little bit of hard criticism. You cannot take it emotionally, and you cannot take it personally. Tell the brother he is fat: fix it, brother. That is love, not hate.

Friends who roast each other are the loyal ones; those who value your success over the need to be liked are the ones who truly want your best. Their words are heavy, but their loyalty is pure. Don’t think that because a man is charitable he doesn’t correct anybody. We have to stop thinking with that emotional Christianity.

This is how the nation of Zephaniah 2:1 gathers. “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired”: in the last days we gather with the believers who fear the Lord, and until we receive our homeland we are all we got. Rebuking one another in love keeps the gathered body clean and keeps the unity.

precepts.label: 2 Chronicles 20:12
precepts.why:
“The burden of the word of the Lord in the land of Hadrach, and Damascus shall be the rest thereof”: this is Syria. And it comes “when the eyes of man, as of all the tribes of Israel, shall be toward the Lord.” All the eyes of Israel, our people, shall be toward the Lord.

2 Chronicles 20:12 has the wording for it: “O our God, wilt thou not judge them? for we have no might against this great company that cometh against us; neither know we what to do: but our eyes are upon thee.” That is what we are saying to the Lord.

The nations are at war around Syria, Lebanon, Gaza and Ashkelon, and we have no might against that great company. We do not know what to do. So we keep our eyes on the Lord, and we have to put our attention toward him. That is the moment Zechariah is speaking of, when the burden of the Lord falls on those lands and all the tribes of Israel look to him.

precepts.label: Leviticus 17:10-14
precepts.why:
Zechariah 9:7 says “And I will take away his blood out of his mouth, and his abominations from between his teeth”. First the scripture about blood: “whatsoever man there be of the house of Israel, or of the strangers that sojourn among you, that eateth any manner of blood; I will even set my face against that soul that eateth blood, and will cut him off from among his people. For the life of the flesh is in the blood”.

“Therefore I said unto the children of Israel, No soul of you shall eat blood”. Whoever hunts and catches a beast or fowl “shall even pour out the blood thereof, and cover it with dust.” “Ye shall eat the blood of no manner of flesh: for the life of all flesh is the blood thereof: whosoever eateth it shall be cut off.” That includes those of you who came from Santo Domingo: you are not to be eating blood sausage, black sausage. Don't eat that.

Now look at the blood in his mouth and the abomination between his teeth. These people, these bastards in Ashdod, in the ritual they call metzitzah b'peh, remove the foreskin of the baby and put their mouth on the wound and suck the blood from it. Infants have caught herpes from it, and the rabbis in New York negotiate to keep doing it. That is an abomination from between your teeth. What the hell is wrong with you? Your mom ain't teach you nothing?

One man called them a militarized vampire nation, living on death and destruction, on blood. Ezekiel 35:5-6 says it of Esau: because thou hast had a perpetual hatred and shed the blood of the children of Israel, “sith thou hast not hated blood, even blood shall pursue thee.” The Most High is exposing them: the bloody mattress and baby clothes in the tunnels in Brooklyn, the baby clothes and toys on Epstein Island. God will take away the blood out of his mouth.

precepts.label: 2 Samuel 5:8
precepts.why:
Zechariah 9:7 ends: “but he that remaineth, even he, shall be for our God, and he shall be as a governor in Judah, and Ekron as a Jebusite.” He that remaineth is you and I. And on the map, Ekron sits right there above Jerusalem.

What does it mean to be as a Jebusite? “And David said on that day, Whosoever getteth up to the gutter, and smiteth the Jebusites, and the lame and the blind, that are hated of David’s soul, he shall be chief and captain. Wherefore they said, The blind and the lame shall not come into the house. So David dwelt in the fort, and called it the city of David.”

When you read the history, David smote the Jebusites and made them servants. That is what he did. So when Zechariah says “Ekron as a Jebusite”, the land that the Philistines hold will be brought under Israel the way David brought the Jebusites under him.

precepts.label: 1 Kings 9:20-21
precepts.why:
“And all the people that were left of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, which were not of the children of Israel, Their children that were left after them in the land, whom the children of Israel also were not able utterly to destroy, upon those did Solomon levy a tribute of bondservice unto this day.”

They were our servants, our slaves. The Jebusites left in the land did not rule over Israel; Solomon put them under a tribute of bondservice.

So when we go back to the last part of Zechariah 9:7, “and Ekron as a Jebusite”, it means they are going to be our servants. Those that are left of the Philistines will be to Israel what the Jebusites were to David and Solomon, while he that remaineth of Israel “shall be as a governor in Judah.” The pride of the Philistines is cut off, and the order is turned back the way God set it.

precepts.label: Exodus 2:25
precepts.why:
Zechariah 9:8: “And I will encamp about mine house because of the army, because of him that passeth by, and because of him that returneth: and no oppressor shall pass through them any more: for now have I seen with mine eyes.” No oppressor shall oppress us any more; they will not pass through.

And “now have I seen with mine eyes” is the same as Exodus 2:25: “And God looked upon the children of Israel, and God had respect unto them.” In Egypt God looked upon Israel under their oppressors and had respect unto them, and then he brought them out.

So when he says now have I seen with mine eyes, he is looking upon us to have respect unto us. The Lord encamps about his house, the oppressor is stopped, and right after it Zechariah says “Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion”, because the King comes.
