precepts.label: 2 Thessalonians 2:1-3
precepts.why:
Paul told Timothy he was persuaded that Christ “is able to keep that which I have committed unto him against that day.” Paul committed his soul, his life, to Christ. What day? Thessalonians explains it: “Now we beseech you, brethren, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and by our gathering together unto him.” That day is the second coming, and all twelve tribes can only gather unto Christ.

“That ye be not soon shaken in mind, or be troubled, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter as from us, as that the day of Christ is at hand.” People were writing letters in Paul’s name saying the second coming had already happened and you missed it. Paul said, I don’t care if you got a letter signed by me, I didn’t write that; that day did not happen yet. Remember in the sixties the FBI would write letters to the Black Panthers and other black organizations in each other’s names. They were doing the same thing with Paul.

“Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first.” Christ is not going to return until all twelve tribes fall away into captivity. Christians break that down as people leaving Christianity; it is not talking about that crap. It is falling into captivity, as Luke 21:24 says: “they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.” All twelve shall fall, and we are still living in the times of the Gentiles.

In Paul’s day, Judah, Benjamin and Levi had not fallen completely; they were still in the land. But 70 AD was soon approaching. So the day Paul committed his soul against has not come yet, and it could not come until all of us fell. And we all fell.

precepts.label: Joel 2:31
precepts.why:
“That day” in Paul’s words to Timothy is the second coming, and Joel shows what kind of day it is: “The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and the terrible day of the Lord come.” This is a time of war and devastation. When Christ returns, it is going to be a great and terrible day.

Amos says the same: “Woe unto you that desire the day of the Lord! to what end is it for you? the day of the Lord is darkness, and not light.” We say we can’t wait for the day of the Lord because we don’t really comprehend the magnitude of what is going to happen. You think it is going to be a bright day and Christ will take us all up to the kingdom. It is not that type of a day; it is not that type of a party.

Zephaniah: “The great day of the Lord is near, it is near, and hasteth greatly, even the voice of the day of the Lord: the mighty man shall cry there bitterly. That day is a day of wrath, a day of trouble and distress.” Don’t think that when the Lord returns we are all going to be standing and cheering. We are going to be running and weeping.

Christ said it in Matthew 24: “Immediately after the tribulation of those days”, which is Jacob’s trouble, “shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light”, because the sky will be black, “and the stars shall fall from heaven”: missiles dropping from the sky. The powers of the nations shall be shaken with war. “and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.” You think you will be happy, stomping your feet and clapping; the Bible says all the tribes shall mourn, meaning cry bitterly. That is the day Paul was preparing Timothy for, and why he told him to stir up the gift, not fear, and not be ashamed of the afflictions of the gospel.

thread.label: 2 Timothy 1:7
thread.text: For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.

precepts.label: Psalms 42:5
precepts.why:
“For God hath not given us the spirit of fear”. When fear or trouble tries to put you down, David shows how to talk to your own soul: “Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted in me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him for the help of his countenance.”

David is speaking to himself, to his soul. Put plain: I might be down, but I'm not broken. I might be down, but I'm not out yet. Satan tried to take me out, but I'm still fighting. My hope is in the Lord, and I still have some fight in me.

Some of you are quick to give up. As soon as something happens, you run out: why did they have to put correction? Correction is a good thing. It keeps you on your toes, it makes you better and stronger. What doesn't break you makes you stronger; that is correction, that is the word of God. You can use a brother's correction to build yourself up: in my mind I was going to do what this brother got corrected for, so let me move from it. Moses said some you correct openly, so that others fear. Some of you never were corrected in your life until you came to IUIC, and you are too prideful to take it.

Brothers, never keep a yes-man around you. If you have a man in your circle who cannot say, bro, I don't think you should do this, that man hates you and is waiting for your downfall. You want men who tell you, don't talk evil of leadership; if you have a problem with a brother, go to him. Sisters are the same: the sister who won't tell you what you want to hear is not your enemy, she is the one you want around you, because she has no respect of persons. Men like that help you get the kingdom of heaven.

precepts.label: Psalms 38:8-9
precepts.why:
David was down but not out, and he did not hide it from God: “I am feeble and sore broken: I have roared by reason of the disquietness of my heart.” To roar is to utter or express in a loud tone: to cry, shout, yell. David says, I'm feeble, I'm broken, and I cried out because of the disquietness of my heart.

“Lord, all my desire is before thee; and my groaning is not hid from thee.” He laid it all before the Lord.

Some of you, when you pray, do not pray for yourself, because you think you are perfect. You need to pray for yourself and ask for help to overcome certain things. Some of you are fighting lust; when you fast, pray that Messiah helps you overcome that lust. We all have lust. Our lust might be different things, but we all have it. Some of you are fighting a covetous spirit; pray that Messiah helps you overcome it.

You are not going to walk into the kingdom of heaven thinking you're perfect and your stuff don't stink. Put your desire and your groaning before the Lord, so that when the storm comes, fear does not overtake you.

precepts.label: Revelation 2:26
precepts.why:
You won't walk into the kingdom thinking you are perfect. This is what Christ said: “And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations”.

The word is overcome. Brothers, you must overcome the lust of America, and you must also overcome the personal thing you struggle with. We all struggle with things. Some of you struggle with lust, with porn, with prostitution, with drugs. Some of you are crackheads, weed heads; some of you it's cigarettes, Black and Milds, women. And yes, it is said to shame you. This is not my word; don't get mad at me. Read what Christ says you have to do.

The words “keepeth my works” mean keep my commandments, keep my laws. My works is this book: keep it. If you keep it, that means you have overcome. You must overcome, or else you are not going to make it to the kingdom.

So when you watch all these prophecies happen, don't include yourself if you won't let the lust go. Some of you need to let things go. That is how you keep from the spirit of fear: you prepare your mind in the scriptures and overcome, so that Esau has nothing to hold over you and you don't betray your brother to hide what you were watching.

precepts.label: Sirach 2:5
precepts.why:
“For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.” You are that gold. We are that gold. How do you purify gold? By putting it in the fire. Some of you need to go into the fire. You have stuff on you that has to be purged out, but you want to keep it and still have the kingdom of heaven. If you don't want to be purged, you cannot get the kingdom. Some of you want to be iron, some of you want to be silver; you have to be that gold.

What is the purpose of going through all that and not getting the kingdom? Esau has been putting you through hell all your life, and you end up missing the kingdom because you hold on to things and don't want God to take the unclean out of you.

Some of you hold on to things that happened fifty years ago, twenty years ago, five years ago. That's like a woman in an argument: you're talking about the orange and she says, yeah, but the pineapple happened five years ago. There's no pineapple here; we're talking about the orange. Some sisters got notes, waiting to bring them out. Men should not be emotional like that.

And “acceptable men in the furnace of adversity”: it takes a strong man to take correction. Weak men cannot. When correction comes, the strong man gets up, repents and keeps moving, and you can tell he is still in the fight. When you get correction, that's when you push harder. Don't lay back. Prove to Messiah, not to leadership, that you are still in the fight.

The Bottle, the Battle, and the Bible

precepts.label: Philippians 3:20
precepts.why:
If Christ is our commander, what does that make us? Soldiers. “Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ.” And a soldier cannot live for this world: “For our conversation is in heaven; from whence also we look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ.”

We are at war. Spiritual war. We don’t use guns or weapons or any of that stuff, but we are at spiritual war, and spiritual war is the most powerful mode of warfare. Our forefathers understood that in this gospel, this mission we are on, we are all soldiers on the battlefield. That is how Paul referred to his fellow laborers.

“No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.” In order to please God, who has called us to be soldiers, we cannot be entangled with the affairs of this life. If you are entangled with the affairs of this life, that means you want to please men. We can’t move like that. Our conversation is in heaven, and we are looking for the Saviour to come from there.

So what does God want us to do? What does God require of us? What is God’s mission? Gather the twelve tribes of Israel from the four corners of the earth. Let the elect be sealed; let the 144 be sealed, so we can go home. That is the business of a good soldier of Jesus Christ, with the mind of a judge that comes from biblical education, instead of the affairs of this life.

thread.label: 2 Timothy 4:10,14-16
thread.text: For Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world, and is departed unto Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus unto Dalmatia.

precepts.label: Mark 4:16-19
precepts.why:
“For Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world.” Demas traveled with Paul and warred with Paul, and he forsook Paul. He saw the looseness of the women: Paul, I’ve got to go, my man, I can’t roll with you no more, I got needs. He let that overcome him. Crescens left for Galatia, Titus for Dalmatia. Mark shows what happened to Paul’s companions, men who were strong in the Lord and in the power of his might. Those guys are some of you guys.

“And these are they likewise which are sown on stony ground; who, when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with gladness.” I’m an Israelite, we got history, oh I love it. “And have no root in themselves, and so endure but for a time.” No root: I don’t study, I don’t addict myself to the ministry, I like my sports, I like my porn, the Bible comes last. So you only endure this gospel for a time.

“afterward, when affliction or persecution ariseth for the word’s sake, immediately they are offended.” Offended, and you leave. Affliction is things that happen to you; persecution is what happens to you for the word’s sake, because you stand strong in this Bible. That is why Paul told Timothy not to be ashamed of his affliction, to suffer in it with him and stir up the gift within him. Christ lets us know some of us are going to leave this truth because of affliction.

And Satan will test. He asks the Lord, can I test him? Can I test her? The brother with a proclivity for the male gender went to the gym at two in the morning, where the freaks come out at night, found two men in the shower, stood there five whole minutes, and they invited him to join in. If you are struggling, stay out of the gym; do calisthenics at your house. You are trying to fight a spirit; don’t go around spirits like that.

“And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word, And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.” The cares of this world and the deceitfulness of riches, a piece of the American pie, may not be your thing. But the lust of other things is anything in you that nobody else knows. You may hide it very well, but God knows it is there, Satan knows it is there, and you do too. Satan is not tempting you with a pork chop. He looks into your soul, sees what you are battling with, and asks to tempt you right there.

That is what took Demas, Crescens and Titus, and it is what Paul went through with Alexander the coppersmith, who was in the ministry and turned against it, “for he hath greatly withstood our words.” We have seen the same: men in the gospel who went online to try to tear this down. “At my first answer no man stood with me, but all men forsook me.” Christ already prophesied it: “And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.” In 2018 brothers were dropping like flies, brothers and sisters we broke bread with, who stayed in our homes and knew our families, offended at the gospel and betraying it. Some tried to start Israelite congregations and fell overnight. God is not going to bless your hands after you did so much evil to your brothers and sisters.

precepts.label: Proverbs 29:1
precepts.why:
Hebrews warns “lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you”. Where does that root come from? Proverbs answers: “He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck”. He that is often corrected hardens his neck, meaning his mind. You can't tell that brother nothing: I'm a man, you a man, I do what I want. Well, do what you want and burn by yourself.

That is the mindset of a lot of our brothers and sisters. They never took the scripture serious. Leadership corrects them, corrects them, corrects them, to the point where the correction is null and void, because they are not going to apply anything. After a while the Lord says, this spirit is rebellious as hell; he always hardens his mind and doesn't give a damn what you're saying.

You end up hardening your heart from always having correction done to you, until at the end of the day bitterness is formed, and then you're out the door with your wife and your children.

So the question for every brother and sister: are you one of the many that shall be offended when correction comes, when the men are told to get their homes in order and the women to be that pillar of rest and not stress? Or will you get in check with the Lord? The bitterness of Hebrews 12 grows out of a neck hardened against reproof.

precepts.label: Psalms 109:6-9
precepts.why:
Hebrews says “Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau”. Paul is comparing the wicked of our people to Esau, who was wicked and estranged from the womb and went to the Canaanitish women when he wanted to get married. The bitter among us become compared to Edom, and Satan becomes their daddy. Psalms shows it: “Set thou a wicked man over him: and let Satan stand at his right hand.” That wicked man is Satan, the daddy of Esau and of the wicked of our people.

“When he shall be judged, let him be condemned: and let his prayer become sin.” Why does his prayer become sin? Because Christ said if you have an ought with your brother, go to him; leave your gift at the altar. You can't come to the Lord while the matter between you and your brother and your sister is not dealt with right. In 2018 there were extortioners speaking against leadership. You are not supposed to rise up against the hoary head; you are supposed to honor, and not revile the gods, your leaders. There was a lot of disrespect and dishonor.

“Let his days be few; and let another take his office. Let his children be fatherless, and his wife a widow.” That is what happens when Satan becomes your daddy. Repent.

So the profane spirit of Hebrews 12, the bitter brother or sister who turns on leadership, carries this lot. We are trying to encourage our people not to be worldly, not to keep the customs of Edom and the I-do-me, but to come back home to your people.

thread.label: Hebrews 13:1-6
thread.text: Let brotherly love continue.

thread.label: Hebrews 13:4
thread.text: Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled: but whoremongers and adulterers God will judge.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 3:5
precepts.why:
“Marriage is honourable in all.” Who makes a marriage honourable? Both sides applying the scriptures, the man and the woman loving their neighbour as themselves and dealing right with each other. A marriage does not become honourable just like that. Being an Israelite married to an Israelite sister does not make it honourable, because some are dishonourable brothers and dishonourable sisters: vessels to dishonour who hate each other, fight and argue all the time, speak evil about each other, with no love in the house. Those marriages are not honourable.

“For if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?” This is what the brothers have to understand. It is not up to leadership to rule you men or to rule your house for you. It is not our job to tell your wife to respect you. It is your job to rule your own damn house.

A lot of you come for counsel, and counsel is given twice on the same matter. If you are counselled twice and it isn’t fixed, you aren’t listening, you are wasting our time, and something is wrong with both of you. Couples come for advice, then a couple of months later: I hate you, I hope you die; and on the Sabbath, shalom, brother, Most High and Christ bless. You are fake and phony. Leaders, stop counselling the dishonourable, hateful brothers and sisters over and over; let them learn online, and deal with the people who really want help.

Leadership’s job is to give you the scriptures so you can fix yourself; it cannot fix you. We cannot force your husband to love you; it is up to you to be a good wife. And brothers, we cannot make your wife respect and love you; you have to figure out how to fix that. The ones who fix it never come back: the brother says yes, I understand, goes home and fixes it, and the sister fixes it. The key is that people have to see their own faults. Some are always looking for somebody to blame, and they will blame leadership, but ruling the house is the man’s charge.

thread.label: Hebrews 13:7
thread.text: Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God: whose faith follow, considering the end of their conversation.

classes.title: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.label: Matthew 16:17-18
precepts.why:
Christ answered Peter, “Blessed art thou, Simon Bar–jona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven.” Then he told him, “thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.”

How do you think that made Peter feel? Christ telling you, I am going to build my church upon you. That is what great leaders do. Good leaders make you believe in them; great leaders make you believe in you. They empower others, they strengthen others, they make you believe in yourself and not in them.

That is how a leader transfers his belief onto others, the faith Hebrews 13:7 tells us to follow. It is how the Bishop is able to raise up other bishops, raise up deacons, raise up captains, and soldiers by the thousands. Great leaders raise up more leaders.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 3:25-28
precepts.why:
Moses prayed, “I pray thee, let me go over, and see the good land that is beyond Jordan, that goodly mountain, and Lebanon. But the Lord was wroth with me for your sakes, and would not hear me”. He was told, “Let it suffice thee; speak no more unto me of this matter”, and to go up to the top of Pisgah and behold the land with his eyes, “for thou shalt not go over this Jordan.”

Moses could not cross over, but look at what he was charged to do: “But charge Joshua, and encourage him, and strengthen him: for he shall go over before this people, and he shall cause them to inherit the land which thou shalt see.” Charge him, encourage him, strengthen him.

That is your job as a leader: to encourage and strengthen the men around you. A leader transfers his belief onto the next man, so that the one coming after him can lead the people into what he himself was given to see. That is part of the faith that those who have the rule over you pass on.

precepts.label: Job 4:3
precepts.why:
“Behold, thou hast instructed many, and thou hast strengthened the weak hands.” Your job as a leader is to instruct many. And your job is to strengthen the weak hands.

It is your job to build the brothers and the sisters up in the spirit. That is part of how a leader transfers his belief onto others: those who have the rule over you and have spoken unto you the word of God instruct you, and when your hands are weak they strengthen them, so that you can follow their faith.

precepts.label: Luke 22:32
precepts.why:
Christ told Peter, “But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.” When you convert, strengthen your brothers. That is the charge that goes with the faith that is passed on to you.

Read on and Peter answers, “Lord, I am ready to go with thee, both into prison, and to death”, and Christ answers that before the cock crows Peter will thrice deny that he knows him. Christ prayed that Peter's faith would not fail, knowing what was coming, and still gave him the work of strengthening his brethren.

This is the leader transferring his belief onto others. Christ imparted his faith to Peter, and Peter was to impart it to the brethren. The one who has been strengthened turns around and strengthens the next man.

precepts.label: Acts 18:23
precepts.why:
“And after he had spent some time there, he departed, and went over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.” Paul went country to country strengthening all the disciples. That is the job of a leader, and it shows how a leader transfers his belief onto others.

The same work goes on today. As the bishops and the deacons trailblazed the way, the captains follow the same path, and when they go to these places they continue to build our people up worldwide. A captain just back from Guyana reports that the brothers and sisters there in South America are growing tremendously, doing real good. The Lord has good things for them.

Like Paul in Galatia and Phrygia, the leaders go out to the nations where our people are and strengthen the disciples there.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 4:17
precepts.why:
“Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me; that by me the preaching might be fully known”. The Lord stood with Paul and strengthened him, so that the preaching might go forth by him.

That is our job: we must strengthen one another. You get weak at different times. You need counsel. You need some exhortation. You have to vent sometimes. And it is your job as a leader to be there to strengthen each other, as the Lord stood with Paul.

So those who have the rule over you and speak the word of God unto you are there to strengthen you, and when you are strengthened, you follow their faith and do the same for those around you.

precepts.label: Nehemiah 3:8-9
precepts.why:
This is the rebuilding of Jerusalem. “Next unto him repaired Uzziel the son of Harhaiah, of the goldsmiths. Next unto him also repaired Hananiah the son of one of the apothecaries, and they fortified Jerusalem unto the broad wall.” Each man repaired his own section of the wall. Then: “And next unto them repaired Rephaiah the son of Hur, the ruler of the half part of Jerusalem.” The ruler of the half part: he was a supervisor over that area.

That is leadership. When you come in the truth you may just edit the video, go on the fly mission, or work in the kitchen. At some point you become over the office: now you are over the brothers that are editing, over the IT team, over the building team, over the sisters. Now your job changes, because you have people under you. Everybody is not built for that level. You are not in charge; you are responsible for those in your charge. In IUIC there are different offices with leads in place, and a man who was once responsible for one office, the Lord entrusted him with more.

Sometimes brothers get overwhelmed, and that will happen. But there is no better thing than to be overwhelmed for the Lord. You do not have a demon on your back, you are not behind bars, you are not suffering illness; you are stressed out for the Lord's work, and that is a beautiful thing. So do not complain. Come up and say, I need more assistance in this office. Pray and fast for more laborers, and rejoice in it, because the Lord gave you that office and put you in that position.

thread.text: From whence come wars and fightings among you? come they not hence, even of your lusts that war in your members?

precepts.label: 1 John 2:15
precepts.why:
“From whence come wars and fightings among you? come they not hence, even of your lusts that war in your members?” It is a consistent battle between the spiritual man and the carnal man. “Ye lust, and have not: ye kill, and desire to have”: you slander the brother or sister who has what you want, give them the evil eye, speak nasty. You ask for a home, a car, a wife, and receive not, because you “ask amiss, that ye may consume it upon your lusts”: to show off, to stunt, to have a trophy wife, to be seen of men.

Christ said if you love the world, you hate me. John writes it: “Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him.” Love not this captivity, neither the precious things and riches in this captivity, neither the mansion on the hill, not even your damn job. A lot of brothers love their jobs more than they love this truth.

These things are hooks inside of you that will pull you out of this truth. They are devices of Satan, the tangible trinkets he gives, which our brothers and sisters lust after as status symbols when the kingdom of heaven is at hand. In Babylon everything is accessible at your fingertips, and everything as far as your eye can see appeals to the flesh.

If any man loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him. That is why James says “the friendship of the world is enmity with God.” Enmity means the state of being actively opposed or hostile, a feud, conflict, bitterness, resentment. That is the mentality that says why do I have to keep the Sabbath, I could be at home, the boxing match is on today. Some sneak off for Christmas and come back with fifteen presents in the trunk. You hate God and God’s laws. This captivity, the dominion of your oppressor, is going to go, and if you don’t kill that old man and that old woman, you are going with him. Kill or be killed.

precepts.label: Matthew 6:24
precepts.why:
On the line of adultery and lust and the love of the world, Christ said: “No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.”

A decision has to be made. Either you hate God, have enmity against him, and love the other, or you hold to the one and despise the other. The other can be money, your career, your bed because you don’t want to be here, a Christmas stocking full of abominations. Some snuck off and celebrated the devastation of their brothers, the slaughter of the tribe of Gad, got a turkey drumstick, watched the football game, then came back saying shalom, Most High in Christ bless. Many will hold on to the world and despise the heavenly Father.

You cannot serve the God of the nation of Israel and mammon. Brothers and sisters are more loyal to their jobs and the white man who runs the corporations, who can terminate your contract after fifteen years of loyalty just as you are getting ready to retire. That is serving mammon.

James calls it what it is: “Ye adulterers and adulteresses.” When these other things have become a god, you have committed adultery against the heavenly Father. Many do not hate the world; they hate having to change and repent. That is the war in your members, and you have to kill that adulterous spirit inside you or it will kill you.

thread.label: James 4:6
thread.text: But he giveth more grace. Wherefore he saith, God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble.

precepts.label: Ephesians 5:26
precepts.why:
God “resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble.” The humble submit to God and resist the devil, and James goes on: “Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.” How do we purify our minds? Paul shows how Christ cleanses his people: “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word.”

In Christianity many think that because they dipped themselves in water they are a whole other person. But the true baptism is washing yourself with the word. Sitting here in the class, hearing the scriptures, is that washing. And to sanctify and cleanse by the washing of water by the word means you have to keep the commandments. That is the way you cleanse yourself.

The hands are cleansed of your evil works and evil ways, and the heart is purified of the old worldly mindset. The double minded are the brothers who want to be here but do not want to be here, one foot in and one foot out the door. That is lukewarm, and the Lord will spew the lukewarm out, which means he will put you to death. So either you are hot and kill that old man with the word, or you are lukewarm and you will be killed. Either way, somebody has to die.

The humble who receive that grace are the ones taking steps to kill the old man, sharpening their swords with the word to subdue the evil spirit that plagued them for years before they knew this glorious gospel. That washing is how the Lord draws nigh to them.

precepts.label: Psalms 19:7
precepts.why:
James says God “giveth grace unto the humble”, and calls on them: “Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.” Paul says Christ cleanses his people “with the washing of water by the word.” David shows what that word is and what it does: “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.”

The law of the Lord is perfect, and that is what is going to cleanse you. That is what makes you perfect. Keeping the commandments is the cleansing. It converts the soul: it turns the old man into a new man, and makes the simple wise.

That is how you purify your mind. Remove from you the old ways, the old worldly mindset. You cannot get that cleansing from the white man's couch or from cashing a check; pay all the bills and you will still feel empty without the Lord in your life. Submit yourselves to his will, to his law, statutes and commandments, and resist the devil, the deceiver: his lies, the Trinity, the apologetics, the false doctrines of the other nations, and the world, point blank, period.

The more you apply the law and read, the more the Lord draws nigh to you and opens his understanding to you: the dark mysteries and the parables, how to guide your household, and how to stand in the temptations, trials and lusts that come your way. The perfect law is the weapon that kills the old man.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 19:6
precepts.why:
Peter calls us “a peculiar people”. What makes us peculiar? Wisdom answers: “For the whole creature in his proper kind was fashioned again anew, serving the peculiar commandments that were given unto them”. The peculiar commandments, the same thing Deuteronomy 4 said, are what separate us. They see the fringes on your garment. They see a beard on your face. They ask why y'all never come out with us on Saturday, and you say I have to keep the Sabbath. The Sabbath, what's that? I thought you said you was Christian. That is what separates you from everybody else.

The commandments “that were given unto them”: all these things were given only to us. That is why 1 Peter 2:9 is talking about the Israelites, not the white man. It is not white Grecians in togas, and the Galatians are not the white man in Turkmenistan. It is talking about you. So many of our brothers and sisters have been destroyed and don't see themselves as a prince, a ruler, a judge, but God says you are all of those things. All the leadership books go back to the Bible, which was given only to us, yet they make billions off leadership conferences while we sit at the bottom.

We must magnify the law: “The Lord is well pleased for his righteousness’ sake; he will magnify the law”. That is each and every one of our jobs, to put the laws of God on a pedestal and stand firm for them. When you do, it automatically puts you in a different position, different from everybody else on the face of the earth, because nobody else is standing firm for the commandments. The way you do anything is the way you do everything; nine times out of ten the cracker over you on the job is no better than you, but you are not doing things according to the commandments.

That separation shows. Our sisters dress modestly while the women in Houston dressed so out of order a dress code had to be put in place. Fifty men reading the Bible on a cruise become the disturbance. They make a man an offender for the word. But we were called out of darkness to show forth his praise. Nobody takes a light and puts it under a bushel, and you don't shine from the back. It is time for all of us to take our places.

thread.label: 1 Peter 5:8-10
thread.text: Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour:

precepts.label: Sirach 42:24-25
precepts.why:
“All things are double one against another”. God created good, and he created evil also. He “hath made nothing imperfect”: Satan was not created imperfect. He was created to do exactly what he is doing, walking about like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.

“One thing establisheth the good or another”. What establishes the good of us and makes us perfect? When we go through temptation, when Satan attacks us and we overcome and are not devoured by him. Satan does devour some; some brothers and sisters get devoured. But those that are not devoured become better and become perfect. That is why Peter says “after that ye have suffered a while, make you perfect”. It is a hard saying, but without Satan, our adversary, we cannot become perfect, because it is his job and his children's job to try us, and as they try us they make us better. Even the real bad things: Job lost all his kids, and that was to make him perfect.

So learn how to fight him and how to see him when he is attacking. See him when he is coming, when he is trying to jump on you and put thoughts in your mind, and say, get out of my mind, Satan. Don't wait until he puts the thought there and you act on it, and afterward you are like Judas, what did I do? That is why the scripture says be vigilant: vigilant means you are watching.

And “who shall be filled with beholding his glory?” Those of us made perfect in trials and tribulation are the ones who will behold the Lord's glory.

precepts.label: Sirach 2:5
precepts.why:
“For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.” That fire, the furnace of adversity, is temptation. Adversity comes from our adversary, and our adversary is that spiritual demon and his children. So the furnace of adversity in Sirach is the work of the adversary the devil in Peter.

Acceptable men are that gold. When an acceptable man goes through that fire, it doesn't destroy him. It makes him better; it purifies him. When Satan attacks and kills and puts in prison, some men it will destroy, and some men it will make perfect in the sight of God. When the ADL and all these governmental organizations attack us, some of you sisters will be up out of here: I ain't messing with them, the government say they a hate group. Some of you brothers will be gone too. But some of you will be purified and become that pure gold.

You have to go through adversity. Your enemy has to attack you; that is how you become better and how you become a better fighter. Then Peter's words come to pass: “after that ye have suffered a while, make you perfect, stablish, strengthen, settle you.” Nobody wants to suffer, but the Lord says if you want the kingdom you have to suffer, and if you are acceptable, after you suffer you will get the kingdom. Suffering makes you perfect, establishes you, strengthens you until you are battle hardened like somebody who has been warring for thirty or forty years, and settles you within your spirit: it is what it is.

thread.label: 2 Peter 1:10-11

thread.label: 1 John 2:15-17
thread.text: Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him.

precepts.label: Sirach 10:12-13
precepts.why:
John says “all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world.” The lust of the flesh: in America everything is accessible; order it and it's there in twenty minutes. The lust of the eyes: social media, looking at the big butt, keeping up with the Joneses, twerking, the competition of niggardom: I can jump on a car better than she can, I can roll a blunt this big, I can rap about nothing and can't say my ABCs. Our people love the world for those things but fail to love God.

And what is the pride of life? Sirach answers: “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker.” That is the pride of life we just read in 1 John. It is when you hate God and retract yourself from the love of the heavenly Father, when you prefer this world, this system and this setup over the guidelines of God, and would rather have this phobia of freedom and be guided by your oppressors.

The scriptures say pride goeth before destruction. When you go contrary to the Lord, death is at your door: “For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that hath it shall pour out abomination: and therefore the Lord brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.”

Your heart is then removed from the one that created you. “And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof”: Esau's rulership is already ordained to pass away. Will you escape when the destruction comes, or pass away with it?

precepts.label: Psalms 40:8
precepts.why:
John says “the world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever.” Who is he that doeth the will of God? David shows it: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” He that doeth the will of God is the one who delights in his law.

That one abides for ever: you will have everlasting life, and you are going to rule over these kingdoms. Everything you could not see yourself living without in this world shall come to an end, but the one with God's law in his heart abides.

So you must hate this world and everything in it. Brothers, you have to hate even the sight of a sister in pants, to the point where it infuriates you instead of catching your eye. The YNs, the young nuisances walking around in the community, should infuriate you. Bring back the belt. But we have a belt: the God of Israel, and he is doing the whipping right now, and it will continue as long as our people love this kingdom in captivity.

Love not the world. Delight in his law, do his will, and abide for ever.

precepts.label: Proverbs 30:20
precepts.why:
“Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world.” If you love this place, the love of the Father is not in you. The state of mind of a saint is, I want to be up out of here; I hate this place. All that is in the world is “the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life”, and the lust of the eyes today is TikTok and social media, where the minds of a lot of young brothers and sisters are.

There is a challenge everybody is doing, a dance where they act like they are eating something. The song is called feeling on my body, and it is all about sex. Young brothers and sisters, even among us, watch it and mimic it, and some school sisters were doing that dumb, stupid dance on the new moon. When she says she loves an eater, you think she is talking about eating food? She ain't talking about eating food. She's talking about eating sausage.

The scripture shows what it is: “Such is the way of an adulterous woman; she eateth, and wipeth her mouth, and saith, I have done no wickedness.” She eats and wipes her mouth, and then says she has done no wickedness. That is the characteristic of an adulterous, wicked woman, and that is what the dance is about: sucking rod.

So sisters, you should not be doing those dances. You don't even understand what's behind them. It is the lust of the eyes: you see it on social media and think it's cool. It isn't innocent; you are conjuring demons. We are supposed to be separate, not following the things we see in the world, because the world passeth away, and the lust thereof, “but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever.”

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 10:1-6
precepts.why:
Jude says “I will therefore put you in remembrance, though ye once knew this, how that the Lord, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed them that believed not.” He is going into history. When we left Egypt we went into the wilderness, and the Israelites rebelled and were put to death. Who else spoke of it in the New Testament? Paul, in Corinthians the tenth chapter. Write that down in your Bible.

“Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud”. Right here it tells you who the people in Corinth were. They weren't white people, weren't Europeans, weren't natural Greeks, Caucasians. They were Israelites: our fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, not Abraham, Isaac and Esau. Under the cloud: the chariot that followed us. They “all passed through the sea; And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea”, because Moses taught the law and taught us Christ, the gospel.

“And did all eat the same spiritual meat; And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.” Christ was always present. “But with many of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the wilderness”: for murmuring, gossiping, sex, fornication.

“Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.” These things were our examples, brothers. That is what Jude puts us in remembrance of: God saved a whole people and still destroyed those who believed not. Don't lust after evil things as they did, and earnestly contend for the faith once delivered unto the saints.

precepts.label: John 3:19
precepts.why:
Jude says the angels which kept not their first estate are reserved “in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.” Has that great day come yet, brothers? No. Those sons of God who went in unto the daughters of men were destroyed in the flood, and those spirits came right back, by way of the three sons, Ham, Shem and Japheth. They are still here today.

John shows what that darkness is: “And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.” Men loving darkness rather than light is sin: you hate God's laws, you hate this truth, you hate the Bible.

There are people like that who were ordained of old to stay like that, the “certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation”. Remember 2 Thessalonians: God gave them up to strong delusion, that they should believe a lie and not repent and come into the light. Some people are bound in that darkness, and there is nothing you can do for them. That is the chains of darkness, reserved unto the judgment of the great day.

precepts.label: Acts 26:17-18
precepts.why:
Christ sent Paul, “Delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send thee, To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light”. To open our eyes, and turn us from darkness to light: from sin to righteousness.

Then, “and from the power of Satan unto God”: from the power of Satan, the prince of the power of the air, his evil communication, those unclean spirits that went out of the mouth of the dragon, the beast and the false prophet. So “that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.”

That is the other side of Jude. Some are bound in chains of darkness, loving darkness rather than light, ordained of old to that condemnation. But the ones Paul was sent to are turned from darkness to light and from Satan unto God, sanctified by faith in Christ. That is the faith once delivered unto the saints that we are earnestly contending for, casting down Esau's lies about fallen angels and Nephilim.

precepts.label: 2 Peter 2:1-6
precepts.why:
“But there were false prophets also among the people, even as there shall be false teachers among you, who privily shall bring in damnable heresies, even denying the Lord that bought them”. This is still going into the same ones Jude speaks of, what Esau calls Nephilim, because they are back today: the evil of our people. “And many shall follow their pernicious ways; by reason of whom the way of truth shall be evil spoken of. And through covetousness shall they with feigned words make merchandise of you”.

“For if God spared not the angels that sinned”. This is not literal angels up in heaven sinning against God. They cannot sin against God; they do his will, and when God tells them to do something, they do it. Stop listening to Esau, the pastors, preachers and congressmen talking about demons, Nephilim and fallen angels. That is a lie. This is the offspring of the sons of God. He “delivered them into chains of darkness”, and that is sin, “to be reserved unto judgment”, the same great day Jude talked about. What they did back then they will keep doing today; they are not going to change.

“And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly; And turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, making them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly”. He destroyed the old world with water and saved Noah and his whole family.

So nobody is confused: Jude is not talking about Uriel having a fight with an angel, uppercutting him, and the angel falling from heaven. That is garbage malarkey. Black folks live by the saying there is nothing new under the sun, and we get that from the Bible; apply the same logic here.

thread.label: Revelation 2:9-11
thread.text: I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich) and I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.

precepts.label: Revelation 12:10-11
precepts.why:
“Behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days”. They are going to pass laws to put us in prisons. That is why they keep building these detention facilities; they fill them with the people they call illegal aliens, but ultimately they are for the twelve tribes of Israel. Imagine ten days in a detention facility, being tortured, your wife and children or the brothers you war with slain in front of you, just to make you say you are not the twelve tribes and Christ is not black, and they will spare your life. Hell no. We have nothing to lose and everything to gain; they have no power over our souls.

Revelation 12 backs it up. We are going into Jacob’s trouble, when Esau does not want this gospel preached any further and will do whatever it takes to try to stop prophecy. “Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night.” Our kingdom is soon to come; before then, we are accused day and night. That is the tribulation ten days, us losing our lives for this gospel.

“And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony”. Their testimony is the testimony of this gospel. Even when persecution happens we will not fold; we don’t care about any white Jesus or any doctrine outside the twelve tribes of Israel being redeemed from our oppressors, Babylon America.

“And they loved not their lives unto the death.” We cannot be trying to spare our lives when Jacob’s trouble takes off. Loving not your life unto death means resisting every temptation to go against your God and your people. Don’t be a damn traitor. That is being faithful unto death for the crown of life.

precepts.label: Romans 12:1
precepts.why:
“Be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.” This is what we are going to sacrifice to get what is actually ours: eternal life, the kingdom of heaven.

Paul says it: “I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.” Every time these prophets go out to teach the word, they are presenting their bodies a living sacrifice. All the prophets in the Bible did it, even unto death. John was banished to the isle of Patmos; James was beheaded. They were martyred because they understood the mission, and you brothers and sisters have to understand the mission. We are the true martyrs.

Many read “be thou faithful unto death” and do not understand it. You have to put yourself there and say: there is nothing these nations can do to me, nothing you can take from me, to make me turn and betray my eternal life. There is no resurrection for them.

“He that hath an ear, let him hear”: you have to be spiritual, keeping the commandments, to understand it. “He that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death”, the death the Lord has power over, the death over your soul.

thread.label: Revelation 2:9-10
thread.text: I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich) and I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.

precepts.label: Revelation 3:9
precepts.why:
“I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich)”. Christ knows the works of the Israelites in the church of Smyrna, a colony of Israelites, and the hell they caught there, hunted by Herod for Rome. They were impoverished, but he reminded them they are rich, because all the promises in the Bible pertain only to the Israelites.

“And I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.” That is why you have people like Herod, who said he was Jewish, and Agrippa and Bernice in Acts. You want to call it hate speech; we are reading from the Bible. Then: “behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison”. That is Herod and Rome, and he calls them the devil.

Revelation 3:9 gives the end of it: “Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee.”

That is a future prophecy that has not occurred yet. Today the synagogue of Satan sits in the land calling itself Jewish; the day is coming when they will worship before the feet of the real Jews and know that God loved us. Until then, “be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.”

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 2:1-16
precepts.why:
Wisdom of Solomon 2 lets you hear the synagogue of Satan think. “For the ungodly said, reasoning with themselves, but not aright, Our life is short and tedious, and in the death of a man there is no remedy: neither was there any man known to have returned from the grave.” This ungodly is Esau.

Now watch what Esau says about us. “He was made to reprove our thoughts.” The Israelite man, the prophet, was made to reprove their thoughts. “He is grievous unto us even to behold”: just looking at us grieves them, because we are a constant reminder that we are the sons of God and they are not. “For his life is not like other men’s, his ways are of another fashion”, because we keep the commandments of God.

“We are esteemed of him as counterfeits”. That goes to Revelation 2:9 and 3:9: they are counterfeits, fakes, frauds; they are not the real Jews. The Bible calls them counterfeits; those are not my words, those are the words of God. “He abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness: he pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed”.

So those which say they are Jews and are not know it themselves. The righteous man grieves them, and that is why the devil casts some of us into prison. Be faithful unto death.

thread.label: Revelation 2:10
thread.text: Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a c

precepts.label: Acts 12:1-3
precepts.why:
“Behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison”. Did the literal devil come and cast people into prison? Did a spiritual demon snatch somebody and throw him in a cell? No. When the Bible says devil, it is interchangeable: it is talking about the father and his children. The same way we can do nothing without our Father and without the Lord in us, these people can do nothing without their father dwelling in them. He uses his children to do what he wants done.

Acts 12 shows who did it: “Now about that time Herod the king stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the church. And he killed James the brother of John with the sword. And because he saw it pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to take Peter also.” Herod was a white man, an Edomite. He killed James and put Peter in prison. So at that time the devil casting into prison was Herod, Satan’s children, Rome.

The seed of the devil came back as Esau, and the sons of God came back as Jacob: “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”. Satan means adversary, accuser, opponent: he is the Lord’s adversary and ours, and so is his seed. Devil means deceiver: as he deceived Eve, his children deceive everyone on the earth. That is why we call the so-called white man the devil, because he deceives the whole earth, and Satan, because he is our adversary and God’s.

So know who we are fighting. This is war, and the devil still casts some of us into prison through his children.

thread.label: Revelation 3:7-10
thread.text: And to the angel of the church in Philadelphia write; These things saith he that is holy, he that is true, he that hath the key of David, he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth;

precepts.label: Isaiah 57:1-2
precepts.why:
Philadelphia means brotherly love, and that church was a colony of Israelites. Christ, “he that hath the key of David”, tells them: “behold, I have set before thee an open door, and no man can shut it”. That open door is salvation. “For thou hast a little strength, and hast kept my word, and hast not denied my name.” They were under persecution, so he says he will make the synagogue of Satan come and worship before their feet.

Then verse 10: “Because thou hast kept the word of my patience, I also will keep thee from the hour of temptation, which shall come upon all the world”. The hour of temptation is Jacob’s trouble, which leads into the world war and Armageddon. The church of Philadelphia will not be there when it happens. Does that mean a force field around them? No. They are at rest.

Isaiah 57 shows it: “The righteous perisheth, and no man layeth it to heart: and merciful men are taken away, none considering that the righteous is taken away from the evil to come.” That is exactly what we just read in Revelation 3:10. “He shall enter into peace: they shall rest in their beds, each one walking in his uprightness.” Each one walking: they are not dead.

So when brothers and sisters die and people say, they keep dying, listen: I have a reason. They are at rest. You do your little tears and cry, that’s fine, but the Lord is keeping the righteous from the evil to come, the way he kept Philadelphia from the hour of temptation.

precepts.label: Daniel 12:2-3
precepts.why:
Isaiah 57 says the righteous “shall rest in their beds, each one walking in his uprightness”: they are not dead. Daniel 12 says the same thing.

“And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake”. Those that sleep in the dust are the ones that died, and they shall awake, “some to everlasting life”: the righteous brothers and the righteous sisters; “and some to shame and everlasting contempt.”

“And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.”

So the saints who died keeping the word of Christ’s patience are only sleeping. They were kept from the hour of temptation that comes upon all the world, Jacob’s trouble, and they will awake to everlasting life. That is why we do not grieve the righteous the way the world does.

precepts.why:

Obama did it secretly: he went and killed Gaddafi, who was trying to uplift the people of Libya, and nobody said a word because Obama was a black man. Trump does it openly. “Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him”. God says the white man’s soul is not right, and some of you want to save him. “He is a proud man”: see how Trump talks proud and arrogant. “Neither keepeth at home”: America is never in its own country; it has military bases all over the earth, in everybody’s country, dictating and oppressing. “Who enlargeth his desire as hell, and is as death”: wherever he goes the people catch hell, and he brings death.

precepts.why:
“After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number”. Now that we are bringing this out, the churches say we are all included, all backgrounds and cultures together. Where was that in 1964? Where was it on the slave ships? That is why the Bible says precept must be upon precept, line upon line, here a little and there a little.

Hosea 1:10: “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered”. That is us. The multitude “which no man could number” is the children of Israel, whose number cannot be measured nor numbered.

“And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” The people told they were not God’s people are the same ones called the sons of the living God.

It also shows time has gone by. Moses said “ye shall be left few in number among the heathen”, because they were killing us; Hosea says we would grow to be like the sand of the sea. That is the great multitude standing before the throne.

precepts.label: Acts 2:5
precepts.why:
The great multitude is “of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues”, and the Christian says, see, we are all included. But read Acts 2:5: “And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.”

Out of every nation under heaven, and they were Jews. So “all nations” in Revelation 7:9 does not mean every race; it means the Israelites scattered into every nation, gathered out of them.

That is the all nations of Revelation 7:9: Jews out of every nation under heaven, the same people as the sand of the sea that cannot be numbered, standing before the throne and before the Lamb.

precepts.label: Isaiah 11:10-12
precepts.why:
If you have time on the street, add Isaiah 11: “the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people”. Why the second time? Because the first time was under Moses.

He recovers the remnant “from Assyria”, modern-day Turkey, where you have the Afro-Turks; “and from Egypt”, lower Egypt and the Afro-Egyptians; “and from Pathros”, modern-day southern Sudan; “and from Cush”, Ethiopia; “and from Elam”, Iran and India, with the Afro-Iranians, the Siddis and the Dalits; “and from Shinar”, Iraq today and the Afro-Iraqis; “and from Hamath”, Syria today and the Afro-Syrians; “and from the islands of the sea”, like Cape Verde, the Hawaiian islands and the Melanesian islands.

“And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” We are the outcasts of Israel.

That is the all nations right there: the remnant of Israel gathered out of every land they were scattered to, the great multitude of Revelation 7:9.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 2:38-42
precepts.why:
Revelation 7:4 gives “an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel”, and then verse 9 gives the great multitude. They say, see, we are all included. Ezra explains it crystal clear.

“Arise up and stand, behold the number of those that be sealed in the feast of the Lord”. The number of thy children, whom thou longedst for, is fulfilled”. Verses 38 to 41 are Revelation 7:4.

Now verse 42: “I Esdras saw upon the mount Sion a great people, whom I could not number, and they all praised the Lord with songs.” That is Revelation 7:9. The great multitude is Zion, mount Zion.

So the 144,000 are the men, the Israelite leaders of the twelve tribes; the great multitude are more men, women and children of Israel. And “these are they which came out of great tribulation”: so much for the church teaching that we don’t have to go through tribulation.

precepts.label: Isaiah 24:21
precepts.why:
This proves who the heavens are in Revelation 12:12. “And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall punish the host of the high ones that are on high”. The high ones that are on high are the ones ruling the earth today: America and Europe. They are the fourth beast, the red dragon, the spiritual wickedness in high places. The Lord shall punish them for all the evil they are doing, and with them the Europeans living in the land of Israel that say they are Jews.

Then: “and the kings of the earth upon the earth.” The kings of the earth are Iran, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, India, Pakistan, Ethiopia, Sudan. God is going to punish the high ones on high, and he is also going to punish those kings of the earth.

So Revelation 12:12 lines up with it. “rejoice, ye heavens, and ye that dwell in them” is spoken to the high ones: rejoice now, this is your kingdom, have fun. “Woe to the inhabiters of the earth” is spoken to the kings of the earth, the nations below, Iran, Saudi Arabia, Ethiopia, India, China. The devil comes down on them with great wrath, and in that day the Lord punishes both.

precepts.label: Isaiah 34:5
precepts.why:
A second witness that the heavens are Europe and America. “For my sword shall be bathed in heaven”. That is the Lord, Christ, and it does not mean his sword is up in the sky; the verse goes on to explain who the heaven is: “behold, it shall come down upon Idumea”.

Idumea is Edom, and Edom today is Europe and America and those Europeans in the land of Israel that call themselves Jews. The sword is bathed in heaven, that is the high ones, and it comes down upon Idumea, so the heaven is the Europeans.

“and upon the people of my curse, to judgment.” God has cursed the white man; he has cursed the Europeans. That is why they have no pigment in their skin. And the sword comes down upon them to judgment: God is going to judge the high ones that are on high.

So when Revelation 12:12 says “Therefore rejoice, ye heavens”, the heavens are Edom. Rejoice now, this is your kingdom, have fun, because the sword that is bathed in heaven is coming down on you to judgment.

precepts.label: Job 20:24-27
precepts.why:
This explains the woe to the inhabiters of the earth. “He shall flee from the iron weapon, and the bow of steel shall strike him through.” He is America. The iron weapon is the missile, ballistic missiles, nuclear missiles, and the bow of steel is nuclear weapons. “It is drawn, and cometh out of the body; yea, the glittering sword cometh out of his gall”: it is called a glittering sword because that is what the missiles look like when they are shooting.

“The heaven shall reveal his iniquity”. That is what you are seeing right now: the Lord is revealing the wickedness America is doing on the earth. “and the earth shall rise up against him.” The high ones on high will be oppressing the nations on the earth; they will oppress Iran, they will oppress Saudi Arabia, they will oppress all nations, and even Europe is going to get it too. And as they do that, all the kings of the earth are going to rise up against America and Israel because of that oppression.

What you see now is the beginning, and it is going to get worse. Many are hailing Iran for shooting missiles, but America could drop one of its crazy bombs, not even the nuclear one, and Iran would be done. Yet Iran will not be fully taken out, and there will be no regime change. The people of Iran will hate America even more; there will be a truce, not peace, after America bombs their nuclear sites, and according to prophecy they will rebuild it all. The powers that be think they are buying time, but the Lord is behind all of it.

That is the great wrath of Revelation 12:12. The devil comes down on the inhabiters of the earth because he knows his time is short. Every move he makes is to buy time and prolong his rule, because in his mind his house will go on forever: make sure the Arabs never come together, make sure Iran never gets nuclear capability, and bomb them. And once he finishes with the nations he is coming for us, the leaders in IUIC, to stop us from prophesying and testifying, because when we testify against him, judgment comes. They are already putting the laws in place.

precepts.label: Revelation 13:5-6
precepts.why:
“And the serpent cast out of his mouth water as a flood after the woman”. His mouth is the media, America’s media, and every single aspect of it is so-called Jewish owned; Amalek controls all the media, and Trump wants to control the whole of it. The water out of the serpent’s mouth is lies. The woman is our people, and the flood is to draw as many of the twelve tribes of Israel as they can into their Christian or democratic lies. That is their agenda.

Revelation 13 describes that mouth: “And there was given unto him a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies; and power was given unto him to continue forty and two months. And he opened his mouth in blasphemy against God, to blaspheme his name, and his tabernacle, and them that dwell in heaven.”

In the time of Rome they had written media, pamphlets they sent out everywhere. It started with Rome; the Americans have it top-notch today, and their messages go out worldwide. That mouth speaking great things and blasphemies is the same mouth casting out the flood after the woman.

precepts.label: Daniel 7:11
precepts.why:
Daniel saw it too: “I beheld then because of the voice of the great words which the horn spake”. Write this down: the horn is America. The voice is their media today, and it goes worldwide; even in Cuba there was American news on certain channels.

“I beheld even till the beast was slain, and his body destroyed, and given to the burning flame.” Now he calls the horn the beast, and it is destined to be destroyed. Revelation 18:8 is the precept: “Therefore shall her plagues come in one day, death, and mourning, and famine; and she shall be utterly burned with fire: for strong is the Lord God who judgeth her.” That is the body given to the burning flame.

“And the kings of the earth, who have committed fornication and lived deliciously with her, shall bewail her, and lament for her, when they shall see the smoke of her burning”. They will cry for this horn, this America.

So the mouth that casts out the flood after the woman is the same voice of great words that brings the beast to the burning flame.

precepts.label: Daniel 7:25
precepts.why:
“And he shall speak great words against the most High”: through their media, the same blasphemies we read in Revelation 13.

“And shall wear out the saints of the most High”. How did they wear us out? In slavery: shackles on our necks, our hands and our ankles; buck breaking; working seven days a week from sunup to sundown. That is what wearing out the saints means.

“And think to change times and laws”: the daylight saving time we just entered; laws like same-sex marriage; our Sabbath changed to Sunday.

“And they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time”: 250 years. What we need to see in this verse is that he speaks great words against the Most High, and that is their media, the mouth of the serpent casting its flood of lies after the woman.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 51:54-57
precepts.why:
“A sound of a cry cometh from Babylon, and great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans”. Babylon here is America, and the Chaldeans are modern Israel today. The Chaldeans were always an ally to Babylon: ancient Babylon were Kushites and the Chaldeans Semites, so brought up to today, America is Babylon and the Israelis are the Chaldeans.

“Because the Lord hath spoiled Babylon, and destroyed out of her the great voice”. What is the great voice? Their media, which goes worldwide and captivates and hypnotizes people everywhere. “When her waves do roar like great waters, a noise of their voice is uttered”: the waves are the nations within her.

“Because the spoiler is come upon her, even upon Babylon”, as we read in Habakkuk, “and her mighty men are taken”, as prisoners of war, “every one of their bows is broken: for the Lord God of recompences shall surely requite.”

“And I will make drunk her princes, and her wise men, her captains”, the admirals and generals, “and her rulers”, the governors and mayors, “and her mighty men”, the soldiers: “and they shall sleep a perpetual sleep, and not wake”. That perpetual sleep is the lake of fire; they are never waking up again. So the serpent’s mouth, the great voice, will be destroyed out of her.

precepts.label: Isaiah 17:12-13
precepts.why:
Jeremiah 51:55 says “when her waves do roar like great waters, a noise of their voice is uttered”. The waves that roar are the nations, and Isaiah 17 is the precept that proves it.

“Woe to the multitude of many people, which make a noise like the noise of the seas; and to the rushing of nations, that make a rushing like the rushing of mighty waters!” The nations are the waters, making a noise like the seas.

“The nations shall rush like the rushing of many waters: but God shall rebuke them, and they shall flee far off, and shall be chased as the chaff of the mountains before the wind, and like a rolling thing before the whirlwind.”

So the waters in these prophecies are peoples and nations. The waves roaring within Babylon are the nations inside her, and however they rush, God will rebuke them and chase them like chaff before the wind.

precepts.label: 2 Maccabees 9:9
precepts.why:
The first vial brings “a noisome and grievous sore.” Noisome means foul smelling, harmful, noxious, extremely offensive to the senses, particularly the smell: a real nasty sore. It is the same plague that came on ancient Egypt, a boil breaking forth upon man and upon beast throughout all the land.

The record shows what noisome looks like on a man. When the Lord struck the wicked king Antiochus, “the worms rose up out of the body of this wicked man, and whiles he lived in sorrow and pain, his flesh fell away, and the filthiness of his smell was noisome to all his army.” His flesh fell off him and his stink offended his whole army.

What could make a man get like that? A nuclear bomb explosion causes severe radiation burns, known as cutaneous radiation injury, that frequently lead to intense itching, blistering and open sores. The burns come in stages: first redness and swelling, then a latent phase, then severe blistering and deep, long lasting necrotic ulcers. When a nuclear bomb goes off and the blast does not kill you, you are going to be rotten, your skin falling off, and it is going to be noisome.

That is how we know this first plague belongs to that one hour, when the destruction comes on America, modern day Egypt: the same kind of sore that ate Antiochus alive falls on the men who have the mark of the beast.

precepts.label: Psalms 91:1-3
precepts.why:
The key thing in the verse is who the sore falls on: “upon the men which had the mark of the beast, and upon them which worshipped his image.” If it is only them, where are we? What happened to us? We are delivered.

Psalms 91 explains why. “He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.” If you dwell in the secret place of the Most High, you dwell in his shadow, meaning his protection. “I will say of the Lord, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust.”

“Surely he shall deliver thee from the snare of the fowler, and from the noisome pestilence.” That is the first plague, the noisome pestilence, and the Lord will deliver you from it. That is why the scripture says the plague fell only on those that worship the beast and have his mark: because we are delivered.

This plague is coming in that one hour, and in that one hour, when the bombs are falling, it is not going to come near us. The radioactive waves, the noisome pestilence, the poisoned water will not touch us, because the Lord is going to deliver us up out of here. The same pestilence that destroys America passes over the people who dwell under his shadow.

precepts.why:
The three unclean spirits like frogs come “out of the mouth of the dragon, and out of the mouth of the beast, and out of the mouth of the false prophet.” Those three unclean spirits are politics, religion and finance. To see the first of them, go to the beast of Revelation 13.

John says, “I beheld another beast coming up out of the earth; and he had two horns like a lamb, and he spake as a dragon.” Those two horns like a lamb are the two political parties, the Democrats and the Republicans: two political systems that look gentle like a lamb. But he speaks as a dragon.

That is the politics, the frog that comes out of the mouth of the dragon. And what comes out of a mouth? Communication, and that communication is propaganda, persuasion and lies. These are “the spirits of devils”, and they do not stay at home: they “go forth unto the kings of the earth and of the whole world”, gathering them “to the battle of that great day of God Almighty.”

precepts.label: Revelation 13:16-17
precepts.why:
The second frog comes “out of the mouth of the beast.” Go back to Revelation 13: “he causeth all, both small and great, rich and poor, free and bond, to receive a mark in their right hand, or in their foreheads: And that no man might buy or sell, save he that had the mark, or the name of the beast, or the number of his name.”

That no man might buy or sell: that is the finance, one of the three unclean spirits like frogs, alongside the politics and the religion.

It is coming to a time where, if you are not in cahoots with, in support of, or in allegiance with what America pushes, you will not be able to buy or sell. On a large scale that is trade between nations, but it is also the regular buying and selling of everyday life. That is why they are trying to do away with the currency as it is now and bring everything into a digital system: to monitor God's people who speak up against this society.

The third frog, out of the mouth of the false prophet, is Christianity, their religion and their religious systems. Politics, finance and religion together are the spirits of devils working miracles, going out to the kings of the whole world, not only here at home.

classes.title: Civil War & the Son of Perdition

precepts.label: Revelation 11:8
precepts.why:
“And the great city was divided into three parts”. What is the great city? Revelation 11:8 answers: “their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.” That great city, spiritually Sodom and Egypt, is America.

So the great city was divided. Remember what Christ says: any kingdom divided against itself shall fall. Before God pours “the cup of the wine of the fierceness of his wrath” on Babylon, something has to happen first: the great city is divided into three parts, “and the cities of the nations fell.” There will be civil war here first; then God is going to destroy this place.

The fifth vial comes before it: poured “upon the seat of the beast; and his kingdom was full of darkness”. The seat of the beast is America, and that darkness is not only sin, adultery and fornication. It is debt, sedition, division, civil war, violence, and the saints being killed here too. “They gnawed their tongues for pain, And blasphemed the God of heaven because of their pains and their sores, and repented not of their deeds.” Their own citizens they are going to be killing, and still they will not repent.

Then “every island fled away, and the mountains were not found. And there fell upon men a great hail out of heaven”. That great hail is nuclear ballistic missiles, looking like hail coming down from heaven: America destroyed with nuclear destruction. So prepare for what is coming. Civil war is coming to this place.
