precepts.label: Habakkuk 2:5
precepts.why:
“I will shew unto thee the judgment of the great whore that sitteth upon many waters”. There is a judgment coming to this place, and nobody wants it judged. Their inward thought is that this kingdom lasts forever. The pride in Esau’s heart says we are in the perfect geographical location, nobody can attack us; meanwhile they go destroy a country and then bring the same people they destroyed over here.

Who sits upon many waters? Put up the map of the US military bases: 845 and more. Who has their navy in everybody’s water, their submarines everywhere? Babylon the great is a world-reaching power over many peoples, nations and tongues, with global influence. The US has launched 469 military interventions since 1798, 251 since 1991. You cannot tell me Babylon is not America.

Habakkuk describes him: “because he transgresseth by wine, he is a proud man, neither keepeth at home, who enlargeth his desire as hell”. He never stays at home. In Vietnam he did the My Lai massacre, murdering hundreds of women, children and old men, raping children as young as twelve, and his Agent Orange still kills people to this day. Look at Iraq; look at Libya, where they are selling Black people for five hundred dollars and no pastor says a word; look at Palestine; look at the proxy war in Ukraine, pumping in billions of weapons. Everywhere he goes he destabilizes the country and it becomes hell.

That is not Saudi Arabia, not the Chinese, not the East Indians. No other nation has that kind of global reach. And he “cannot be satisfied, but gathereth unto him all nations, and heapeth unto him all people”. Now the world is shifting to many powers, China and Russia rising, and this place is prophesied to fall. So prepare yourselves, mentally, physically and spiritually: this is war.

classes.title: The Divine Orchestration and Purpose of the People You Encounter

precepts.label: Obadiah 1:15-17
precepts.why:
“And I saw the woman drunken with the blood of the saints, and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus”. The woman is Babylon the Great, America, and the martyrs of Jesus are the Israelites: those who stand up for this truth all the way up to the threat of death and beyond it. Many of us are going to get killed. They drank our blood by putting us in captivity and dealing evil with us.

Obadiah explains that drinking: “For the day of the Lord is near upon all the heathen: as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head.” The reward of what the nations did to us is coming back on them. “For as ye have drunk upon my holy mountain”: what did they drink upon us? Captivity, slavery, rape, robbery, murder, lies, rigged juries, castrations, lynchings, railroading; the Rasheem Carters, the Kendrick Johnsons.

“So shall all the heathen drink continually, yea, they shall drink, and they shall swallow down”. All the nations that did this to God’s people will drink the captivity, the slavery, the whipped backs, the lynchings, and digest it. “And they shall be as though they had not been.” They dehumanized us until we do not even recognize we were once a great people, reduced us to nothing, when we are the jewels of God. So they will be reduced to nothing, as Isaiah 14:21 cuts off their name.

“But upon mount Zion shall be deliverance, and there shall be holiness; and the house of Jacob shall possess their possessions.” Deliverance is for the ones of us that repent and stop BSing. The ones who do not repent and keep up the BS, the Most High is going to wipe out along with our enemies.

precepts.label: Isaiah 13:5
precepts.why:
“The beast that thou sawest was, and is not; and shall ascend out of the bottomless pit, and go into perdition”. It was in John’s vision but not in his time. When it came, it came out of Europe, Great Britain to be exact. And it shall go into perdition, destruction. That is where we are now; that is what this war is signifying.

The weapons to do it are already here. You don’t have to wonder where the fire is going to come from. The Lord will come with fire because he is coming with those weapons; he is going to be literally riding on the weapons being fired, and coming with something like two hundred million angels. That is what Isaiah 13:5 says: the Lord and the weapons of his indignation come from a far country, “to destroy the whole land”, the whole land, singular.

That fire is the perdition of Babylon the Great; that is what the beast is going to get. And “they that dwell on the earth shall wonder, whose names were not written in the book of life”. They have no clue that this is Babylon the Great, and they are not getting the kingdom, no matter how many churches they set up.

Every time you pray the Lord’s prayer, thy kingdom come, thy will be done in earth, you are advocating for the destruction of this kingdom. Christ is not setting his kingdom beside this one. The King of kings is coming to topple it with the weapons of his indignation.

precepts.label: Revelation 18:1-4
precepts.why:
Revelation 17 ends with the woman: “the waters which thou sawest, where the whore sitteth, are peoples, and multitudes, and nations, and tongues.” Put up the Statue of Liberty: Lady Liberty sits upon many waters; she is everywhere. The ten horns, Belgium, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Germany, the United Kingdom, Italy, Greece, France, Denmark and Ireland, “shall hate the whore, and shall make her desolate and naked, and shall eat her flesh, and burn her with fire.” It will be an ambush; the entire country will be destroyed. “And the woman which thou sawest is that great city, which reigneth over the kings of the earth.” We call it a country; God calls it a great city. Nobody dominates America; America reigns over everybody.

Then chapter 18 opens right after: “Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird.” Why does it say fallen twice? Because Israel is the little Babylon.

“For all nations have drunk of the wine of the wrath of her fornication”: her policies, the same thing Daniel 8 says, that through his policy he shall cause craft to prosper. All nations follow their policies. “And the kings of the earth have committed fornication with her”: the nations got in bed with her. “And the merchants of the earth”, the corporations and companies, “are waxed rich through the abundance of her delicacies.”

“Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.” That lets you know where the Israelites are: in Babylon. They say Babylon is Iraq. No, no, no: it is letting you know the twelve tribes are here.

precepts.label: Sirach 10:9
precepts.why:
“And the merchants of the earth shall weep and mourn over her; for no man buyeth their merchandise any more”. The merchants are the corporations that make major deals with countries. The gold, silver and precious stones come this way by ship in those big containers, and the majority of what is listed comes from the continent of Africa. Then: “and slaves”: that was you and me. “And souls of men”: you want a piece of the pie, you have to sell your soul. There are things you must do.

Ecclesiasticus says it: “Why is earth and ashes proud?” Earth and ashes represents man; why is man proud? “There is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man”. They covet what does not belong to them. If you are covetous, you want a piece of the American pie, those billions of dollars in contracts. “For such an one setteth his own soul to sale; because while he liveth he casteth away his bowels.” While he lives he casts away his bowels, the lower intestine, the rectum.

You think Oprah got all that money just because she was a great talk show host? You think LeBron and these athletes got those contracts because nobody is as good as them? Michael Jai White is a good actor, but there are certain things he said he is not going to do, so he does not get those contracts. Ye said, if you see a video of me with a goat, because he knew what they held over him. They have something on all of them. The model from our Houston school, the Black Starlet who found a line of producers at the door: to get the contract you cast away your bowels.

That is why Paul says “they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.” Covetousness is the last of the ten commandments, and it starts in the mind; covet and you will steal, steal and you will lie, and it goes on to murder. The fear that keeps them from repenting is being publicly humiliated for what they did to get their fortunes, the way they destroyed Wendy Williams. But the Lord can still preserve the soul: come out of that lifestyle.

classes.title: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:48
precepts.why:
Babylon's merchandise runs from “gold, and silver, and precious stones” down to “slaves, and souls of men.” The tin, the copper, the iron, the rubber, the bauxite, the slaves and the cheap labor have all been taken out of our countries. These countries are not underdeveloped; they are overexploited. They all should be rich countries, world powers, with the blessings the Lord gave us in those places. It was done in Latin America and in Africa, especially the west coast where we are dispersed, and the slave routes and trade routes were the commerce they made of us.

The way they keep that dominance today is economic, backed by the threat of military power, and it follows a pattern, as with Noriega and now Maduro. First they criminalize the leader with drug, terror and corruption narratives, framing mischief by a law. Then they declare the regime illegitimate. Then they apply sanctions and economic siege. Then they isolate the country diplomatically and militarily, remove or extract the leadership, and install or manage a transition authority.

The sanctions are the modern face of Deuteronomy 28:48, for those who say the curses were only for back then or only for the time of the conquistadors: “Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things”. Want of all things because of sanctions and their economic might. If you try to nationalize your resources or do things outside of their money, even though you have your own resources you are overexploited to the point that you cannot do it on your own. There is no might in your hand.

“and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” A lot of times we did this willingly. It is the same pattern we followed with Assyria and Egypt: when the United States became a world power we leaned on them, and found out really quick that they do not keep their word on anything. It is history repeating itself, the doctrine of the scripture executed over and over again.

precepts.label: Revelation 2:9
precepts.why:
“I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich).” First and foremost, the riches are the promise of the kingdom of heaven. Unto us pertain the promises, the law, the adoption of sons, all of it; we are the ones Christ died for. That is the true riches.

But Revelation 18 gives it a new spin. Babylon trades in gold, silver, precious stones, fine wood, iron and marble, and these come out of our lands. So-called third world countries are rich with resources; it is the people who are poor, because they are overexploited. What a distinction. The countries of Israel are not underdeveloped, and the poverty of our people sits on top of the riches of our lands.

“and I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.” Those who say they are Jews and are not are part of the same machine working to oppress our people, and it is the same playbook of sanctions, isolation and regime change that runs through the whole system.

So Revelation 2:9 stands beside Revelation 18:12: the merchants of Babylon grow rich off the goods of the lands where Israel is scattered, while Israel lives in tribulation and poverty, though rich in the promises and in the land itself.

classes.title: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.label: Jude 1:14-15
precepts.why:
“He that sat upon him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war.” His vesture is “dipped in blood” because the Lord will be warring; enough nations are going to be slaughtered. “And the armies which were in heaven followed him upon white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean.” When Christ comes back, he is coming back with armies. You think he is coming back to kiss and shake hands? No. He is coming back for war, for deliverance, for vengeance.

So who are those armies that follow him? Jude answers: “And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints”. That is the armies: the saints in the white robes, the 144,000. Christ is coming back with his top Gs: the brothers that loved not their lives unto the death, that received their immortal body, clothed in fine linen, white and clean. They are coming back with the Lord for vengeance.

“To execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds which they have ungodly committed, and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.” All the hard speeches they have spoken against the Lord: the Lord is coming for vengeance.

Then “out of his mouth goeth a sharp sword, that with it he should smite the nations”. He is not using a literal weapon; he is using his words, and he is not coming to save the nations but to destroy them. The beast, America and Europe, and the kings of the earth will really believe they can gather their armies and fight against him and against his army of saints.

thread.label: Revelation 19:10
thread.text: And I fell at his feet to worship him. And he said unto me, See thou do it not: I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren that have the testimony of Jesus: worship God: for the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of proph

classes.title: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.label: Revelation 22:8-9
precepts.why:
John says it twice. In Revelation 19 he fell at the angel's feet, and here again: “I John saw these things, and heard them. And when I had heard and seen, I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel which shewed me these things.”

And the angel says the same thing again: “See thou do it not: for I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren the prophets, and of them which keep the sayings of this book: worship God.” He will not take worship, because he is not God. He is a fellowservant, one of the brethren.

That is who the angels are: our brothers. They are not demons. They ate with Lot because they have mouths just like us, and they were going to lie down because they look like us. Esau calls them humanoids, and to Esau they are going to be some demons, but those are our brothers. The angels have tribes too, and in Revelation 21, do not be surprised if the angels standing at the twelve gates are each standing at the gate of their own tribe.

precepts.label: Tobit 5:12-14
precepts.why:
Here Raphael, before he makes himself known, presents himself to Tobit another way: “I am Azarias, the son of Ananias the great, and of thy brethren.” An angel of God naming himself as one of the brethren, just as the angel told John, “I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren.”

Tobit answers, “Thou art welcome, brother; be not now angry with me, because I have enquired to know thy tribe and thy family; for thou art my brother, of an honest and good stock.” Tobit asks after his tribe and his family, and receives him as a brother.

He knows his people: “I know Ananias and Jonathas, sons of that great Samaias, as we went together to Jerusalem to worship, and offered the firstborn, and the tenths of the fruits; and they were not seduced with the error of our brethren: my brother, thou art of a good stock.”

So the angel who walked with Tobit's son was taken for an Israelite brother, of a tribe and a family. That is how close the angels are to us: they look like us, they have tribes too, and they are our brethren.

precepts.label: Tobit 12:15
precepts.why:
Now Raphael makes himself known: “I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels, which present the prayers of the saints, and which go in and out before the glory of the Holy One.” The one Tobit called brother, Azarias of his brethren, was the angel all along.

Why do the angels present the prayers of the saints? Because they minister unto us. They are ministering spirits working on our behalf, because those are our brothers.

They are not demonic spirits sent here to oppose the people that inhabit this place called the United Snakes of America. That is untrue. That is popular persuasion; that is lies. The world is being taught to call what comes out of the heavens demons and fallen angels, so that it will gather to fight against Christ and his army. But the angels are our brethren, fellowservants who keep the testimony of Jesus, and we worship God alone.

thread.label: Revelation 19:11-20
thread.text: And I saw heaven opened, and behold a white horse; and he that sat upon him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war.

classes.title: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.label: Isaiah 47:3
precepts.why:
The armies in heaven follow Christ “upon white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean.” That fine linen, white and clean, is the immortal body. To prove it, go to Isaiah, speaking to Babylon: “Thy nakedness shall be uncovered, yea, thy shame shall be seen: I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man.”

Christ said he is going to take vengeance, and he will not meet Babylon as a man. Christ is coming back with that immortal body. You will not be able to nail him back to the cross like you did in Jerusalem.

That is what the white horse and the fine linen, white and clean, make reference to. And he comes to make war, because God is a man of war: “in righteousness he doth judge and make war.” His vesture is dipped in blood, because there is going to be a lot of bloodshed, a lot of killing. On his head are many crowns, because he is going to take everyone's crowns and be the one King, “KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS.”

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 5:1-6
precepts.why:
Revelation says the beast and the kings of the earth and their armies were gathered together to make war against him that sits on the horse. Wisdom shows what happens when they see him: “Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.” That is us, the Israelites, standing before Esau and the nations, who made no account of our labours here.

“When they see it, they shall be troubled with terrible fear, and shall be amazed at the strangeness of his salvation, so far beyond all that they looked for.” The strangeness of his salvation is the chariots, us being taken up. That is going to be strange and foreign to them. They will no longer talk about the deliverance out of Egypt, but about the new deliverance from the land of the north. A black God, a black Christ, coming to redeem his black people: that is going to be the new talk of the town.

“And they repenting and groaning for anguish of spirit shall say within themselves, This was he, whom we had sometimes in derision, and a proverb of reproach.” Christ is going to put it in their mind: these are the people you afflicted, raped, robbed, murdered and enslaved. These are my people.

“We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour: How is he numbered among the children of God, and his lot is among the saints! Therefore have we erred from the way of truth.”

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 13:1-11
precepts.why:
Revelation says the armies were gathered together to make war against him that sat on the horse and against his army. Ezra saw that same war. “there arose a wind from the sea”, and “that man waxed strong with the thousands of heaven: and when he turned his countenance to look, all the things trembled.” The man that came out of the sea is Christ, with the thousands of heaven, the armies that follow him.

And “whensoever the voice went out of his mouth, all they burned that heard his voice, like as the earth faileth when it feeleth the fire.” He speaks the laws out of his mouth, and the people just disintegrate, because they are guilty of that law. That is the sharp sword out of his mouth in Revelation, the laws of God.

Then “there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea”. They will have one consent, because the Most High is going to harden them like he did Pharaoh. And the popular persuasion is already laying the groundwork: let's all come together and fight the demons coming from space.

After this, “all they which were gathered together to subdue him were sore afraid, and yet durst fight.” Scared to death, but the Most High moves them. As Romans 9 shows, he built them up, just like ancient Egypt: Babylon the Great, this white man, this Edomite, built up just to be destroyed, made to fight against him.

And “he neither lifted up his hand, nor held sword, nor any instrument of war”, but sent out of his mouth “a blast of fire”, “a flaming breath”, and “sparks and tempests”, and “burned them up every one, so that upon a sudden of an innumerable multitude nothing was to be perceived, but only dust and smell of smoke.” Ashes to ashes, and dust to dust.

thread.label: Revelation 19:12-13
thread.text: His eyes were as a flame of fire, and on his head were many crowns; and he had a name written, that no man knew, but he himself.

classes.title: Wars Are Here: Seek Good Not Evil

precepts.label: Revelation 1:1
precepts.why:
“His eyes were as a flame of fire, and on his head were many crowns; and he had a name written, that no man knew, but he himself.” No man knew it but he himself, so what are you tripping about, YHWH, Yahawashi, Jesus Christ? We are English speakers; we learned Jesus Christ. Call him what you call him, but we have to keep the commandments.

“And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God.” Why is his vesture dipped in blood? Because Christ is about righteous destruction; you read that in Isaiah 63. The Lord is a man of war. We serve a terrible God, and a merciful one, and he is going to use these nations to create a final battle.

They stand “afar off for the fear of her torment, saying, Alas, alas, that great city Babylon, that mighty city! for in one hour is thy judgment come.” It is the same wording as Esdras: the smoke going up, and those about her bewailing her. And Revelation 18 comes right after the chapter 17 we read, where the great whore and the city are shown.

Then “they that remain under her shall do service unto them that have put her in fear”: they become prisoners of war. That is the end of Babylon, America.

thread.label: 2 Esdras 16:68-70
thread.text: For, behold, the burning wrath of a great multitude is kindled over you, and they shall take away certain of you, and feed you, being idle, with things offered unto idols.

precepts.label: Sirach 33:27
precepts.why:
“For, behold, the burning wrath of a great multitude is kindled over you”. That great multitude is what Christ said: you shall be hated of all nations for my name's sake. And “they shall take away certain of you, and feed you, being idle”. Idle, i-d-l-e: a person avoiding work; lazy, indolent, slothful, workshy, shiftless, loafing; without purpose or effect, pointless.

In this truth, if you are idle you are avoiding work. Not work in the world: God's work. You are lazy in this truth. You have no purpose; you are just here. Some of you have been here for years and you have no office, doing nothing. You are idle.

“Send him to labour, that he be not idle; for idleness teacheth much evil.” Brothers and sisters, when you are idle in the truth, you are learning evil. That is why you spend your time on porn, smoking cigarettes, smoking weed, hitting women up in their DMs. You have idle time, and there is a whole lot of work in this truth to be done.

We can spot that idleness as soon as you come in: the one who sits down and just looks around, looking at the women's side, taking no notes. If this means something to you, you are engulfed in it; you are writing things down and trying to put it to memory. The idle are the certain ones the multitude will take away and feed.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 4:1-5
precepts.why:
The idle will be fed “with things offered unto idols.” Idols in the Bible are statues, figurines, golden calves, and also money, career and power that compete with God for worship. So what is the most idolatrous religion here in America? Christianity. You may think that is biased; Paul identifies the religion.

“Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils”. This is the latter times. Why will some give heed to seducing spirits? Because you are idle; you have idle time. “Speaking lies in hypocrisy”: I believe in God, but I am not going to do anything the Bible says. “having their conscience seared with a hot iron; Forbidding to marry”: what religion forbids men to marry? Catholics; that is Christianity. “and commanding to abstain from meats”: who cannot eat meat for 40 days? Catholics; they call it Lent.

Those meats “God hath created to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth”, and the truth is God's law. “For every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving: For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” Where is the food sanctified by the word of God? Leviticus 11.

The Roman Catholic Church is the mother church of every Protestant denomination on the tree: Orthodox, Jehovah's Witness, Presbyterian, Lutheran, Methodist, Episcopalian, Mormon, Evangelical, Pentecostal, Baptist, Adventist, Anglican, all the way to Christian nationalism. That is the idolatry the multitude will feed the idle, and they are already saying out loud that they are going to impose it on this country.

precepts.label: Revelation 13:6-8
precepts.why:
What do all those churches have in common? They worship the image of the beast. “And he opened his mouth in blasphemy against God, to blaspheme his name, and his tabernacle, and them that dwell in heaven.” Their blasphemy is the perversion of the gospel of Christ, the perversion of the truth.

“And it was given unto him to make war with the saints, and to overcome them”. Esau made war with us: Rome, Spain, Portugal. Pope Nicholas V made that edict to enslave us and force us into Christianity. And they overcame us; they enslaved us. “and power was given him over all kindreds, and tongues, and nations.”

“And all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him”: the same man that overcame us. A book published in 1920, The Pillory, the Tale of the Borgia Pope, says it is an open secret that Cesare Borgia, son of Pope Alexander, posed for the image of Jesus. Salvatore, the savior: that is Cesare Borgia. Even Muslims will tell you that image is Jesus; ask a Buddhist and he will say the same. Everybody acknowledges it as Jesus the Christ.

All that worship him are those “whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.” That is the idol the multitude will feed to the idle.

precepts.label: Revelation 12:17
precepts.why:
In every place and in the next cities there shall be “a great insurrection upon those that fear the Lord.” Revelation shows who is behind it: “And the dragon was wroth with the woman, and went to make war with the remnant of her seed, which keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.”

The dragon is wroth: our enemies see us and they are angry. That is why in France they already said, shut down IUIC; a black Jesus, the Israelites, that is anti-semitic, we cannot allow this to go on. And he went to make war with the remnant: that is physical war, not only spiritual. That is tribulation, Jacob's trouble, persecution against those who keep the commandments and the testimony of Jesus Christ.

Christ warned of the same: “Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name's sake. And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.” You say you would never consent to their religion, but a whip across your back will change some of you, and you will be compelled to blaspheme.

And those who consent will be had in derision. Nobody likes a traitor. Like the apes in Planet of the Apes who betrayed their own and wore the word donkey before they were killed, Esau will use you and get rid of you. The ones who keep the commandments and the testimony are the ones the dragon makes war with; that is why Christ said, if they persecute you in this city, flee to the next.

thread.label: 2 Esdras 16:68-73
thread.text: For, behold, the burning wrath of a great multitude is kindled over you, and they shall take away certain of you, and feed you, being idle, with things offered unto idols.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 4:1-3
precepts.why:
The great multitude “shall take away certain of you, and feed you, being idle, with things offered unto idols.” What does that mean? It is talking about Christianity. If you are idle, they are going to feed you Christianity. How do we know? Paul prophesied it: “Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils”.

We already know some of you are going to depart from this faith. Why? Because persecution is coming, and when you cannot pay your bills and cannot get food, you will leave. America wants to bring in digital currency so they can control us. In China, if you jaywalk, they take money out of your account; imagine being told you may not teach the gospel or gather on the seventh day, and when we do it anyway, your digital bank account is hit.

What is the doctrine of devils? Paul explains it: “Speaking lies in hypocrisy; having their conscience seared with a hot iron; Forbidding to marry, and commanding to abstain from meats”. What religion forbids men to marry? Catholicism, Christianity. Commanding to abstain from meats: that is Lent, no meat for 40 days. That is the food offered to idols: Christianity, Roman Catholicism.

Why will they feed it to you? Because you do not study. When persecution comes, you are fearful, you cannot endure to the end, so you give up and betray the King of kings. And “they that consent unto them shall be had in derision and in reproach, and trodden under foot.” Even the white man hates a traitor. In the Planet of the Apes the apes who betrayed their own wore the word donkey on their backs, and when they were no longer needed, they were killed. Then you face the King, and the lake of fire. But those who endure, “Then shall they be known, who are my chosen; and they shall be tried as the gold in the fire.”

thread.label: 2 Esdras 16:71-78
thread.text: They shall be like mad men, sparing none, but still spoiling and destroying those that fear the Lord.

precepts.label: 1 Maccabees 1:41-50
precepts.why:
“They shall be like mad men, sparing none, but still spoiling and destroying those that fear the Lord.” We read the book of Acts and think that could never happen again, but Paul himself said, “being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.” The prophecy says it is going to happen again, and it happened under the Greeks too.

“Moreover king Antiochus wrote to his whole kingdom, that all should be one people, And every one should leave his laws: so all the heathen agreed according to the commandment of the king. Yea, many also of the Israelites consented to his religion, and sacrificed unto idols, and profaned the sabbath.” That is what is going to happen again. It happened in the time of Paul, in the time of the Maccabees, in Babylon when they tried to get us to worship the false god. That which has been is that which shall be; there is no new thing under the sun. Idolatry: leave that God and come worship this god.

They sent letters “that they should follow the strange laws of the land”, profane the sabbaths and festival days, sacrifice swine's flesh, leave their children uncircumcised, “To the end they might forget the law, and change all the ordinances. And whosoever would not do according to the commandment of the king, he said, he should die.” You think they cannot make a Sunday law and say, that Sabbath thing, no, worship God on the day we say?

The same thing we read in the Maccabees is what Rome, Spain and Portugal did to our people in the Inquisition; read Jews and Moors. And you say it can never happen, this is the United States of America? It happened during slavery. The same thing.

precepts.label: Hebrews 10:34
precepts.why:
“For they shall waste and take away their goods, and cast them out of their houses.” They did it in the time of Rome, when the Pharisees did it with Rome's guidance. Paul tells the Hebrews, “For ye had compassion of me in my bonds, and took joyfully the spoiling of your goods, knowing in yourselves that ye have in heaven a better and an enduring substance.”

Ye had compassion of me in my bonds: when Paul was in prison, they supported him. And they took joyfully the spoiling, the robbing, of their goods: their homes and houses, lands and properties. Those Israelites sacrificed their whole livelihood. They knew that supporting Paul would reveal them, and whatever they had would be taken.

Are we prepared for that? Do we really think about it? The cushy side of the room: I'm so comfortable, I got my new house, my new car, my new hair, my new nails. Are you ready for what the scriptures say is going to happen? Are we willing to lose everything, knowing we have in heaven a better and enduring substance? That is another level of faith we have to build ourselves up to in the short, limited time we have.

Even the world is warning that if a crisis comes and the government says get on a bus for your safety, do not get on: prepare your food, water, power and shelter so you do not have to rely on them. We have been telling our people that for years.

precepts.label: Matthew 10:32-33
precepts.why:
“Then shall they be known, who are my chosen; and they shall be tried as the gold in the fire.” That verse is very important, because it goes back to what Christ said: “Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven. But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.”

Christ is talking about tribulation, persecution, Jacob's trouble. So what will the chosen be saying about Christ in that day, will they deny him or confess him? They are going to confess him.

Why does it say “Then shall they be known”? Because right now everybody says they believe in the Lord. Women say it; men say it. But when this starts to happen, you are going to see who is real and who is fake. On that day the ones who confess Christ before their tormentors are the ones known to be his chosen, tried as gold in the fire, and he will confess them before his Father.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 3:1-6
precepts.why:
The chosen are “tried as the gold in the fire”, and Wisdom gives more detail. “But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and there shall no torment touch them.” Christ said we will be afflicted, so what does no torment mean? That is the lake of fire. That torment will not touch us.

“In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die: and their departure is taken for misery, And their going from us to be utter destruction: but they are in peace.” Christ said, fear not them which kill the body; fear him who can kill body and soul. Man cannot touch your soul. They seem to die because the body died, but the real man, the real woman, is not dead. We keep falling for Esau's craftiness: it's all over, we're finished. It is not over. They are in peace; that is sleep, rest.

“For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality. And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded”. Jacob's trouble is just a little chastisement. “for God proved them, and found them worthy for himself.” God is going to prove us. Everybody says they believe; he will say, let that one get caught early and see what they do. He found them worthy because they confessed Christ before their tormentors.

“As gold in the furnace hath he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.” The death of the saints is as a burnt offering to the Lord. Christ gave his life, and he said if you will not take up your cross and follow him, you are not worthy of him.

precepts.label: Matthew 10:38
precepts.why:
Wisdom says the righteous are tried as gold in the furnace and received as a burnt offering. Christ said, “And he that taketh not his cross, and followeth after me, is not worthy of me.”

Christians say that means you cannot pay your bills and you have to carry all your problems on your back. No, that is not what it is talking about. When Christ was carrying the cross, where did it lead him? To death. He is saying the same thing for us.

We have to be willing to sacrifice ourselves. That is what Wisdom of Solomon was just saying: the souls of the righteous who die for the truth are in the hand of God. If you cannot confess the Lord, even unto death, you are not worthy to be his disciple. That is the cross, and that is how the chosen will be known.

precepts.label: Acts 12:1-15
precepts.why:
“Hear, O ye my beloved, saith the Lord: behold, the days of trouble are at hand, but I will deliver you from the same. Be ye not afraid neither doubt”. Why neither doubt? Because doubt comes. My mama just got put to death, my children, my wife; Lord, are you going to save us? Remember John the Baptist when he was imprisoned; that little bit of doubt crept in. Acts shows the situation.

“Now about that time Herod the king stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the church. And he killed James the brother of John with the sword. And because he saw it pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to take Peter also. (Then were the days of unleavened bread.)” James was beheaded; Peter was in prison. The angel brought Peter out, and he went to “the house of Mary the mother of John, whose surname was Mark; where many were gathered together praying.” That was a safe house where Israelites were hiding and praying. When the damsel knew Peter's voice, “they said unto her, Thou art mad”, and “Then said they, It is his angel.”

What did they think had happened to Peter? That he had been put to death. It shows you could not go visit him. There was no visitation, as there are prisons like Guantanamo Bay in Cuba today, with no lawyers and no visitors, and they are building more like it. So do not think, the brothers don't care about me, the sisters didn't come visit me. There will be places nobody can visit you. It is not that we do not care; we cannot get to you. All the saints could do was pray.

And Peter was on the run, a fugitive from the government the rest of his life. The Lord intervened for one and gave him more time, and the other, James, was killed. It is going to get like that, brothers and sisters. That is why we study, pray and apply: knowing ahead of time is supposed to strengthen your resolve, so that you are not afraid, neither doubt.

precepts.label: 1 John 1:8-10
precepts.why:
“for God is your guide, And the guide of them who keep my commandments and precepts, saith the Lord God: let not your sins weigh you down”. Why say, let not your sins weigh you down? Because we do sin, and churches love to try to trap you with it. “If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.”

Christians on the street will say, do you sin, my brother? Yes. But my sin cannot justify you continuing in sin. Verse 9 is the key; verse 9 is the difference between me and you.

When we start cutting them up, they say, you think you're better than us? Do you sin? Tell them yes, and go right here and show them the difference. They are liars, because they teach that you can sin with no consequences. We teach that if we do sin, the black Messiah laid down his life, if we believe on him, so that we can fight to stop sinning. Simple answer; don't let them jam you up.

We do make errors and fall into folly at times. Confess it and keep fighting, and let not your sins weigh you down.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 2:11
precepts.why:
“let not your iniquities lift up themselves.” “Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins”. When you keep entertaining that sin, eventually you will be bound by it. Peter says, “Dearly beloved, I beseech you as strangers and pilgrims, abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul”.

This is a spiritual war, a war for your soul. Take porn. Brothers say, I got it under control; it don't bother me. No, you don't have it under control. Picture a hallway of doors. A lot of you say, I only watch straight porn, like it is a good thing. That is door number one. Then the threesome, then the train. After a while you get desensitized; that does not excite you anymore, so you go to the next door down: chicks with dicks, then bestiality, then scat, then lesbian, then pedophilia. That is where the doors lead.

It is not normal. And you know it is the devil: when the Bishop was a little kid, his father had magazines hidden up in the drop ceiling. How did two little boys know to get a chair and climb up there, when they never saw their father do it? Playboy, Hustler, then VHS, then DVDs, and today easy access in your hand.

That is how iniquity lifts itself up until you are bound with your sins, covered like a field with thorns. Abstain from fleshly lusts; they are at war with your soul.

precepts.label: Romans 6:14-16
precepts.why:
When you keep entertaining a sin, it binds you. Paul says, “For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under the law, but under grace.” We are not under the law of sacrifice, but under grace. “What then? shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace? God forbid.”

“Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?” His servants ye are to whom ye obey. If you wake up thinking about porn, go to work thinking about porn, and go to sleep thinking about porn, that is your god. You are its servant.

Grace is not a license to keep sinning; it is so that sin shall not have dominion over you. Christ laid down his life so we could fight to stop sinning, not so we could be bound in it. And when you are bound, there is no magic scripture that will release you; you have to want to be released.

precepts.label: Hebrews 6:4-8
precepts.why:
“Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins, and covered with their iniquities like as a field is covered over with bushes, and the path thereof covered with thorns, that no man may travel through! It is left undressed, and is cast into the fire to be consumed therewith.” Hebrews says the same thing.

“For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance”. Those who were once enlightened, who came into this truth, and fall away back into their sin or back into false religion: it is impossible to renew them again to repentance.

“For the earth which drinketh in the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them by whom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God: But that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh unto cursing; whose end is to be burned.”

That is the field of 2 Esdras 16:78, covered with thorns, left undressed and cast into the fire. The ground that drinks in the word and brings forth fruit receives blessing; the one bound with its sins and bearing thorns ends in the fire.

precepts.label: Job 32:21-22
precepts.why:
“For I know not to give flattering titles; in so doing my maker would soon take me away.” When you get the flattering title, your maker soon takes you away. What does that mean? You want the flattering title, you get the test, you fail the test. Bam. Thought I was worthy. Nope.

So be mindful of what you ask for. Brothers work underhandedly to become leaders, and it don't work like that; this is the Lord's business, and he is the one giving it out. Brothers that ask for rank, that say give me the 50's test, never make it, and that is how you know Satan is pushing them. When brothers ask for the test, nine times out of ten they fail it, because spiritually you are not ready if you are asking. Nobody asks to be a leader. The Lord raised all these men up. The Bishop didn't ask to be a bishop; he became a bishop. If you are asking for it, you are in the wrong place.

When the student is ready, the teacher will be there. The Lord will place you where you are supposed to be; promotion comes from the Lord, and there is a reason you are in the position you are in. Once you fulfill that office, the Lord will make it happen. Many brothers who wanted position fell down and never made it back, while others who were down came back on fire. The work determines where you are supposed to be. Brothers get jealous when another brother gets position, but if you love the Lord you work for the Lord, not for position. In Maccabees the brother who said let me get me a name ended up put to death.

That is what Judith 8:24 asks of a leader: not a title, but “let us shew an example to our brethren, because their hearts depend upon us”. The higher up you go, the more people you serve. If you don't have the mindset to build up those beneath you and to support and push up the leader above you, forget it; the Lord can't use you.

thread.label: Wisdom of Solomon 4:8-9
thread.text: For honourable age is not that which standeth in length of time, nor that is measured by number of years.

precepts.label: Job 12:20
precepts.why:
We are supposed to learn from the aged. But as Wisdom of Solomon 4 says, honourable age is “not that which standeth in length of time, nor that is measured by number of years”, and Job shows why: “He removeth away the speech of the trusty, and taketh away the understanding of the aged.”

Look how the Lord deals. Just because you think you are wise in your older years, he will take away your understanding, so that no one should trust in what an old fool says. Our people think that because you are up in age you automatically get the respect. It is not about the age. It is about the wisdom the Lord placed in you, and the Lord can remove that from you.

That is why Daniel's wisdom was called upon while he was a young man, and why Paul instructed Timothy not to let anyone despise his youth: he was a younger man who became an elder over the church. Many of the prophets were called young and set over congregations to lead the people, because the aged, who were supposed to have the wisdom, did not. They were judging incorrectly, they were in briberies, and like the elders in the history of Susanna they were engulfed in their lust. So the Lord called younger men to do what the older men were not doing.

So “wisdom is the gray hair unto men, and an unspotted life is old age.” There is a reason the Messiah called you in your old age so the younger men can teach you. If instead of embracing it you say, I'm too old for these young men to tell me what to do, you cannot teach me nothing, you are going to die in your sin, brother. Our leaders in Israel United in Christ have proven themselves through time and through the rigorous scriptures, and have applied them, and that is why we give them the honor they deserve.

thread.label: Wisdom of Solomon 5:15
thread.text: But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with the Lord, and the care of them is with the most High.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 13:31
precepts.why:
“But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with the Lord”. They “receive a glorious kingdom, and a beautiful crown from the Lord’s hand”: the Lord himself is going to place that crown upon you. “With his arm shall he protect them. He shall take to him his jealousy for complete armour, and make the creature his weapon for the revenge of his enemies.” Second Esdras shows when that revenge comes.

“Behold, the days come, when the most High will begin to deliver them that are upon the earth. And he shall come to the astonishment of them that dwell on the earth.” Before it, “one shall undertake to fight against another, one city against another, one place against another, one people against another, and one realm against another.” There will be wars one against another, city against city, the same as was read earlier in the class.

“And the time shall be when these things shall come to pass, and the signs shall happen which I shewed thee before, and then shall my Son be declared”: then Christ shall be declared. He is not coming back as a regular man that anyone can do harm to; he is coming back with his army. An innumerable multitude gathers “willing to come, and to overcome him by fighting. But he shall stand upon the top of the mount Sion.”

“And this my Son shall rebuke the wicked inventions of those nations, which for their wicked life are fallen into the tempest”. precepts.label: Psalms 50:21
precepts.why:
Why is it that when our iniquity had an end, Esau refused to let us go and kept shedding our blood? Solomon speaks of the ancient Egyptians, and this is modern Egypt today: “not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation, and that their malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.” Their malice is bred in them: God made them that way. They will never change as a race of people. That's why it has been a perpetual hatred from Cain to Abel, Jacob to Esau, blacks and whites, playing itself out over and over, while Christianity blinds us from accepting what God is telling us.

Name a century that black people have had pure peace around this white man. Not we-got-the-vote peace: you still get jailed, racially profiled, shot down, and you can't do what white people do when they get pulled over. The record lists it: the transatlantic slave trade and child slavery from 1619 to 1865, racial terror after emancipation, massacres in Memphis, Colfax, Wilmington, Atlanta, East St. Louis, the Red Summer, Arkansas, Tulsa, Rosewood. And that is only what was reported; imagine what was not documented.

As a result of all this enslavement and all these massacres, Esau is thinking a certain way now. He thinks he's getting away with it: “These things hast thou done, and I kept silence.” Oh, wait a minute, we just enslaved the Lord's people and he didn't do anything.

“thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself.” That is what Esau is thinking to this day. That's why they don't hold themselves accountable for anything. They hold themselves not guilty when they slay us, when they kill us, when they put us into slavery, when they don't give us reparations. Esau thinks he is God.

“but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes.” There will be a judgment for these things. So don't think that smiling white man in your face means to do you good.

thread.label: Wisdom of Solomon 14:8
thread.text: But that which is made with hands is cursed, as well it, as he that made it: he, because he made it; and it, because, being corruptible, it was called god.

precepts.label: Romans 9:20
precepts.why:
Wisdom says “that which is made with hands is cursed, as well it, as he that made it: he, because he made it; and it, because, being corruptible, it was called god.” We did not glorify the Lord; we went after vain imaginations, professed ourselves to be wise, made idolatrous images after the image of corruptible man, and then called them god. The thing made and its maker are both cursed.

Now go to Christ, who is also a maker: he made everything seen and unseen, in earth and in heaven. Paul asks, “Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus?” It is a rhetorical question, because everything he made is in its perfect form and perfect order. The hummingbirds still go to the nectar, lions still chase the beasts, mothers still give suck to their young, the whales do not get out of the water to walk on land, and the water does not pass the bounds of the sand unless the Lord sends his angels in the storm. Everything is in perfect order except the twelve tribes of Israel. Keep my commandments that you may live, and we said no.

“Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?” Christ created both. Jacob and Esau came from the same mother and father, the same lump: one a vessel of honour, which we descend from, and the other a vessel of dishonour.

Then: “What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction”. While Esau fulfils his role as God’s sword, the Lord lets him do what he was created for, and what he was created for is destruction. They are here to serve a purpose, and then the Lord is going to destroy them. Wipe your tears: the nations got to go.

So the war of the gods is this: the true Maker whose works stay in order, against the gods men make with hands, which are cursed with the men who made them.

precepts.label: Luke 1:68-75
precepts.why:
Wisdom says “of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.” There can be no salvation without your enemy being destroyed. Luke shows that this is what salvation always meant.

“Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people”. His people: that is possessive, and his people are the Israelites. “And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David; As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began: That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us”. Saved from who? Our enemies.

Who is your enemy, black man, black woman? Some are scared to say it for fear of losing their job. Yes, Satan is your enemy, but he works with his children, and his children are the Caucasian race. Not just the white man: the Arabs and all nations are going to pay for what they did to our people. Teach your kids that these people do not love you; from the mother’s womb we have been fighting with them. We live in a false illusion that everybody is equal and everybody loves everybody. Our enemies enslaved us, destroyed us, scattered us in slavery and took our land, and all nations hate us.

“To perform the mercy promised to our fathers, and to remember his holy covenant; The oath which he sware to our father Abraham”: the mercy promised to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the covenant he made with us. “That he would grant unto us, that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear”. That is Passover right there. Today we are in the hands of our enemies, and Christ is going to return and redeem us from them. And for that to happen, they all got to die, the same way the Lord drowned all the Egyptians in the sea.

“Might serve him without fear”, because in ancient Egypt we were fearful to serve our God. When we asked to go sacrifice, Pharaoh said we had too much idle time and gave us more work. It is the same today when you ask for a day off and are afraid you will be fired. Deliverance means serving him “In holiness and righteousness before him, all the days of our life.”

So salvation is not your enemies getting saved. Imagine Moses coming to deliver Israel and the Israelites fighting to save the Egyptians; that is what is happening today. Passover is the wars of the Lord: the Lord making war on Egypt, destroying them, and saving his people.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 19:22
precepts.why:
Wisdom closes the account of the Lord’s wars on Egypt the way chapter 18 described them: salvation for his people and destruction for their enemies. “For in all things, O Lord, thou didst magnify thy people, and glorify them”. In all things the Lord magnified his people, the twelve tribes of Israel.

“Neither didst thou lightly regard them: but didst assist them in every time and place.” God assisted us in every time and wherever we were. The Lord was always there fighting for us, and even in these last days the Lord will help us.

That is why the class went on to Jehoshaphat: “Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God’s.” Don’t be scared of armies and people. Teach and speak the word of God no matter what they threaten you with, because the Lord is always there fighting with you.

When an army surrounded Elisha, his servant cried, “Alas, my master! how shall we do?” Elisha answered, “Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them.” The Lord opened the young man’s eyes, “and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.” Angels just waiting for the word. The same thing will come in the future: agents will surround houses and come for some of you. You cannot see it spiritually, but the Lord and his angels are with us, and the growth of IUIC and of Israel could only be accomplished because the Lord is with us, assisting his people in every time and place.

precepts.label: Proverbs 8:13
precepts.why:
“A wise man will fear in every thing, and in the day of sinning he will beware of offence.” A wise man or woman, a brother or sister who applies the commandments, fears in everything. Why does he fear? What is the fear of the Lord? “The fear of the Lord is to hate evil: pride, and arrogancy, and the evil way, and the froward mouth, do I hate.”

The fear of the Lord is to despise and loathe evil and everything that comes in the package with it. Pride is evil in the eyesight of the Lord, and a lot of us have a lot of it: you can’t tell me nothing, I’m older than you. Some sisters say, I want an older sister over me, not a younger one; brothers say, I want an older brother over me. That is pride. The Lord sent these people and put them in your life. Where someone over you has no children, leadership will pair you with someone who can help guide you with yours. You can learn from a baby; every day you wake up on this planet, you learn something.

Arrogancy: many of you cannot stand it when somebody corrects you for your own benefit. You get emotional and walk out the door: I know everything, you can’t tell me nothing. Then you are saying God can’t tell you nothing. Why are you here?

The froward mouth is that disrespectful, childlike, churlish mouth. A lot of you sisters are known for it with the new sisters coming in; some brothers are nasty too. New members come through the door and don’t want to come back because you are nasty. You have to soften, remove that man spirit, have a charitable spirit, kill that old man and that old woman. Christ said whoever offends one of his little ones, better a millstone be hanged about his neck. You have a judgment coming for that.

Does the Lord like those attributes? No: “do I hate.” So do a checkup from the neck up. Write it on the mirror: I deal with pride, arrogancy, an evil eye toward my brothers and sisters. Read your four chapters a day, because you will give account for yourself alone. That is the fear the wise man has, and why in the day of sinning he beware of offence.

precepts.label: Revelation 1:3
precepts.why:
Sirach says “I will yet pour out doctrine as prophecy, and leave it to all ages for ever.” With a war between America and Iran unfolding and many prophecies being fulfilled, we look at what the Bible says about prophecy itself.

“Blessed is he that readeth, and they that hear the words of this prophecy, and keep those things which are written therein: for the time is at hand.” Blessed is he that reads and hears, and keeps the things written therein. What is written in the scriptures? The laws of the Most High God.

So the blessing is not only in reading the prophecy but in keeping the law. We are blessed when we read and keep the things written in the law, because the time is at hand, and the doctrine poured out as prophecy was left for all ages, including ours.

precepts.label: 2 Peter 1:19-21
precepts.why:
“I will yet make doctrine to shine as the morning, and will send forth her light afar off.” Peter says, “We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed”. Take heed to do what the scriptures say. The Most High called us into this truth, so we have to take heed.

“as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts”. We are that light shining in a dark place. That is why Christ said, let your light so shine before men. We have to be that example for our people, to win them over into the faith. Whether you are in DC, New Orleans, California or the UK, the Most High chose us, and through our example we have to win our people over.

“Knowing this first, that no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation. For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.” Prophecy is the foretelling of future events in the Bible, and it did not come by the will of man. Holy men of God, holy black men, holy Hispanic men, spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost. That is the light sent forth afar off.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 15:1-5
precepts.why:
“Behold, speak thou in the ears of my people the words of prophecy, which I will put in thy mouth, saith the Lord”. Speak in the ears of my people. That is why in Ezekiel he said not to go to a people of a strange speech: we have to deal with our people.

“And cause them to be written in paper: for they are faithful and true.” Everything written in the Bible is faithful and true.

“Fear not the imaginations against thee, let not the incredulity of them trouble thee, that speak against thee. For all the unfaithful shall die in their unfaithfulness.” Do not fear what the nations are going to do to us for teaching against America and against governments. The Bible says do not fear.

“Behold, saith the Lord, I will bring plagues upon the world; the sword, famine, death, and destruction.” The Most High says he is going to bring judgment upon the world. That is the doctrine Sirach says was poured out as prophecy and left to all ages, and we do not labour for ourselves only: we speak it in the ears of our people.

precepts.label: 2 Chronicles 15:7-8
precepts.why:
When we teach the Bible and bring out the prophecy, in the street or in classes, what are these scriptures supposed to do for our people? The prophet told King Asa: “Be ye strong therefore, and let not your hands be weak: for your work shall be rewarded.” The days we are living in now are not the time for us to be weak.

“And when Asa heard these words, and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage, and put away the abominable idols out of all the land of Judah and Benjamin, and out of the cities which he had taken from mount Ephraim”. When Asa heard the words of the prophecy, he took courage.

That is what prophecy is supposed to do for us: give us the courage to let go of our idols and our secret sins. We are seeing prophecy unravel right before our eyes: Iran and Israel going to war, and now America getting involved. It was a rumor and talk for years, and now we see it unfold. That means more Israelites are repenting, and more of our brothers and our people are waking up. That is the doctrine poured out as prophecy, laboured for all them that seek wisdom.

precepts.label: Sirach 38:17-19
precepts.why:
“Give not over thy mind to heaviness.” Every class is preparing you for what is coming: rent, mortgage, food and gas are going sky-high, ten dollars a gallon, and you will not get a raise. Can you change it? Then why worry about it? “Love thine own soul, and comfort thy heart, remove sorrow far from thee: for sorrow hath killed many.” Stress and worry have killed many, and you are no different.

Sirach shows what heaviness does: “Weep bitterly, and make great moan, and use lamentation, as he is worthy, and that a day or two, lest thou be evil spoken of: and then comfort thyself for thy heaviness.” This is speaking of when somebody passes: mourn, and then comfort yourself.

“For of heaviness cometh death, and the heaviness of the heart breaketh strength.” Heaviness, stress, brings death. And the heaviness of the heart breaks strength: stress makes a man weak. When you are stressed, you don’t want to work out, you don’t want to go to work. Some people eat more; you gain weight, you become fat and sloppy, you lay back, and eventually it is death.

So, brothers, do not let stress wear you down so that you don’t want to do the Most High’s work. Some of you have sat here five or six years in regular clothes. You see the prophecies coming to pass, wars all over the place, World War III a matter of time, and you still sit there. What are you waiting for? What is keeping you back is sin. Examine yourself.

When correction comes, push harder; prove to Messiah you are still in the fight. Don’t hold grudges and keep to yourself, because that is when Satan messes with your head. A merry heart makes a cheerful countenance, but by sorrow of the heart the spirit is broken. The Most High is doing his part. It is time we do ours.

precepts.label: 2 Maccabees 15:9-17
precepts.why:
Sirach says “Let us now praise famous men” and names them as “Leaders of the people”, leaders, not one. Second Maccabees shows what those leaders do. Judas Maccabeus was preparing the men for war, and we are at war too, brothers: against sin and against our physical enemies, the children of Satan, Edom, Esau.

First a leader has to know the condition of the battle. “And so comforting them out of the law and the prophets, and withal putting them in mind of the battles that they won afore, he made them more cheerful.” If the first time you hear there is a war going on is weeks after it started, you are sleep. If you are not comforting yourself, your children, your wife and your husband out of the law and the prophets, you are not ready for the famine the Lord said is coming, when your stomach touches your back and your kids are looking at you.

“And when he had stirred up their minds, he gave them their charge, shewing them therewithal the falsehood of the heathen, and the breach of oaths.” That is why the class keeps showing that Esau is the devil, lying and breaking every treaty and oath. If your daughter secretly wants to be Tinkerbell, or wears the Frozen wig because she thinks Esau is still a princess, she does not see his breach of oaths. As a mother and a father you have to rework her mind and put her in the mindset of our fathers. Keep the body, take the mind: that was the slave master’s method, and the leader’s work is to take back the mind.

“And this was his vision”: leaders are visionaries, and where there is no vision the people perish. Onias was “a virtuous and a good man”; virtue is moral excellence, and our moral compass is God’s commandments that make us shine like gold. He was “reverend in conversation”, eloquent in speech; “gentle in condition”, keeping his composure, not hot-headed; “well spoken also”; and “exercised from a child in all points of virtue.” Nobody wakes up leading people. We are born leaders, but we become that in time. And “holding up his hands prayed for the whole body of the Jews”: leaders serve and sacrifice themselves for the betterment of the people.

Jeremias gave Judas a sword of gold: “Take this holy sword, a gift from God, with the which thou shalt wound the adversaries.” Then “Thus being well comforted by the words of Judas”: not Judas’s own mindset but the words of God, which comfort a people with a spirit of fear on them and stir them up “to valour, and to encourage the hearts of the young men.” They determined “courageously to set upon them, and manfully to try the matter by conflict.” That is the result of a great leader.

That is why the nations destroy the leaders first, because the leaders are in many cases the lifeline of the people. A leader is needed to bring comfort to a people that has been robbed, raped and murdered, and no nation on this planet needs great leaders more than ours.

precepts.label: 1 Maccabees 3:43
precepts.why:
Sirach praises the “Leaders of the people”, plural, and First Maccabees shows how they worked: “They said one to another, Let us restore the decayed fortune of our people, and let us fight for our people and the sanctuary.” They said it one to another. Nobody tried to do it by himself. When the Bishop went to the streets, he had a reader; that is why the scriptures say go two by two. The Bishop has said for years that this work is too big for one man.

We are in that decayed estate now. The mindset of 99% of our people is in a horrible state: our women thinking they can wear tights outside and nothing is wrong, grown men going outside in a crop top with the belly out, our young women on the dance teams. If that does not put you in a different state of mind, you are destroyed. That is the urgency you see in the brothers teaching loud in the streets, and that is why the Bishop and the deacons teach the way they teach.

Restoring the decayed estate of our people is what is happening at IUSC: our women in order, our men in order, our children in order.

“Let us fight for our people”, and for the sanctuary. You will go way further for somebody else than you will for yourself, and sacrifice way more for someone else than for yourself. That is why selfish people only go so far: they are satisfied at some point. A leader’s mind is on the whole people, like the leaders Sirach praises, who left a name behind them.

precepts.label: Daniel 11:39
precepts.why:
Alexander “parted his kingdom among them, while he was yet alive”, and “his servants bare rule every one in his place.” His generals divided it up: Ptolemy took Egypt, Lysimachus took Thrace and Asia Minor, Seleucus took Syria, and Cassander took Macedonia. Alexander had everything united as one; they could not unite, so they divided the kingdom.

Daniel shows the pattern: “Thus shall he do in the most strong holds with a strange god, whom he shall acknowledge and increase with glory”. Back then, in the time of the Greeks, the strange gods were Zeus, Aphrodite and the like. The strange god today is Caesar Borgia.

It goes on, “and he shall cause them to rule over many”: he causes his people to rule over many nations, many countries. He “shall divide the land for gain.” That is what Alexander's generals did.

Many of these scriptures have levels to them. It started with the Greeks, but Esau kept that same energy at the Berlin Conference in the late 1800s. No Africans, no Negroes and no Latinos were in that meeting; it was about white supremacy, and they divided up the entire continent of Africa for gain, and the land of Israel with it. That is what the Balfour Declaration was about: some of these so-called Khazars wanted that land.

precepts.label: Psalms 55:21
precepts.why:
The Greeks and then the Europeans divided the land for gain. David shows how they got in: “The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart: his words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords.”

When the white man comes, his words are smoother than butter. He will talk about Jesus, about love, about honour and respect, and you will fall in love with what he says. But his intent all along was war and to destroy you.

They did not come into Africa talking war. They came with missionaries who talked the love of white Jesus: we love you, dusty Africans. In Africa you have Hamites and Shemites; the Shemites are the Bantus, and the Nilotes are the Hamites, who were their mercenaries. They brought their religions, spoke words of peace, learned our strengths and our weaknesses, and then devastated us with colonialism and slavery. That is how they divided Africa for financial gain, and why Africa is not united today.

Kwame Nkrumah wanted to unite the entire continent with one visa and one financial system backed by gold. The CIA said, we got to get rid of this dude, and he was run out of Ghana to Guinea.

They taught us to read but not to reason. That is why people get confused over Romans 9:13 and John 3:16: they can read, but they cannot reason. Softer than oil, yet drawn swords: behind every smooth word, the intent was war.

precepts.why:
Mattathias would not do what everybody else was doing. He cried, “Whosoever is zealous of the law, and maintaineth the covenant, let him follow me.” Somebody had to stand up, and that is the mark of a true leader. Acts shows what the leaders of the church were doing: “It seemed good unto us, being assembled with one accord, to send chosen men unto you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul, Men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.”

Assembled with one accord: bishops on one accord, deacons on one accord, captains on one accord. And they send chosen men, not just anybody. You could say they send out Bishop Nathanyel and Deacon Isaac, as they sent Barnabas and Paul.

“Men that have hazarded their lives”: a real leader risks his life for Christ. They call Michael Jordan a leader, football coaches leaders of men; Michael Jordan is not risking anything. Wyclef, what are you doing? The men of this camp have been to Haiti, to Africa, to the barrios of Puerto Rico. They are not going to the suburbs; they are going to the hood, all over IUIC, putting their lives on the line for the name of Christ.

And leaders build leaders. That is an attribute of a father: a father wants his son to be better than him. The bishops are building leadership, sending men to countries and corners that could not be touched before, and now others have been raised up to touch them. But if your mindset is job security, sitting in the high seat, and not building brothers to be better than yourself, forget about it: the Lord will remove you.

classes.title: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.label: Hosea 8:4
precepts.why:
Judas heard of the Romans, “that they were mighty and valiant men”, and that “by their policy and patience they had conquered all the place”. With their friends they “kept amity”, but whom they would help to a kingdom, those reigned, and whom they would, they displaced. Hosea shows Israel doing the very thing: “They have set up kings, but not by me: they have made princes, and I knew it not”.

Ephraim, the northern kingdom, did the same with Assyria and with Egypt. We were always trying to go to other countries to get leverage, never realizing that all we had to do was return to God, reunite with the southern kingdom, keep God's commandments the way they were given, and be one people.

Those same tendencies are here to this day. When the United States became a world power it did what Rome did. Rome trained proxy rulers, like Herod, an Edomite set as ruler over us in Israel; America trains proxy militaries and governments through the School of the Americas, renamed the Western Hemisphere Institute for Security Cooperation, and removes the leaders who resist. That is how they made princes: they trained the Jasons, the ungodly wretches who turned against their own people, the dictators of the northern kingdom countries of Latin America.

Then: “of their silver and their gold have they made them idols, that they may be cut off.” They traded their resources and leveraged what they had to put these people in front of them. Whom they would help, they helped; whom they would weaken, they weakened; whom they would remove, they removed. That sums up the School of the Americas, and the 56 interventions in Latin America: the spirit of Cain coming through Esau, from Rome to America.

precepts.label: 1 Maccabees 8:24-29
precepts.why:
Rome was such “that, whom they would help to a kingdom, those reign; and whom again they would, they displace”: this is where America got the idea of the coup, of destabilizing countries. Judas Maccabeus was catching so much hell from the Greeks that he went to Rome for help, and these are the articles Rome gave him.

“If there come first any war upon the Romans or any of their confederates throughout all their dominion, The people of the Jews shall help them, as the time shall be appointed, with all their heart: Neither shall they give any thing unto them that make war upon them, or aid them with victuals, weapons, money, or ships, as it hath seemed good unto the Romans”. No food, no weapons, no money, no ships to the other side. Today that is called a sanction. That is why they cut Cuba off and forbid all countries to help Cuba; that is why America told the Caribbean, get rid of the Cuban doctors or we cut off your food supply, and the Caribbean said, we need you, but you have to go.

“In the same manner also, if war come first upon the nation of the Jews, the Romans shall help them with all their heart”: America will help you with all their heart, as long as you are theirs. “According to these articles did the Romans make a covenant with the people of the Jews.” It is the same today: America makes articles with countries, and this is where they got it from.

So when you hear about rebel forces, ask where the money and weapons come from: America, Britain, France or Israel, always one of these European powers. The new president of Syria was an al-Qaeda rebel commander with a $10 million bounty on his head, cleaned up and given a haircut. Out of a country of millions, two or three hundred disgruntled people are given money and promises to overthrow the government. Whom they would, they displace.

thread.label: 2 Maccabees 7:14
thread.text: So when he was ready to die he said thus, It is good, being put to death by men, to look for hope from God to be raised up again by him: as for thee, thou shalt have no resurrection to life.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 18:7
precepts.why:
The brother about to die said, “It is good, being put to death by men, to look for hope from God to be raised up again by him.” It is good that this mortal body is slain when you look for a resurrection from the Almighty. “As for thee, thou shalt have no resurrection to life”: as for the heathen, the fake Jews, the Iranians, the other nations, there is no resurrection for them. There is a difference between the twelve tribes of Israel and the other nations. The Most High made a covenant with our forefathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

Wisdom of Solomon goes along with it, and this has to be your mindset concerning salvation and gathering with your people: “So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.” The salvation of the righteous and the destruction of those who are against you come together.

So don’t get scared, y’all. Don’t be scared when you see your enemies’ blood being shed. Maybe some blood might splatter on you. Don’t get scared. The Lord has got our back, and we will not fear what man can do to us: you can kill this body, and we look to be raised again.

Until we receive our homeland, we are all we got. We are pilgrims here, with no favorite place, only our favorite people, the faithful brothers and sisters who keep the commandments. So we must keep the unity, show ourselves friendly, exhort each other, and show charity and mercy one to another.
